in writing. − genetic diversity is being lost at an alarming rate, despite its vital importance for human survival. the protection and conservation of genetic diversity is a key element in achieving the millennium development goals. genetic resources are of particular importance for sustainable agriculture and food security. genetic diversity is also one of the most important conditions for the survival of species and the resilience of ecosystems. the loss of genetic diversity, which occurs as part of the process of biodiversity degradation, is therefore a key challenge for humanity. in addition, genetic resources from countries with a high biodiversity contribute significantly to pharmaceutical research and development. however, intellectual property rights have proven to be a major problem in poor countries in terms of access to medicines. intellectual property rights should therefore not prevent their inhabitants from having access to affordable medicines, in particular where those rights relate to genetic resources originating in developing countries.
in writing. − as bio-piracy is not yet legally defined and thus properly repressed, it is very popular in international industrial practice as a highly profitable practice of commercial exploitation of indigenous traditional knowledge and genetic resources without obtaining permission and providing compensation to source countries and their populations. available statistics show that up to three quarters of the world's population use or directly depend on natural traditional medicines. and for the sake of fairness, it should be added that about 50% of synthetic drugs are based on a natural base. moreover, genetic resources are used in various forms in the pharmaceutical industry for research and development, which demonstrates their economic value and their profitability. i would therefore like to stress that intellectual property rights must not prevent patients, especially in developing countries, from accessing medicines. in order to protect biodiversity and intellectual property in relation to genetic resources, i consider it a priority to define the concept of biopiracy clearly and on the basis of comprehensive analyses, so that we can proceed to suppress it. the introduction of mandatory disclosure of the origin of genetic resources during patent proceedings, which would make it possible to verify whether the conditions of informed consent have been met, etc., would also contribute to strengthening protection.

in writing. − the proposal is part of a package to review eu legislation on credit rating agencies. the directive aims to reduce the reliance on external ratings. credit rating agencies provide outlooks and carry out credit risk research and play an important role in financial markets by providing guidance that is well understood by market participants such as undertakings for collective investment in transferable securities (ucits) and alternative investment funds (aifs). however, ucits and aifs should assess the credit rating agencies' opinions and credit risk separately, thereby indicating their agreement or disagreement with the agencies' opinions. a rating is important for markets but should not be considered as the sole indicator of credit risk.

in writing. − technical conservation measures for fisheries resources are among the most important elements of a regionalised approach to fisheries management. the current commission proposal seeks to extend the rules to technical measures for a further transitional period until a regionalised framework for technical measures in line with the common fisheries policy is adopted. in addition to the extension of the current technical measures, the proposed text contains an update of the existing measures based on the stecf advice and the neafc recommendations, as well as measures to reduce discards in the north-east atlantic as agreed with norway and the faroe islands in 2010, which have not yet been transposed into eu legislation. i recognise the need for these measures, which are designed to ensure that fish stocks are fished in a sustainable way and that their ecosystems are preserved. however, these measures must be formulated and designed in the light of the evolving nature of fisheries and scientific advice.

in writing. - the programmes of specific solutions for remoteness and insularity (posei) were introduced in 1991 to support the french overseas departments and extended a year later to the outermost regions of portugal and spain. nine regions currently benefit from this measure: guadeloupe, french guiana, martinique, réunion, saint-barthélemy and saint-martin belonging to france; the azores and madeira belonging to portugal and the canary islands belonging to spain. a tenth region, namely the french department of mayotte, should be added. these programmes are essential for the maintenance and development of agricultural production and the processing sector in the regions. without the existence of the posei programmes, the visibility of the sectors covered would be at risk today, given the economic difficulties faced by these regions, resulting from their geographical location, and the very limited possibilities for diversifying their activities. the commission proposal amends regulation (ec) no 247/2006 on aid to the outermost regions, in particular to take account of the various legislative revisions that have taken place in recent years. the proposal aims in particular to adapt the regulation to the new provisions on delegated and implementing acts provided for by the treaty of lisbon.
in writing. − the programmes of specific solutions to the remoteness and insularity of posei were introduced in 1991 to support the french overseas departments and extended a year later to the outermost regions of portugal and spain. nine regions currently benefit from this measure: guadeloupe, french guiana, martinique, réunion, saint-barthélemy and saint-martin belonging to france; the azores and madeira belonging to portugal and the canary islands belonging to spain. the posei programme is based on two separate components. on the one hand, there is a specific supply regime which is aimed at supplying these areas with fodder for livestock, for the processing industry and for direct consumption. the aid granted under this scheme is limited to a ceiling set for each country in order to avoid any unfair competition with production on the islands. on the other hand, the second component of posei, which is the most consistent and draws on around 80% of the total amount of aid, concerns measures to support local agricultural production, which is crucial for the maintenance and viability of these activities.

in writing. − with the accession of bulgaria and romania, the european union has enlarged its customs union. as a result, the eu was obliged under wto rules to enter into negotiations with wto members, who are entitled to negotiate within the framework of the commitments schedules of the acceding members, with a view to agreeing on a mutually acceptable compensatory arrangement to offset the increase in duties and the resulting significant losses. in order to meet wto requirements, these agreements address two issues. the first is the compensation of higher duties, which is most often achieved by introducing tariff quotas against specific countries or by increasing existing quotas. secondly, the fact that the pre-accession tariff quota of bulgaria and romania applied to all is also to be added to the existing eu tariff quota applied to all. on 29 january 2007, the council authorised the commission to open negotiations with the countries eligible for compensation. for example, in the eu-us compensation agreement, this applies in particular to poultry and pork meat as well as food preparations. i agree with the rapporteur, mr moreir, that the commission was right to choose tariff rate quotas as a compensation instrument for the american products concerned, as tariff rate quotas are the most targeted way of compensating for losses.

in writing. − technical conservation measures for fisheries resources are among the most important elements of a regionalised approach to fisheries management and are at the forefront of decisions on fishing opportunities. they set out rules for fishing zones and the fishing gear used as opposed to the quantities allowed (fishing effort) or the catches (tac and quotas). technical protection measures are the rules that fishermen throughout the european union must follow on a daily basis when they go on a fishing expedition to ensure that the way and place of fishing is carried out in a sustainable manner. the measures relate to minimum landings, minimum mesh sizes, zones and closed seasons, by-catch limits, criteria for the use of more selective fishing gear and measures to protect the marine environment and therefore have a significant impact on the achievement of the objectives of the common fisheries policy. i consider that in order to ensure the continuity of the proper protection and management of marine biological resources, it is necessary to update the regulation in question accordingly and also to make efforts to reach a political agreement on the issue.

in writing. − on 31 july 2012, the commission presented a proposal for a rapid reaction mechanism to enable member states to respond more quickly and efficiently to vat fraud. a member state facing widespread vat fraud could introduce certain exceptional measures under the rapid reaction mechanism in a way that is not possible under current vat legislation. under the conditions currently in place, if a member state wishes to combat vat fraud by means of measures not provided for in eu vat legislation, it must formally request a derogation. the commission shall then draw up a proposal to that end and submit it to the council for unanimous adoption before the measures concerned can be implemented. however, i believe that this process can be lengthy and cumbersome and that the member state concerned may be reluctant to take the necessary measures to stop the fraud. however, with a rapid reaction mechanism, member states would no longer have to wait for the completion of this formal process before applying concrete anti-fraud measures. the rapid response mechanism was envisaged in the new vat strategy and the anti-fraud and tax evasion communication as a means of strengthening the fight against tax fraud in the eu and protecting public revenues.
in writing. − if a member state currently wants to fight vat fraud, it must formally request a derogation from eu vat legislation. the commission then draws up a proposal, which must be approved unanimously by the council. this process can be lengthy and cumbersome and the member state concerned may be reluctant to take the necessary measures to stop the fraud. a rapid reaction mechanism would allow member states to respond more quickly and efficiently to vat fraud. member states could apply this mechanism within a month. it transfers the obligation to pay vat from the supplier of goods or services to the recipient. however, tax authorities should also take into account the administrative burden on taxpayers. the rapid reaction mechanism shall only be applied in serious cases of fraud. i therefore expect a long-term anti-fraud strategy to be developed, as the complexity of vat legislation across the eu is an opportunity for fraudsters. at the same time, the member states must retain the competence to determine their own vat rate.

in writing. − if you have the commission proposal aims to establish a european platform for online dispute resolution (the 'osr platform'). it will be an interactive website offering consumers and traders a single point of access to out-of-court settlement of certain disputes contractual disputes arising from the cross-border online sale of goods or the provision of services by a trader established in one member state to a consumer established in another member state. the platform will be free of charge and available in all official eu languages. the proposed directive aims to improve redress possibilities for consumers by ensuring that all consumer complaints can be submitted to an adr entity (e.g. an arbitrator, conciliator, ombudsman or complaints board) for out-of-court resolution. the platform will enable the parties and the adr entity to implement the online dispute resolution procedure. the network of dsos will be established to support the resolution of disputes referred by the dsb platform.
in writing. − the commission's proposal for alternative dispute resolution (adr) for consumer disputes aims to provide a simple, efficient and low-cost means of dispute resolution involving the sale of goods or the provision of services throughout the european union. once implemented, this directive will enable all eu-based consumers to have access to a quality adr entity if they have problems with the purchase of goods or the provision of services whether at home or abroad from a trader established in an eu member state. although consumer protection has improved since the single market was established, 'gaps' still remain that make life difficult for european citizens. the proposed directive aims essentially to remove the three most serious obstacles to consumers and traders' access to a well-functioning adr entity. in the first case, we are talking about the fact that the coverage of the ars is still not uniform either at sectoral or geographical level. second, many consumers are simply not aware of or sufficiently informed about the benefits of using adr mechanisms. finally, if ars systems exist, their quality varies greatly and often does not meet the quality principles set out in the commission's recommendations. the aim is to ensure that consumers have access to high-quality and transparent adr procedures wherever they make their purchases in the union.

in writing. − on 3 november 1998, the council adopted directive 98/83/ec on the quality of water intended for human consumption. this new directive had to be transposed into national law by the end of 2000 and complied with by the end of 2003. contamination of drinking water with radioactive substances may occur through accidental releases of radioactivity or through the use of inappropriate disposal procedures. water systems that are at risk of such contamination shall be subject to extensive monitoring of radioactive contamination to ensure that drinking water is safe. there are many regions in europe with such geological and hydrological characteristics that they have to be considered with the worrying possibility of natural occurrence of radioactive substances. therefore, on 27 june 2011, the commission adopted a proposal laying down requirements for the protection of public health with regard to radioactive substances in water intended for human consumption on the basis of article 31 of the euratom treaty. i believe that each member state should set up monitoring programmes to check that water intended for human consumption meets the requirements of this directive. at the same time, the methods used to analyse the quality of water intended for human consumption should be such as to ensure the reliability and comparability of its results.

in writing. − as investors increasingly seek to achieve social objectives and not just financial returns, a social investment market is emerging in the union, partly constituted by investment funds targeting social enterprises. such investment funds shall provide funding to social enterprises that act as drivers of social change by offering innovative solutions to social problems, helping to address the social consequences of the financial crisis and contributing in a valuable way to the achievement of the europe 2020 objectives. it is necessary to establish a common framework of rules concerning the use of the designation 'european social entrepreneurship fund' by means of uniform rules in the union. in the absence of such a common framework, there is a risk that member states would adopt different measures at national level, which would have a direct negative impact on the proper functioning of the internal market and would create obstacles to the proper functioning of that market, as funds wishing to operate across the union would be subject to different rules in different member states. i consider it justified to adopt a regulation laying down uniform rules applicable to european social entrepreneurship funds and imposing corresponding obligations on their managers in all member states who wish to raise capital across the union using the designation 'european social entrepreneurship fund'. those requirements should ensure the confidence of investors wishing to invest in such funds.

in writing. − in 2008, at the onset of the economic crisis, the direct impact on men's work was stronger than on women's work. women were not the first victims of the crisis, but the situation has gradually worsened since 2009. women in the eu have been hit by a silent crisis. its effects were slower and less pronounced than in men. but they cannot be ignored. women in the public sector, where they represent on average 70% of the workforce, are the main victims of budgetary cuts decided by member state governments. the reduction in the number of public sector employees reached 25% in some member states. moreover, salaries in the public sector have been reduced or frozen and it is common practice that fixed-term contracts are not renewed. for women who have stayed in employment, the job is often at a lower level of qualification than they have achieved, and they keep the job at the risk of losing their qualifications. job prospects for the coming years show that 15% of low-skilled jobs will disappear, while 15% of new jobs will require high-skilled skills. i think it is very important to consider all training policies, taking into account the special position of women.
in writing. − as a result of the crisis, the position of women, their working conditions, have become much more precarious. budget cuts also have a significant impact on women. their professional advancement is precarious, and in many cases they have no formal employment contract or work part-time. as a result, they have less income, which also leads to lower pensions. with reduced social benefits, health care and sickness benefits, and reduced child care budgets, women are often forced to give up their jobs to provide for dependent family members. in other cases, they undertake additional tasks to ensure that costs are covered. single parents, most of whom are women, are at risk of poverty as a result of reductions in family allowances. i agree that negotiations with the social partners should be conducted to achieve a better balance between family and professional life and to contribute to the retention of women in the workforce by improving childcare facilities. families with women in employment have higher family incomes, and therefore higher consumption, which leads to economic growth. member states should strongly encourage women's entrepreneurship and job creation in the social and solidarity-based sectors of the economy. i believe that the report adopted can improve the situation of economically disadvantaged groups, including women, and that is why i supported it.

in writing. − gender equality is a fundamental human right. pursuant to article 8 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union, the union shall aim, in all its activities, at eliminating inequalities and at promoting equality between men and women. stereotyped perceptions of women in the labour market lead to occupational segregation and gender pay gaps. the gender pay gap of 16.4% in 2010 shows the seriousness of this problem. in addition, women are often underrepresented or ignored in the media or portrayed in roles traditionally considered female, which encourages the reinforcement of gender discrimination in different areas of society and across all age groups. the prevalence of negative gender stereotypes based on societal beliefs and attitudes affects women and limits their opportunities and options in the social, economic and political spheres. in order to address the lack of women in senior positions in economic and political decision-making, the persistence of gender stereotypes in all layers of society needs to be addressed. the report therefore aims to reduce the prevalence of negative gender stereotypes in the eu, which limit the opportunities and possibilities of men, and even more so of women. the elimination of gender stereotypes in education, media and advertising, the labour market and economic and political decision-making requires new eu policies and legislation.
in writing. − much eu legislation takes the form of directives, which set out general rules and objectives. however, the choice of means to achieve them is left to the member states and the regional and local authorities. the lack of a satisfactory level of implementation of eu environmental law is reflected in the high number of environmental infringements and complaints. there are significant differences in the implementation of legislation between member states as well as within member states, which lead to negative environmental impacts and thus to the need for a more systematic and holistic approach, which is essential to overcome these 'implementation gaps'. as recently as 2011, the environment was the area with the highest number of reported breaches of union law in the eu (299), accounting for 17% of all breaches, and 114 new infringement procedures were initiated in the same year. full compliance with eu environmental legislation is a treaty obligation and a criterion for the use of eu funds in the member states. i believe that member states should therefore implement environmental legislation in a timely and cost-effective manner in order to improve the state of the environment in the eu as a whole.

in writing. − the legal basis for the european development fund (edf) is the council's internal agreement. the partnership agreement between the african, caribbean and pacific states (acp states), of the one part, and the european community and its member states, of the other part, signed in cotonou on 23 june 2000 (the cotonou agreement), has laid the formal foundations for eu cooperation with the acp states. the legal basis for the association agreements between the union and the overseas countries and territories (octs) is part iv of the treaty on the functioning of the european union and the overseas association decision of 27 november 2001, by virtue of which certain overseas countries and territories are associated with the european union. the commission adopted a draft decision on the association of the overseas countries and territories on 16 july 2012 and it is currently being discussed in the council. the commission emphasises the reduction and ultimate eradication of poverty, which is the main objective of the european union's development cooperation. special attention must also be paid to the special protection of women and girls, and the union must also make a firm commitment under the 11th edf to improve the lives of marginalised groups (children, human rights activists, persons with disabilities and, more generally, any person or group who suffers discrimination on the grounds of their religion, political convictions or sexual orientation).
in writing. − the 11th edf report covers the period 2014-2020 for the financing of eu cooperation with african, caribbean and pacific countries and overseas countries and territories. the primary objective of union development cooperation shall remain the reduction and, subsequently, the eradication of poverty, as well as the objectives relating to the basic social sectors and to equality of opportunity between men and women. the european parliament proposes that 20% of the 11th edf be spent on basic social services, in particular health and primary education. in the draft internal agreement, the commission proposes a maximum budget of eur 30 319 000 000 for the 11th edf (2014 to 2020), representing an increase of around 13% in the volume of assistance made available to the acp states and the octs compared to the 10th edf. i believe that the new multiannual financial framework for financing eu cooperation with african, caribbean and pacific countries and overseas countries and territories will contribute to the development of the regions concerned and can improve the social and health and education networks. all of this is essential for future ascension, which is why i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. − the european development fund is a key instrument for development aid. but in times of crisis, there is a need to talk more about how european aid is used. i therefore support many of the proposals in the report. but i also want to point out that in the field of development aid, targeted aid from the member states is often more effective than eu bombastic programmes. women in poor countries need doctors and medicine, but in the name of "reproductive rights", they get abortion clinics from us. this is why the european parliament must start respecting the declaration of the 21st acp-eu parliamentary assembly, which says: 'the eu should refrain from attempts to impose its values which are not universally accepted in the eu-acp partnership'.
in writing. − the draft budget of the european union for the next 7 years, as presented by the government of the slovak republic, is favourable to slovakia. it will bring us 10% more funding than this fiscal period. the resulting up to 25% flexibility in the common agricultural policy will increase direct payments to slovak farmers and help increase the volume of slovak food products on our market. slovakia also spent more than eur 225 million to phase out two blocks of the je bohunice. on the other hand, the budget does not cover the financial commitments that the eu has made. there's a threat of structural deficits and deformities with consequences. we need to be able to revise the seven-year budget after two or three years. we need more flexibility between categories and between years to move funds to where they are best used for growth and jobs. we want to work with the council to eliminate these and other risks. the only option for further negotiations was to support the european parliament's resolution on the multiannual financial framework. as a message to slovakia, i can say that the favorable terms that the government has negotiated are not threatened in further negotiations.

in writing. − the regulation lays down the rules to be followed in the compilation and publication of basic macroeconomic data in the eu. the commission proposal is in fact a major revision of the european system of national and regional accounts (the european system of accounts esa), which builds on the latest revision of the united nations system of national accounts (sna adopted in 2008) and addresses the issue in more detail. statistics are central and one of the essential topics of public debate: independent, reliable, comparable and up-to-date data are essential for policy-makers as well as for economic operators and citizens to measure, assess and monitor economic reality and developments. every effort should be made to ensure that the revised esa provides eu citizens with macroeconomic statistics of the highest quality, based on a sound methodology and following a precise timetable. the union member states have raised concerns in particular about the administrative burden and this report therefore proposes that, where possible, automated methods of real-time data collection should be used.
in writing. − the regulation on the system of national and regional accounts sets out the rules to be followed when compiling and publishing eu basic macroeconomic data. independent, reliable, comparable and up-to-date data are essential for policy-makers as well as for economic operators and citizens to measure, assess and monitor economic reality and developments. the commission proposal is in fact a major revision of the european system of national and regional accounts, which is based on the latest revision of the united nations system of national accounts. given that member states point to concerns about high administrative burdens, the report suggests that, where possible, automated methods of real-time data collection should be used. i voted for the report.
in writing. − the flag state control aspects of the maritime labour convention (mlc) 2006 should be embedded in eu legislation in a more detailed and concrete way. the main advantage of incorporating the maritime labour convention into european union law is that it provides for a much stricter enforcement regime in the eu, for example through eu infringement procedures, which would further strengthen compliance. the eu provisions on flag state control should reflect much more the specific and explicit requirements contained in the convention on maritime labour standards in order to avoid divergent interpretations by member states which could lead to unfair competition and social dumping. i consider it justified and important that, within the scope of eu competence, the convention on maritime labour standards be transposed as faithfully as possible into the proposed directive.

in writing. − when the next term begins in 2014, the current derogation from article 14 (2) of the treaty on european union (teu) will end and the european parliament will consist of 751 members (750 plus the president). the current number of seats is 754 736 for members elected in accordance with the treaty of nice, which was in force at the time of the 2009 elections, plus 18 members appointed under the treaty of lisbon by amending article 2 of protocol no 36 on transitional provisions, which provided for a temporary derogation from article 14 (2) teu (providing that no member state may be allocated more than 96 seats) in order to allow the 99 seats allocated to germany under the treaty of nice to be maintained until 2014. the decision establishing the composition of the new parliament may also require a wider distribution of seats to take account of possible changes in the population of the member states or to improve the interpretation and application of the principle of proportionality by descent laid down by the treaty. under article 14 (2) teu, the new composition of parliament is to be determined by the european council acting unanimously on a proposal from the european parliament and with its consent. parliament is thus responsible for submitting a proposal to the european council.
in writing. − liqueurs are classified within the categories according to the definitions set out in annex ii to regulation (ec) no 110/2008. according to recital 2 of regulation (ec) no 110/2008, the measures applicable to the spirit drinks sector should protect the reputation that spirit drinks have acquired on the european union and world markets by continuing to take into account the traditional processes used in the production of spirit drinks. absinthe, a spirit drink traditionally produced in several member states, has not been defined as a product category in annex ii to that regulation. depending on the regional occurrence of certain herbs and changing consumer preferences, traditional absinthe production practices have begun to differ to some extent in many member states, so that not all traditional recipes set a minimum anethole content and the anethole content for many products currently available on the market remains below the level of 0,5 g/l as proposed by the commission. following the entry into force of the draft regulation drawn up by the commission, producers of these variants of absinthe would be obliged, in view of this newly introduced definition of absinthe, to stop using the designation 'absint' as a sales denomination or to change their long-standing recipes, even in spite of their traditional production methods. i believe that such a change in the essential characteristics of the product may provoke a negative reaction from consumers and thus undermine their confidence.
in writing. − the communication from the commission to the european parliament, the council, the european economic and social committee and the committee of the regions entitled 'the cap to 2020: meeting the food, natural resources and territorial challenges of the future' sets out the possible tasks, objectives and objectives of the common agricultural policy (cap) after 2013. the discussions on this communication have shown that the cap should be reformed with effect from 1 january 2014. it is essential to have a strong cap supported by the budget needed to generate real growth in the period 2007 to 2013 to enable the european union to produce the necessary quantity of a variety of high-quality foodstuffs at a constant rate, and to help promote employment, preserve and produce environmental goods, combat climate change and manage land. in addition, the cap should be based on provisions which are easily understandable to farmers, other stakeholders and citizens in general, in order to ensure transparency of implementation. one of the main objectives and key requirements of the cap reform is to reduce the administrative burden. this objective should be duly taken into account when drawing up the relevant provisions of the direct support scheme. the number of support schemes should not exceed the necessary range and farmers and member states should be able to comply with the relevant requirements and obligations without excessive red tape.
in writing. − if we are to talk about a new common agricultural policy, we need to set clear priorities. i consider food safety and environmental protection to be the main ones. in future, only active farmers should be beneficiaries of direct agricultural payments. whereas land owners who use their land for various activities that are miles away from agriculture should lose their right to direct payments. the distribution of direct payments to farmers from different member states must in any case be fair. there is a need to improve transparency in the disclosure of beneficiaries of agricultural subsidies in a way that does not prejudice farmers' right to privacy. if we are to bring fresh blood into the aging agricultural sector, young farmers must be eligible for higher subsidies. however, it is true that direct payments for large farms should be gradually reduced. it is important that the eu's common agricultural policy is increasingly green, with 30% of the total funding being conditional on complying with binding environmental measures. the definition of green measures should depend on the size of the farm and the extent to which other environmental measures are applied. i am very pleased that for the first time in the history of the eu, the european parliament and the council are deciding together on the final form of the new eu agricultural policy. i believe that, by working together, we have secured a fairer distribution of payments across member states, which will help support agriculture in the eu member states in the next seven-year budget period.
in writing. − communication from the commission to the european parliament, the council, the european economic and social committee and the committee of the regions entitled 'the cap to 2020: meeting the food, natural resources and territorial challenges of the future' identifies the potential challenges, objectives and orientations of the common agricultural policy (cap) after 2013. on the basis of the discussion on that communication, the cap should be reformed with effect from 1 january 2014. that reform should cover all the main instruments of the cap, including council regulation (ec) no 1234/2007 establishing a common organisation of agricultural markets and on specific provisions for certain agricultural products (single cmo regulation). given the scope of this reform, it is appropriate to repeal regulation (ec) no 1234/2007 and replace it by a new regulation on the single common organisation of the markets. the reform should also, as far as possible, harmonise, streamline and simplify the provisions, in particular those covering more than one agricultural sector, including by ensuring that non-essential elements of the measures can be adopted by the commission by means of delegated acts. moreover, the reform should continue along the same lines as previous reforms to achieve greater competitiveness and market orientation.

in writing. − reducing red tape is one of the key objectives and main requirements of the reform of the common agricultural policy (cap). realistic tolerances and limits for de minimis aid should be established and an appropriate balance between trust and control should be established to ensure that the future administrative burden on member states and beneficiaries is kept at a reasonable level. in the context of the elimination of red tape, due account should be taken of the administrative and other costs of control at all levels and the use of efficient administrative and monitoring systems should be rewarded. the primary objective should be to reduce administrative costs to a reasonable level and to ensure that the administrative burden on farmers and administrative staff is brought back to a reasonable level. in order to increase the awareness of beneficiaries of the relationship between agricultural practices, farm management and risk management on the one hand and standards relating to the environment, climate change, good agricultural condition, food safety, public health, animal health, plant health and animal welfare on the other hand, it is necessary that member states set up a comprehensive farm advisory system to offer advice to beneficiaries. at the same time, i believe that member states should also ensure a clear distinction between advice and controls.

in writing. − the endocrine system regulates a large part of the processes in the human body, including reproduction, metabolism, growth, the balance between salts and water, and the function of the heart. the incidence of disorders is increasing, particularly in relation to human reproductive capacity, with endocrine disrupting substances considered as one of the contributing factors. a number of disturbing trends may be observed. over the past two decades, evidence has mounted that the human body is becoming increasingly endocrine-disrupting. worldwide, the incidence and diagnosis of a wide range of disorders have increased dramatically. we are seeing an increase in birth defects, cases of cancer and diabetes, and an increase in neurodevelopmental disorders such as autism and adhd. such rapid changes can only be explained by the action of external environmental factors. this environmental impact comes from a number of different sources, including lifestyle, dietary, pathogenic, medical, pharmaceutical and economic factors, as well as social causes such as stress. there are also a number of studies that show that exposure to chemicals also plays a role. all these factors may be related. the protection of human health is an important part of eu policy (article 35 of the treaty). to this end, it is necessary to apply the precautionary principle (article 191 of the treaty) in full.

in writing. − all types of asbestos are dangerous and its harmful effects are documented and regulated. most of the adverse health effects of inhaled asbestos do not appear until decades after exposure. it is known that threshold exposure levels below which exposure to chrysotile asbestos would not pose a carcinogenic risk have not yet been established and that an effective way to protect human health is to prohibit the use of chrysotile asbestos fibres and products containing them. an increased risk of cancer has been observed in people exposed to very low levels of asbestos fibres. the creation of landfills with asbestos waste is a temporary solution to a problem that is thus passed on to future generations, as asbestos fibres are practically indestructible over time. however, in addition to the human dimension of inadequate health and safety protection at the workplace, this problem also has harmful effects on the economy. health and safety problems at the workplace are a barrier to growth and competitiveness, while also causing a disproportionate increase in social security costs. i think it is important that the eu, together with international organisations, should promote instruments which would classify the asbestos market as a trade in toxic substances. at the same time, it is important that all victims of asbestos in the eu and their relatives receive prompt and appropriate medical treatment and adequate financial support from the national health insurance system.
in writing. − while none of us doubts that asbestos is harmful, it must be borne in mind that it is a highly harmful material that must be handled with extreme care. not only can cancer be caused by inhaling asbestos fibers but other serious health problems can also result. the main victims are those who have worked with materials containing asbestos, but also people who have been in the vicinity of such work. article 168 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union provides that the union is to ensure a high level of protection of human health. in this spirit, it is our duty to establish rules to provide adequate health care to all who suffer from the effects of asbestos fibre inhalation. illnesses resulting from the performance of work duties must be labelled as occupational diseases in all member states in order to provide patients with appropriate treatment. i appreciate the young people's desire for revenge. they need to be able to anticipate the hazards of materials used in older buildings and have sufficient knowledge of the possible consequences of exposure to asbestos for later generations. for this reason, we must also ensure that landfills are strictly labelled.
in writing. − the harmfulness of asbestos to humans and the environment is now well known. few people know, however, how dangerous asbestos really is. it has been shown that inhaled asbestos can cause pulmonary fibrosis asbestosis, lung cancer, thoracic and peritoneal mesothelioma and thoracic changes. although the european commission decided in 1999 to ban the use of all types of asbestos, it is essential that measures be taken to minimise the impact on both the individual and the environment as a whole in order to phase out asbestos. i voted in favour of the present report because i believe that legislation alone is not enough and that more needs to be done to implement it in practice. i expect the eu to adopt more effective measures in relation to the member states, which will create better conditions for the progressive removal and disposal of asbestos materials. the system of controls on the removal and disposal of asbestos shall be improved. education, skills and competences of people, development of asbestos eradication programmes, safety procedures and protection of workers need to be improved.
in writing. − in march 2006, the commission withdrew its proposal for a regulation on the statute for a european mutual fund. in recent years, the european parliament has adopted a number of resolutions calling for the adoption of a regulation on the statute for a european mutual society, but it is regrettable that, after withdrawing the draft statute for a european mutual society in 2006, the commission has not produced any new proposal providing mutual societies with an appropriate legal instrument to facilitate their cross-border activities. fortunately, it recognised the need for a statute and committed itself to developing better legislation for social economy organisations (including mutual societies), stressing that mutual societies should be able to operate across borders and thus contribute to european efforts to 'increase growth and strengthen trust' in the european economic area. it is important to hope that this european statute will be ambitious and innovative in protecting workers and their families in the event of mobility within the countries of the union.

in writing. as i warned a year ago, the so-called arab spring in egypt has brought neither freedom nor democracy. it has been confirmed that the enthusiastic comparison of the velvet revolution in the former czechoslovakia with the tahrir square protests in egypt was just a misunderstanding of the situation by some media and politicians. sadly, the main victims of this error are the christians, who are among the indigenous inhabitants of the region. the rise of political islam makes them second- or third-class citizens, constantly at risk of being accused of insulting islam, which in many cases ends in violence or the death of the accused. eu diplomacy has so far failed to provide effective assistance and protection not only to these people but also to its own citizens, as evidenced by the case of the kidnapped slovak boy adamek azaz. the resolution also calls on the commission and the european union's chief diplomat to take more effective action, in particular by making development aid conditional on concrete political reforms.
in writing. − tensions on the korean peninsula have been rising since the dprk launched a 'satellite' using ballistic missile technology in december 2012 and conducted a nuclear test in february of that year in protest against the international community's unification. both the council of the european union and the un security council have strongly condemned these acts as a serious breach of the dprk's international obligations under a un security council resolution and as a serious threat to the maintenance of regional and international peace and security. it is important to seek a political solution to the nuclear issue through diplomatic means. the dprk should endeavour to re-engage in the talks and make efforts to achieve lasting peace and security on the korean peninsula, thereby ensuring, as far as possible, a prosperous and stable future for the country.
in writing. − china's interest in growing and acquiring a position in the world commensurate with its political and economic strength is a fundamental principle of its policy. given china's size and remarkable growth, these changes have a tremendous impact on world politics and trade. the eu offers the largest market in the world. it plays a central role in finding sustainable solutions to current environmental, energy and globalisation challenges. it has shown its ability to gradually extend its influence beyond its borders, becoming the largest provider of development aid in the world. in order to confirm the importance of their relationship, the eu and china agreed in 2003 on a strategic partnership. some differences persist, but they are effectively resolved and relations become more solid and realistic. china is also heavily involved, alongside the eu, in the process of globalisation and increasingly in the international system. the aim should be to create a situation in which china and the eu can leverage their strengths to offer joint solutions to global challenges.
in writing. − the rhetoric coming from beijing in recent years clearly shows that china is genuinely concerned about the unfavourable economic developments in europe, most notably the debt crisis. the chinese economy is mainly export oriented and the european union is the largest trading power and the main destination of chinese exports. china is the eu's second largest trading partner, after the united states. it follows logically that china needs the economic growth of its trading partners in order to support its own economic development. european companies, unfortunately, still cannot invest in china on the same terms as chinese investments in europe. despite chinese progress in reducing trade barriers preventing access to the chinese market, many barriers remain, as evidenced by the report of the eu chamber of commerce in china. the report shows that as many as 43% of ceos of european companies in china believe that the measures taken by the chinese government are discriminatory against them. europe and china need each other. in this spirit, a new phase in eu-china trade relations must be launched, based on a partnership of equals, mutual benefit and common development. this is the principle of reciprocity that europeans have long called for.
in writing. − since the signing of the eu-china agreement in 1985, cooperation has developed into a strategic partnership of great importance to the relationship. i welcome the public commitment made during the strategic dialogue last year to set a good example of cooperation through a strategic partnership based on shared interests and mutual understanding. the promotion of 60 sectoral dialogues is a good example of international cooperation. if a high-level partnership is to be mutually beneficial, we need to define better the strengthening of dialogues in the concept of a strategic partnership in the future. the commission will also be supporting the development of the european union's external relations policy, in particular the fight against counterfeiting and the fight against fraud.
in writing. − a joint europol investigation team, codenamed 'operation veto', has uncovered widespread manipulation of sports results in recent years, with 680 matches suspected worldwide, including 380 in europe. the team described a far-reaching network affecting sports results that has hit the very heart of the sport, and in which 425 people are suspected of involvement and 50 others have been arrested. however, these figures are only the 'tip of the iceberg' as the sports sector is estimated to generate total revenues of several billion euros per year. the influence on sporting outcomes affects many member states, which is a matter of serious concern as it is linked to organised crime and poses a significant threat to organised sport in virtually all member states. moreover, corruption in sport can also spread to the competent authorities, which ultimately threatens people's confidence in the effectiveness of democratic institutions in protecting the democratic state. it is necessary for the commission to develop a coordinated approach in the fight against match-fixing and organised crime by coordinating the efforts of the main stakeholders in this area and providing a platform for discussion. i consider it equally important in this context that sports organisations themselves adopt a zero tolerance policy towards corruption at both internal and external levels, thus preventing their members from being vulnerable to external pressure.
in writing. − the european parliament will soon have to give its consent to the european union's accession to the international cotton advisory committee (icac). the icac is an international organisation of cotton producing, exporting and importing countries. although the union's accession to the icac is not a problem per se, inta decided to draw up a resolution on several aspects of the global cotton value chain. i believe that in this context it is essential to address in particular the issue of forced and child labour in cotton production. the european union has several trade instruments at its disposal to be used in the fight against forced and child labour. these include, for example, the scheme of generalised tariff preferences. it is equally justified for the commission to propose an effective mechanism mapping goods produced through forced and child labour.
for the efd group. one of the most explosive cities in pre-islamic iraq became the city of kirkuk, home to millions of people. nearby, rich oil fields have given it the nickname little iraq. its territory is hotly contested by up to three local ethnic groups. under saddam hussein, tens of thousands of kurds were expelled from the city and their homes were occupied by arabs. after the overthrow of the hussein regime, the kurds began to return to their homes and began to drive out the arabs as well as the local turkmen from the city. kurds are coming to town who have never lived here. the kurdish autonomous administration apparently decided to appropriate this territory, perhaps because of the mineral wealth found there. violence, terror, political assassination - these are local methods of asserting political and economic influence. since the region is also fighting for control of its oil resources, we cannot be under the illusion that the local interests of the oil traders are behind the ongoing violence. however, the iraqi administration is clearly unable to prevent conflict between the respective ethnic and religious groups living in the country. and in the kirkuk dispute, it leaves too much room for the kurds to push and persecute the local predominantly turkmen population, but also the arabs. perhaps we should therefore make a strong appeal not only to the iraqi government but also to the kurdish autonomous government to resolve this problem, so that the local population does not become unnecessarily victims of economic, economic and political disputes over wealth in the region.

there is no doubt that the commission's proposal to withdraw 900 million allowances from the european union's emissions trading scheme will be a major intervention in the current carbon market. the consequence of this measure will naturally be an increase in the price of carbon, which on the one hand may put pressure on polluters to innovate their technologies more intensively, but on the other hand will immediately translate into price increases in many industrial products, which ultimately will be paid by our citizens. the question therefore remains whether it is wise to open up such a sensitive subject at a time when our industrial production is declining and important european producers are fleeing to other parts of the world because of the insidious and bureaucratic management of the union's economic policy.
in writing. the eu emissions trading scheme is a key tool for cost-effectively reducing industrial emissions. its creation was a market-based measure to regulate co2 prices, which enables us to incentivise low-emission technologies and investments in renewable energy. despite the fact that emissions have been declining since the ets was set up, the system is still highly unequal in its operation. one reason is the economic crisis, which is still very much in effect today, and which has led to the accumulation of 955 million surplus emissions. it can be said that the supply of allowances is currently far in excess of demand, so that carbon prices have decreased from approximately eur 30/tonne co2 to approximately eur 5/tonne co2. such a significant decrease in quota prices has serious consequences for the adequate incentives for sustainable and technological investments and hampers investments in low-carbon technologies. in order to overcome the current disparities, the legislative provisions on the timing of the auctioning of greenhouse gas emission allowances should be amended as soon as possible. to ensure the stability and predictability of the eu ets, operational intervention is occasionally necessary, as this is in the interest of all eu member states.
the commission's proposal to suspend the application of the european union's emissions trading scheme to intercontinental flights in 2012 is justified by the fact that the european commission wishes to improve the prospects for a successful outcome of the establishment of global market measures in international aviation at the forthcoming general assembly of the international civil aviation organisation in september 2013. i don't want to debate the meaning of our gesture today. i want to point out the technical difficulties that will accompany our generosity. indeed, we will probably have to fine-tune the mechanisms for surrendering the 2012 allowances in such a way that competition is not distorted and that all transactions are conducted in a fair and transparent manner. a global agreement on this matter on the icao's soil would certainly be a great success. but it is also realistic to expect that, despite our efforts, such an agreement will not be reached in the time available.

the internet is the most common medium used by people of all ages. almost all of us have had experience with security problems, to a greater or lesser degree. it is not for nothing that we call programs that can spread without the user's knowledge viruses. they can act as a biological virus that causes infection in the host. inadequate protection of equipment will allow the spread of destructive viruses that can interfere with our work or even our privacy. mass use of the internet therefore requires the adequate provision of security as well as information to ordinary users on how to achieve its highest level. i am of the opinion that it is essential that there should be an authority to carry out this task, we just need to know what powers such an authority has and will have and how its results will be handled. but in times of economic crisis we also need to ensure transparency and eliminate unnecessary costs, and that is why i am of the opinion that this office called enisa should be moved to brussels.
the regulation of the european parliament and of the council on the european network and information security agency establishes the agency as the formal successor of the original agency based in heraklion, crete. with the increasing volume and importance of electronic communications, the importance of network and information security is also growing and it may therefore be appropriate to consider the creation of such an institution with a longer mandate than the proposed five to seven years. the continuous improvisation and debate about the agency's purpose has certainly marked its work in the period so far. the independent evaluation of the agency's activities since 2004 has led to recommendations for a clearer definition of the agency's tasks and objectives and an appropriate budget. the technical and instrumental support of the equipment and programmes for collecting and analysing data from early warning systems must be able to cope with dynamically changing security threats and therefore, i think, we should approach the further mandate of this agency with greater seriousness and attention.
international trade is one of the most effective means of tackling poverty and boosting economic growth in countries struggling with poverty. to neglect its obligations towards the less fortunate parts of the world would be to betray the fundamental values on which it is founded. one of the most direct ways to help is through trade. but like anything, trade-led development has its pitfalls. the reasoning report identifies two of the most pressing problems, namely corruption and the behaviour of international companies outside the european union. the european union cannot support corrupt regimes and the selection of trade partners on the basis of transparency is an effective means, in particular, of combating corruption. and another problem is the social responsibility of multinational corporations, which often behave differently inside the european union and outside the european union.
in writing. trade promotes poverty reduction and growth. while trade is a necessary condition for development, it is not enough on its own. domestic reforms are essential for growth driven by trade and investment. the economic performance of the least developed countries is hampered by a number of factors: low diversification of their economies and export base, insufficient infrastructure and services, lack of necessary skills, poor governance, corruption and lack of transparency, ineffective tax policies and tax evasion, poor social policies and insufficient redistribution instruments. the european union must focus its efforts on the poorest and most vulnerable countries and ensure that these efforts are tailored to their needs and constraints. one of the eu's main objectives is to ensure that economic growth and development are accompanied by social justice, including key labour standards and sustainable environmental practices, including through external policies. the least developed countries and other vulnerable countries are more exposed to the negative effects of crises. the rich countries and the eu, in the global economy, have a moral obligation to help reduce the levels of poverty and suffering in the world. one way we can do this effectively is by working out trade agreements that allow developing countries to participate effectively in the international economy and reap the benefits of globalisation.
the european union's trade and investment policy is not immune from the rules and principles that apply to other areas where the european union has competence. the objectives set out in the treaty on european union can only be achieved if the european union remains true to its values. given the european union's important position in the world and the moral responsibility that this entails, we are obliged to contribute by all possible means to improving the situation in the world. i therefore warmly welcome this resolution and the work of the rapporteur, which clearly shows the position of the european parliament as the only representative body in the european union and sends a clear signal that it will call for the principle of policy coherence for development to be respected and will always support the introduction of instruments that will lead to the support and integration of developing countries.

written − the european network and information security agency (enisa) was established in march 2004 for a period of five years, which was subsequently extended in 2008 until march 2012. in september 2010, the commission presented two proposals: the first was to extend the agency's mandate for 18 months until september 2013 and the second was more ambitious and concerned with modernising and streamlining the functioning of the agency. the agency meets specific needs at eu level: it coordinates stakeholders more effectively and efficiently than could be achieved through cooperation between member states. in addition, the agency should carry out additional tasks in relation to the computer emergency response units (cert) which would ensure that each of the certs of the member states and of the union has sufficiently developed capabilities and that those capabilities are matched to the capabilities of the most advanced units. network and information security often takes on a more global dimension, as recent events have shown, and therefore the agency needs to be able to engage in dialogue and cooperation with third countries and international organisations in order to better develop a common approach to potential threats.

written − the european emissions trading system (ets) is a key instrument with which the european union aims to reduce greenhouse gas emissions. it is a good tool that combines the needs of the market and is also designed to lead to environmental protection. if the ets is not set up in an efficient and flexible manner, taking into account the current conditions, it can be said with certainty that the objective set will not be achieved. moreover, an improperly set ets risks fragmenting the internal market, which is in direct contradiction with the fundamental objective of the european union, which is to create a single internal market. moreover, the ets is the basis for the smooth transition to a low-carbon economy that is planned in the future for environmental protection and would be a step backwards to a different, less environmentally friendly system. in addition, the effectiveness of the ets is also evidenced by the fact that countries such as australia and south korea have been inspired by the european example and are introducing similar schemes. for the reasons stated above, i support the motion for a resolution.
in writing. − between 1990 and 2006, carbon dioxide emissions from aviation almost doubled in the european union. this figure represents about 3% of total greenhouse gas emissions and is on the rise. it is forecast to grow by a further 63% by 2020. we must bear in mind that our commitment is to reduce our emissions by 20% compared with 1990 levels. therefore, everything must be done to effectively tackle global warming, but this can only be achieved on an international basis. that is why i believe it is important that aviation, which is part of the eu ets, should also play its part in the fight against climate change. two thirds of emissions are caused by intercontinental flights, but only one third of these are caused by flights from the eu. third countries should therefore also comply with the provisions of the ets. i voted in favour of the commission's position in the interests of a successful negotiation. this is our chance to show that the european union is not standing in the way of international agreement.

the gradual development and strengthening of relations with ukraine opens the way for us to acquire a significant partner on the eastern borders of the union. while the proposed amendments to the agreement between the european community and ukraine on the facilitation of the issuance of visas significantly improve and simplify the procedures in place, they do not allow citizens to travel freely between the union and ukraine. the eu has also committed itself to the development of a common visa policy, including the visa waiver for the citizens of the union. first of all, we need to assess the effect of the changes currently being made as soon as possible. consequently, we must agree with the ukrainians on the technical and legislative measures that the ukrainian side should implement in order to be able to talk meaningfully about free movement across the border. however, i think that any measure that facilitates people-to-people contacts and travel between ukraine and the union should be supported.
the global economic crisis has left its mark on all the member states of the european union, and today we have still not managed to properly bridge the period of regression and we must not distinguish between the euro area countries and the rest of the world. we are all in this together, and we must therefore be careful about measures that would lead to even greater macroeconomic imbalances. we are witnessing the birth of a banking union which will continue to be an important tool in the future in dealing with similarly complex economic and financial situations as we are experiencing today. it is certainly essential that euro area countries have sufficient financing under the mechanisms of the banking union to maintain the stability of the currency. however, for the banking union to truly benefit the whole of the european union, the resources allocated to crisis management need to be available to all.
it is natural that, like the euro area countries, other eu countries may find themselves in a situation where they need to recapitalise their banks. the european stability mechanism is designed to hedge euro area risks and, in its current form, is not designed to provide assistance to other member states. the report presented by ms hübner describes two options for working towards a bank recapitalisation solution for non-euro area members. i admit that from a legal point of view, the more acceptable alternative seems to me to be based on an amendment to the treaty establishing the european stability mechanism which would allow the participating states to contribute to the paid-up capital in order to provide a rescue mechanism for the recapitalisation of their banks. the second solution, namely the creation of a new instrument in the form of a loan that could be granted to the governments of non-euro area member states for the purpose of recapitalising banks, would, in my view, only fix the division between the functioning of the member states and the non-euro area member states.

in writing. − in the absence of a regulation establishing the multiannual financial framework (mff regulation) by the end of this year, article 312 (4) of the treaty on the functioning of the european union, which provides for the application of the ceilings of the last year of the current mff, and article 30 of the interinstitutional agreement on budgetary discipline and sound financial management in force, which provides for the extension of the 2013 ceilings, adjusted on the basis of a fixed deflator of 2% per annum, until a new mff regulation is adopted, will apply. i believe that it is in the context of the continuing economic and financial problems, as reflected in the austerity measures taken by several member states in response to the debt crisis, that parliament should continue to exercise a high degree of budgetary responsibility, control and restraint. similarly, i think it is important that parliament should seek to strike a delicate balance between budgetary constraints and structural savings on the one hand and a concerted effort to achieve efficiency on the other.
every country in the european union, whether in the eurozone or not, is facing a crisis. restrictive measures are being taken, and the consequences are being felt by people in every state. one important tool for dealing with the crisis is the stabilisation of the banking system. a eur 500 billion stabilisation mechanism has been set up for the euro area countries. for non-euro area countries, it is 50 billion. i therefore appreciate and supported the rapporteur's work, as it brings more financial assistance instruments to non-euro area member states. the lack of recapitalisation of banks and greater accountability of those who run them are only partial solutions. the foundations are being laid for a future banking union, which is to provide a single supervisory mechanism, a single resolution authority and a single deposit protection scheme. these measures will apply to all eu countries, including those outside the euro area.
in writing. − in order to ensure a genuine level playing field between euro-area and non-euro-area member states, it is necessary to aim to make bank recapitalisation possible also in non-euro-area member states. non-euro area member states have access to the balance of payments instrument, but its possibilities are rather limited compared with the ems. there appear to be no legal problems preventing the use of the balance of payments instrument to recapitalise banks. however, the instrument is limited by the amount of funds available to it. it is assumed that the maximum capacity of the balance of payments instrument cannot exceed eur 60 billion. if one of the borrowing member states were unable to repay the loan, the eu could risk being unable to repay its own liabilities. if a financial institution were to be recapitalised directly through the balance of payments facility, the eu budget would have an exposure to that financial institution. the risk is therefore significantly lower if the loan is granted to a member state rather than directly to a financial institution.
in writing. − if you have in the bank's annual report, the current president of the european central bank (ecb), mario draghi, called 2011 an "extraordinary year". whether he was, time will tell. although a new cycle has begun, its beginnings can be traced back to 2010 - partly to the worsening crisis and partly to the ecb's increasingly far-reaching interventions within the union, not least in the form of the recovery plans it has helped to enforce against some deficit countries. the ecb's actions were clearly guided by the context of the economic and social crisis and the 2011 annual report clearly reflects these changes. while looking ahead, one of the projects facing the eu is to establish a banking union to enable more effective, faster and appropriate responses to be used in times of crisis. this project will continue to follow its basic assumptions. however, i believe that it will not be possible to implement it without a clear relationship between the instruments, tasks and responsibilities in terms of legislation, monetary policy-making, surveillance and crisis management.

in writing. − council directive 2006/112/ec of 28 november 2006 on the common system of value added tax lays down rules on the time and place of supply of goods and services, the taxable amount, the taxable amount (vat) and the right to deduct. in order to ensure reliable and uniform treatment, to prevent irregularities, distortions of competition, double taxation or non-taxation and to limit the risk of tax evasion, i consider it important and justified to introduce specific rules covering the treatment of vat vouchers. at the same time, the tax treatment of the transactions linked to the voucher depends on the specific characteristics of the voucher. i therefore consider it important to distinguish between the different types of vouchers and to lay down the distinguishing features in union legislation. i also believe that a uniform framework for vouchers is a necessary condition for the implementation of the rules on the change of place of delivery in business-to-consumer relations by 2015. without this, it could be that an undertaking which sells identical vouchers to private persons in two different member states could apply completely different vat treatment to both vouchers, even if the vouchers and the goods or services to which they relate are the same. i consider this to be rather counterproductive in terms of simplifying and unifying the approaches envisaged in the new rules for the business-to-consumer relationship.
in writing − if you have the partial unification of the rules on the common system of value added tax is an important step towards the creation of a single market. the current vat system is not efficient. moreover, it is not in line with the concept of the internal market as set out in the primary treaties, as confirmed by the case law of the court of justice of the european union. it is clear from its case-law that anything which makes the exercise of fundamental freedoms less attractive, even indirectly, is contrary to european law. the european union has the mandate to act in this area and the duty to redress this adverse situation. the commission proposal is beneficial for public administrations as well as for businesses. for example, it avoids a situation where a company operating in several member states does not pay tax in any of them, thus eliminating the loss of revenue for the public treasury. on the other hand, undertakings will benefit from the legal certainty they have gained in meeting their tax obligations. for the reasons i have already mentioned, i welcome and support the commission's proposal.

in writing. − the hague convention of 23 november 2007 on the international recovery of child support and other forms of family maintenance constitutes an important mechanism for citizens, enabling them to claim and enforce child support against a debtor established in a third country. the european parliament has already approved the convention. however, in order to be applicable to the european union, it is necessary and important to deposit an instrument of approval. i consider it justified that all measures should be taken in the near future to enable the hague convention on the international recovery of child support and other forms of family maintenance to enter into force.
in writing − the adoption of the hague convention is primarily a measure to protect children, as the bulk of claims relate to child support. most children on child support are living in a single-parent family. for a single parent, the financial burden of providing for the family is doubled, and in many cases, alimony is a necessary means of covering the financial deficit. late payments often result in a situation where a child's basic needs must be denied. the commission should be able to assess the compatibility of the aid with the internal market on the basis of the criteria set out in article 107 (3) (c) of the treaty. it is therefore necessary that the hague convention enter into force as soon as possible. on the other hand, i would like to point out that effective child support is no substitute for a loving parent. therefore, not only should means be sought that address the negative consequences of family breakdown but also those that prevent such adverse situations from occurring in the first place.
in writing − every child has the right to an adequate standard of living necessary for his or her physical, mental, moral and social development, regardless of where he or she is born and where he or she lives. parents have a legal obligation to provide for their children and are responsible, within their means and financial means, for ensuring the living conditions necessary for their development. the hague convention on the international recovery of child support and other forms of family maintenance provides a good basis for a worldwide system of administrative cooperation and recognition and enforcement of decisions and agreements relating to maintenance. it provides for free legal aid in virtually all matters relating to child support and simplified procedures for recognition and enforcement. i supported the report because the measures adopted in annexes ii and iii not only simplify the procedure but also help to eliminate the frequently recurring delays in the recovery of maintenance for children and other family members.
