in writing. − i voted in favour of deletion of article 4 of the sógor report. i am disappointed by the current situation of sending the report back to committee, also keeping article 4. besides creating uncertainty in statistics, the current version of the report has unpredictable consequences for some member states, mainly the new ones. it is unacceptable that one of the european basic principles, namely the principle of free movement of people actually creates discrimination against new member states. it is indisputable that there is a phenomenon of numerous new member states’ citizens ‘using’ their right of free movement seeking job in one of the ‘old’ member states. however, often this is about short-term residence linked to short- or fix-term working contracts after which the ‘newcomers’ return to their home countries. we should not forget that this is about the movement of eu citizens within the eu and not an immigration issue. it is about living the basic principles of the eu. determining the qualified majority in the council by "usual residence" would have therefore undermine the spirit of european citizenship and would have fundamental consequences, resulting that the voice of citizens of new member states would have been curtailed.
in writing. − if you have the growing and complex demographic challenges have created a clear need for a common regulatory framework for demographic statistics at european level. it is necessary and important to collect high-quality information on the population and life events related to the population in the union. almost every policy area the eu deals with - whether economic, social or environmental policy - requires high-quality demographic statistics to help set operational targets and assess progress. the democratic process within the union requires annual population estimates of the highest possible quality. data on the total population of each member state, collected and published by eurostat, are used each year in the union's decision-making process (qualified majority voting in the council). moreover, the monitoring of progress made in the eu in terms of economic, social and territorial cohesion is assessed through a report based, inter alia, on regional demographic data from eurostat. for this reason, in my view, european demographic statistics have such an important justification.
in writing. − i would like to express my regret that the report on european demographic statistics, which is also relevant to the future decision-making procedures of the eu in the council, was not discussed in plenary. i believe that the usual estimation of population by place of residence for qualified majority voting in the council may lead to a new kind of political imbalance at eu level, may not reflect the real demographic situation in europe and may undermine the form of cooperation between member states as it is known today. european migration processes are not new developments, such movements have always existed, only their causes change. the european union is founded on the principle of free movement, which includes the right of citizens of the union to move and reside freely within its territory. it is precisely contrary to the spirit of that principle to adopt rules which are likely to upset the political balance between member states by using data obtained from union citizens enjoying the right of free movement. the proposal for a regulation does not place adequate population statistics at the heart of the council's vote count. the evaluation report provided for in the review clause supplementing the text of the regulation will be given particular attention, as it will have to give a realistic picture of, inter alia, the impact of demographic data collected under the new system on qualified majority decision-making in the council.
in writing − the importance of accurate and reliable statistics and information on the population and life events associated with democratic processes in the european union is growing. although at first glance it may seem that we are voting on a very technical report, we must be aware that high-quality statistical data on individual member states are also used in the decision-making process within the structures of the european union. qualified majority voting in the eu council will be defined as from 1 november 2014 by a majority representing 55% of the council members, drawn from the 15 member states and representing 65% of the population. if our decisions are to be fully legitimate, they must also be based on the right data. it is now eurostat that publishes demographic and statistical data every year and monitors the economic, social and territorial progress of the member states and of the eu itself. if we do not want to jeopardise the collection of statistical data by changing definitions and international best practices, we should generally follow the approach of the european commission and the council. i believe that our task is to lay the foundation for the harmonised collection of reliable demographic data.
in writing. − if you have under the eu waste shipment regulation, the export of hazardous waste from eu countries to non-oecd countries has been prohibited since 1998. due to the diversity of hazardous materials on board a ship, any ship coming from the eu for dismantling is hazardous waste and can therefore only be legally dismantled within the oecd. however, this legislation is almost systematically circumvented. according to the commission's impact assessment, in 2009, more than 90% of eu-flagged ships were actually dismantled outside the oecd countries, mainly in south asia. the global ship scrapping rate increased almost sixfold between 2007 and 2009. in the current situation, many ship owners are scrapping their vessels rather than investing in expensive additional equipment. in order to improve the current situation, the commission aims, through the ship recycling regulation in question, to significantly reduce the negative impacts associated with the recycling of eu-flagged ships, in particular in south asia, without creating an unnecessary economic burden.

the european court of human rights ruled last week that if a healthy person wants to perform euthanasia, the state should create the conditions for it. otherwise, the state is in breach of article 8 of the european convention on the right to privacy. article 2 of the convention guarantees the right to life for every human being. the right to euthanasia simply cannot be compatible with this convention. this is also confirmed by the legal situation of the vast majority of member states. if we elevate the right to privacy over the right to life, we destroy the natural hierarchy of rights enshrined in the convention. i would therefore urge my colleagues who ignore the needs of the natural family in the creation of european standards to read the gros judgment in detail. because if old people who are healthy in body and mind see no reason to go on living, it is a signal that the family bonds between our generations are breaking down.

in writing. let us look at the facts. the european union loses up to €1 trillion a year to tax fraud and evasion! this incredible figure costs us €2,000 per year for every single citizen of the european union. the average tax loss in europe now exceeds the total amount spent by member states on healthcare and is more than four times the amount spent on education in the eu! the tax revenue measure in its current form represents an alarming loss of revenue for public administration in the union and thus a major threat to the european union's social model, which is based on quality public services available to all our citizens! the loss of tax revenue continues to increase the deficit and debt levels of all member states, which is extremely damaging, especially in the current most difficult period of the crisis! however, as a result of tax fraud and tax evasion, all available resources to support public investment, growth and employment are being phased out. but what's striking about all of this is that we've accepted this state of affairs for decades. we need the strength of the social model! we need to ensure growth and social cohesion, these things are more important in these difficult times than ever before! i believe that effective and progressive taxation is of paramount importance in the context of the competences of public authorities. the citizens of the european union have their needs and expectations, and we have a duty to meet those expectations.
in writing. in the eu, it is estimated that up to €1 trillion is lost annually to tax fraud and tax evasion. however, there is research that says that the amount is much higher than 1 trillion eur per year! if we could stop these tax evasions, the total public debt of the eu countries would be paid off in only 8.8 years. interestingly, there is no relationship between the level of tax burden in a country and the level of tax evasion. recent studies have refuted the view that the higher the tax burden, the higher the tax evasion and tax avoidance. companies that use tax evasion as a business strategy gain an unfair competitive advantage over publicly traded companies that cannot use similar practices. this ultimately harms the competitiveness of the member states. tax fraud and tax evasion are depleting the resources needed to support the necessary public investment, growth and employment. our aim must therefore be to develop a common european strategy that all the member states will accept and implement. states must agree to harmonise their tax bases, to enforce measures to prevent the shifting of profits to tax havens and tax avoidance.
in writing. in the european union, it is estimated that up to eur 1 trillion is lost each year to tax fraud and tax evasion. this alarming size of the tax revenue gap represents a cost of approximately eur 2 000 per eu citizen per year. the average tax loss in europe today exceeds the total amount spent by member states on health and is more than four times the amount spent on education. all this has been happening for decades, in times of the greatest economic, financial and social crisis, when the automatic stabilisers of the welfare state to ensure growth and social cohesion are more important than ever. the current gap in tax revenues in europe therefore represents not only an alarming loss of public revenue but also a danger to the preservation of the eu's social model based on quality public services accessible to all. tax fraud and tax evasion therefore constitute a serious and multifaceted problem requiring a coordinated approach at national, eu and international level. i therefore consider it necessary for the commission to come forward with a legislative proposal which would provide clear criteria for the distinction between tax havens. at the same time, a blacklist of these tax havens should be drawn up by the end of next year and the necessary tools should be provided to block banking licenses for financial institutions involved in tax fraud.
in writing. − international air transport relations between member states and third countries have traditionally been governed by bilateral air service agreements. these include a 'destination clause' which allows a third country to refuse, withdraw or suspend the authorisation or licence of an air carrier which has been designated by a member state but which is not majority owned or subject to effective control by that member state or its nationals. the council, by its decision of 5 june 2003, therefore authorised the commission to negotiate so-called horizontal agreements with the third countries concerned, replacing the traditional designation clause with an eu designation clause allowing all eu carriers to benefit from the right of establishment and to obtain non-discriminatory access to routes between the eu and third countries. in this case, sri lanka has signed 15 bilateral agreements, the relevant provisions of which need to be replaced or supplemented by the provisions of a single agreement concluded on behalf of the union. the agreement was signed on 27 september 2012. in its decision of 26 november 2012, the council requested parliament to give its consent to the conclusion of the agreement in accordance with the provisions of the treaty on the functioning of the european union. i consider it appropriate for the committee on transport and tourism to give its consent to the conclusion of the agreement.

in writing. − the takeover offers directive provides minimum guidelines to ensure transparency and legal certainty in the execution of takeover bids and to grant information rights to shareholders, employees and other interested parties. some member states are considering adapting or have already adapted their harmonised national takeover bid rules in order to increase transparency in the capital market and strengthen the rights of the target company and its stakeholders. member states were given until may 2006 to transpose the provisions of the directive into their national law. given the financial and economic developments of the last few years, a proper assessment of the application of the directive is difficult, if not impossible. the financial crisis that started in 2007 hit all european markets. despite a whole package of measures to stabilise and revive the economy, the crisis has deepened and europe is still mired in the crisis of capital markets and the economic and debt crisis. it is an unfortunate coincidence that the date of transposition of the directive coincides with the beginning of the crisis. it is therefore justified to seek to provide more relevant data on the basis of which it will be possible to determine not only the necessary amendments to the directive but also the specific harmonisation measures that are desirable to be adopted in the future.

in writing. − the deepwater horizon explosion on 20 april 2010 killed 11 men and caused an oil slick containing some 4.9 million barrels (780,000 m3) of crude oil. it took three months to close the well and another two months to complete the rescue well. the accident also prompted a review of eu policies: the european commission immediately started to assess the safety of offshore oil and gas production in european waters. it concluded that further steps should be prepared to ensure that best practices, regulatory regimes already in place in some eu member states, are disseminated across the eu through a clear modern framework at eu level. the proposal for a regulation on safety of offshore oil and gas exploration, development and production, which the commission presented to parliament in october 2011, focuses on concrete measures that should redress any discrepancies and fragmentation between member states' practice and legislation in offshore oil and gas production. the proposal aims to respond to the increased risk by ensuring that the industry uses best practices across the union to manage serious threats by strengthening the union's preparedness and response capacity and clarifying the existing legal framework for liability and redress.

in writing. − renewable energy allows us to diversify our energy supply. this increases our security of supply and improves european competitiveness, creating new sectors, jobs, economic growth and export opportunities, while reducing greenhouse gas emissions. strong growth in renewable energy by 2030 could create more than 3 million jobs, including in smes. if europe maintains its leadership in renewable energy, our global competitiveness will also increase, as the 'clean technology' sector becomes increasingly important in the world. in 2007, the european union set an ambitious target of 20% renewable energy and 10% renewable energy in transport by 2020 and supported these objectives with a range of supporting policies. the renewable energy target is a key objective of the europe 2020 strategy to ensure smart, sustainable and inclusive growth. these policies are delivering their first results at the beginning of 2012 and the eu is now well on track to achieve its objectives.

in writing. − if you have in a democracy, the media play a vital public watchdog role, as they allow citizens to express their right to information, to control and to assess the actions and decisions of those who exercise power or influence, in particular on the occasion of consultations on elections. they can also play a role in shaping the agendas of public bodies by using their authority as information brokers and thus acting as public opinion shapers. free and independent media and the free exchange of information play a crucial role in the processes of democratic transformation in non-democratic regimes. the commission is asked to closely monitor the freedom and pluralism of the media in the acceding countries and to pay due attention to the role of free media in promoting democracy worldwide. the fundamental rights of citizens to freedom of expression and information can only be guaranteed through freedom and pluralism of the media, with journalists and the media able to exercise their right and duty to inform and report on events and decisions of public interest to citizens in an impartial and neutral manner.
in writing. − freedom of speech and expression, which includes freedom of the media, is one of the greatest achievements of human society and one of the fundamental pillars of the rule of law. for this reason, it must be protected, since it is precisely today that invisible pressures to limit it are mounting. on the other hand, although i fully share the resolution's aims, its text sometimes gives the impression that the authors of the text equate defamation with freedom of speech. the authors themselves point out in point x to the serious shortcomings in journalistic work due to the abandonment of control and double control of journalistic sources. i also consider slander to be a serious lack of journalistic work. while i do not agree that defamation should be classified as a criminal offence, there must be mechanisms in place to enable victims of defamation to defend themselves effectively. under no circumstances can gossip be accepted as a socially acceptable form of journalistic work.
in writing. − the importance of media freedom and pluralism arises in relation to a pluralistic and democratic political system. freedom and pluralism of the media are the result and guarantee of an effective and legitimate democratically elected government. the media are expected to provide a platform for freedom of expression accessible to all social groups. they should furthermore promote constructive public debate and appropriate political engagement of citizens aimed at raising the level of political awareness. however, all these demands and requirements for the media face a number of constraints, in many cases due to the nature of the media as such, but also arising from the social and political context. freedom and pluralism of the media must therefore be balanced against the requirements of respect for the fundamental human rights and civil liberties on which the union is founded. the report by renate weber therefore correctly identifies the points of support needed to maintain and possibly improve the position of the media. these include, for example, supporting the establishment of universal criteria for the appointment of heads of state media, ensuring their independence from state power. it also calls for the revision and amendment of the audiovisual media services directive (avmsd-2010/13/eu), in particular to extend its scope. it should include minimum standards for the protection and safeguarding of fundamental rights such as freedom of expression, the right to information and transparency.
in writing. − free media, pluralism and independent journalism are essential elements for the proper functioning of any democracy and the rule of law. unfortunately, we still see violations of media freedom in some eu member states, as this report shows. although the report does not contain everything i expected it to contain, i supported it because i think it can become an important tool for the ep to discuss media freedom more broadly. i also find it very positive that the report on the media not only takes stock of the situation but also sets out specific subjects and measures that can greatly help free media and the maintenance of media pluralism in the future. i expect the commission to make every effort within its powers to ensure that the eu member states respect the charter of fundamental rights. while i see the protection of freedom of expression and information and freedom of the media as a duty of the member states, i believe that the eu will adopt legislative measures that protect pluralism as one of the fundamental pillars of the right to information and freedom of expression.
i supported the report submitted for two reasons. first, i share the rapporteur's view that sustainable pension systems must be based on a combination of the general and capitalisation pillars. the basis of pensions is solidarity between generations, but in an ageing europe this will soon no longer be the case. the second reason for my support is that the commission has called on the member states in its white paper to include the period of caring for another person in retirement. i consider this a very important moment, because it's the first bold step towards recognizing the value of women's informal work. i hope that others will follow, which will confirm that in europe our eyes have finally been opened.
2012 was the european year of active ageing and solidarity between generations. on this occasion, i organized and participated in several events for people of retirement age. among the most frequent questions were those on pensions, which are a priority for our older citizens in terms of ensuring a decent standard of living and economic independence. the demographic ageing curve poses a major challenge to pension systems across the european union. i supported the report because i think it highlights the current problems of pension systems and, importantly, it comes with concrete proposals to ensure adequately sustainable, secure european pension systems.
in writing. − the sustainability of pension systems in europe is becoming an increasingly pressing issue. demographic changes make it rational to adjust the retirement age to life expectancy in each member state. however, it is a sobering and at least equally serious problem that workers leave the labour market much earlier than the statutory retirement age. the creation of working conditions, the training of people over 50 is essential if we want to keep them in the labour market. the myth that early retirement creates more job opportunities for young people needs to be debunked, because research shows that where youth unemployment is high, older people are also high. the gender pension gap is also a problem to be solved. it is unacceptable that women are disadvantaged because they have children or that they use calculations that result in lower pensions. one of the key messages of the report is that pension systems need to be diversified, even if there is no uniform interpretation of the second or third pillars. the ability of the second pillar, the payment of pensions, to perform could also be jeopardised by the attempt to make pension funds subject to the capital requirements directive.
in writing. − pensions have come under pressure in every eu country. governments in the euro area are introducing austerity measures to comply with the stability and growth pact by balancing income and expenditure or are forced to make drastic cuts to reduce excessive deficits. moreover, the population of all member states is ageing. life expectancy varies across europe, but is increasing everywhere. also, a growing number of retired people are living longer and in better health. the proportion of the working population is decreasing. the birth rate is falling, young people are studying longer and entering the labour market later. solidarity between generations, which means that young people in work will cover the cost of pensions for older people, cannot be further escalated at any cost. the european agenda for adequate, safe and sustainable pensions for young and old appears to be the appropriate starting point for a discussion that can be followed by reforms through non-legally binding instruments and, where appropriate, legislation. overall, while recognising and maintaining the obligations of member states and social partners, there is now a need to build systems that contribute to greater labour market mobility and freedom of movement and provide solutions for the present and the future.
in writing. − experience has shown that no form of pension system is 100% effective, and i therefore believe that the state should allow all three pillars to exist in parallel, complementing each other and allowing the citizen to have a choice and to participate actively in the decision-making process on the construction of his pension. i would like to draw attention to the problem of discrimination against women, which unfortunately also exists in this area. we still face the situation that women have a lower financial valuation, which results in a lower pension. similarly, they are penalized for motherhood, as they often interrupt their careers to care for their families. the pension system cannot be set up to punish women for choosing to become mothers, as low fertility is one of the roots of today's unhappy demographic situation. furthermore, i would like to point out that the problem of loss of pension rights, to which the rapporteur draws attention in her explanatory report, is clearly not due to a lack of legislation but mainly to the incorrect application of existing legislation by national public authorities, who are unable to apply existing legislation or the case law of the court of justice to a specific situation, which often results in the non-payment of pension rights through the fault of the public administration.
the ultimate objective of the measures to establish a banking union is to ensure the stability of the single currency, the euro. the forthcoming changes also include the conferral of new powers on the european central bank, which should take over the supervision of euro area financial institutions from july 2014. the new powers will thus also allow the european central bank to decide on the closure and liquidation of a problematic financial institution anywhere in the euro area. in addition to conducting an independent monetary policy, the ecb will also be involved in major economic decisions, and i therefore propose to subject this area of supervisory policy to the supervision of the european parliament. i am not sure that this very mechanism of political involvement of the european parliament in the activities of the european central bank will not be a problem for the functioning of the european central bank as an independent institution. while the intention to better control the work of financial institutions in the euro area is justified, we need to model very sensitively the institutions and mechanisms for exercising this control. in the end, i think we should work on a system that oversees the good management of financial institutions and, when necessary and when problems arise, allows for a certain degree of solidarity between banks, but not solidarity between taxpayers and the financial sector.
in writing. since the start of the banking crisis, the euro area has not only seen a weakening of the stability of the financial system, but also a significant erosion of confidence in banks and the euro. while the establishment of banking supervisors has helped to improve cooperation between national supervisors and to create a single set of rules for eu financial services, the euro area economy continues to be mired in recession and unemployment rates are breaking new records. the discussion on this subject alone shows that any negotiations relating to the prudential supervision of credit institutions and involving specific tasks for the ecb are not at all straightforward and therefore require due attention. the confidence of the banking sector can only be restored if common standards are respected and a single supervisory mechanism with direct supervision of banks and cross-border banking markets is put in place. i expect the ecb to work very closely with the european supervisors and to ensure convergence and consistency of supervisory practices.

the european union is a community of sovereign states which have formed a coordinated political and economic grouping by treaty. the measures proposed by the commission and the parliament in relation to european monetary union should therefore respect this fundamental premise and not deprive national parliaments and governments of the member states of the freedom to determine their economic and social policies. the next step towards fiscal or economic union, as proposed by the french president, for example, cannot be achieved without making changes to the treaty of lisbon, which means that our citizens would also have to agree to and accept such a concept. however, our citizens' confidence in the european project is clearly declining and more and more citizens feel that their governments and parliaments are more competent to solve their problems. the commission and parliament's approach to centralising decision-making does not seem to be in line with the will of the citizens, and it might be better to look for a solution based on well-coordinated cooperation between member states rather than leading us towards a transfer union.
madam president, parliament is now voting on consent to the eu-canada agreement on customs cooperation with respect to matters related to supply chain security. the proposed agreement builds on and expands the preceding agreements of 1998 on mutual assistance in customs matters establishing a legal basis for eu-canada customs cooperation on supply chain security and risk management. in particular it opens the door to mutual recognition agreements on customs security, reinforces the customs-related aspects for securing the logistics chain on international trade including container security, and facilitates legitimate trade. the agreement has no budgetary implications for the union budget; it will certainly improve our trade relations with canada, and it is complementary and probably helpful to the comprehensive economic and trade agreement, negotiations for which i hope will be concluded very soon.

in writing. − tax havens and tax avoidance are a major political issue today. it is estimated that up to eur 1 trillion of public finances is lost each year as a result of unfair tax schemes. this alarming sum represents a cost of approximately eur 2000 per year, per capita for each european citizen. the average amount lost in tax evasion in europe today exceeds the total amount spent by member states on healthcare, and is also more than four times the amount spent on education within the member states of the european union. in the current crisis, more than 26 million people are unable to find work, thousands lose their savings and are forced to face difficult living conditions. europe must strive to take the necessary measures to build on the current progress in the fight against tax fraud and tax evasion. i believe it is imperative to stand up for social justice. it is also very important to work towards a stricter regulatory approach to avoid the risk of active circumvention and thus of such large-scale tax evasion or financial losses.
in writing. − coordination at european level is essential, as it is true that each chain is only as strong as its weakest link, and the loss of public revenue is alarming. on the other hand, the fiscal sovereignty of the state must be fully respected, which implies the possibility for the state to organise its own tax system, including the setting of a lower tax burden. moreover, member states cannot punish conduct and the subsequent creation of business structures which in practice result in non-payment of tax if they themselves have provided for that purpose by vague or excessively vague legislation enabling the taxable person to act in that way. it is unrealistic to expect a taxpayer to voluntarily comply with something that the law does not require. i believe that the most effective way to prevent undesirable behaviour by taxpayers is not to punish them but to fill the gaps in both domestic legislation and bilateral tax treaties that de facto legalise such behaviour.
in writing. − all member states are now faced with the problem that public budgets spend more than they receive. it is right that on the one hand we are looking for ways of using the budget more efficiently. but at the same time, you have to think about the revenue side. tax evasion and avoidance are not the only problems, but also tax avoidance, which exploits loopholes in existing legislation and a lack of pan-european and international cooperation. the total tax loss is estimated to be around eur 2 000 per eu citizen per year. i support preserving the tax sovereignty of eu member states, but at the same time i agree that we need to start tackling the problem of tax havens. the first step is a proposed eu-wide definition of tax havens, which should be followed by the establishment of a blacklist of tax havens. companies that violate eu tax rules should be excluded from public procurement. as taxation is not an eu competence, the responsibility for combating tax fraud lies primarily with the member states.
in writing. − the recent debt crisis has given rise to a number of new problems in the european union, which require a proper adjustment of tax policies in the short, medium and long term. some countries have already made these adjustments, but others are still waiting. it is essential to stress that tax policy remains a matter for national authorities and that it is therefore necessary to respect the different tax systems of the member states, while removing as soon as possible the obstacles to the internal market and the uncertainty and misunderstandings resulting from legal gaps. while fiscal discipline and structural reforms are essential to restore confidence in fiscal policy and reduce public debt, it is also justified to prioritise fiscal measures aimed at growth and consumption taxes over labour taxes, as they appear to be more appropriate in the long term to support economic growth and employment. as the issues of double taxation and tax evasion remain a serious problem and lead to significant budgetary losses in the european union, i consider it important and justified to give this problem adequate attention.
in writing. − tax policy remains the national competence of each member state, but appropriate effective coordination of tax rules at european level can bring more transparency to tax policies and stability to budgets. at a time when each member state is struggling to balance its budget, tax policy must be the determining factor in mitigating the impact on employers, but at the same time it must be a source of growth and development for the economy. tax collection must be made more efficient, but at the same time the refund of tax overpayments must be made within the statutory deadlines, so that the state does not become a liquidator of enterprises. i supported the report and i agree with the rapporteur's proposal to create, on the basis of a thorough analysis, a pan-european information system to ensure greater transparency and to serve to monitor the different tax structures and to inform each other in order to prevent various tax fraud and evasion.
four years ago, the leaders of the european union agreed to include the czech republic in the exception to the application of the charter of fundamental rights of the european union. however, as the rapporteur notes, this derogation does not derogate from the binding provisions of the charter. it's a waiver of participation. it does not amend the charter. the text of the protocol does not alter the legal situation which would have existed in the absence of the protocol. however, the very existence of the protocol has given rise to legal uncertainty and political confusion. in this respect, it has an adverse impact not only on the united kingdom, poland or potentially the czech republic, but on all eu countries. we did not vote today on whether or not the czech republic can join the exception to the application of the charter. parliament decided whether a convention should be convened in such a situation. i voted in favour because i don't think it's necessary to convene a convention.
in writing. − the charter of fundamental rights of the european union was drawn up by a convention which met from 17 december 1999 to 2 october 2000 and in which representatives of the european parliament, the member states, national parliaments and the commission took part. the charter was subsequently promulgated on 7 december 2000 and the text was adopted in strasbourg on 12 december 2007. the second convention ran from 22 february 2002 to 18 july 2003 and aimed to draft a treaty establishing a constitution for europe, the substantial part of which was incorporated into the treaty of lisbon, which entered into force on 1 december 2009. both conventions were convened to address the main issues concerning the constitutional order of the union, including the adoption of a binding text establishing binding rights and principles recognised by the union. it is therefore not necessary to convene a convention to examine a proposal to extend to the czech republic protocol no 30 on the application of the charter of fundamental rights of the european union to poland and the united kingdom, since the possible effect of that proposal would be limited.
in writing. − the government of the czech republic is seeking its country's accession to protocol no 30 on the application of the charter of fundamental rights of the european union to poland and the united kingdom. all three states most concerned by this discussion approached the question of the charter from different angles. the uk has sought to limit the possibility that the charter would give the eu a new reason to legislate in certain areas, namely labour law, thereby going beyond its framework. poland, on the other hand, wanted the charter to be free of restrictions on its right to decide on issues such as public morality, family law, abortion, gay rights, etc. the possibility of withdrawing from the protocol is currently being discussed in poland. the czech republic, on the instructions of its president, has adopted a rather eurosceptic stance. during the negotiations on the lisbon treaty, it reached its own categorical declaration no 53, in which it expressed its concern about the charter's impact on the principle of subsidiarity, the allocation of powers, respect for national constitutions and international agreements.
in writing. − the commission proposal responds to the need for a comprehensive european legal framework that will provide recognition and the highest possible level of protection to all victims throughout the union. the proposal for a regulation complements the european protection order directive, which ensures mutual recognition of protection measures in criminal matters. the combined application of both instruments (criminal and civil) will allow persons who have been granted a protection order to move freely and safely within the eu as provided for in article 3 of the treaty on european union and will ultimately lead to the strengthening and development of the area of freedom, security and justice in the union. in accordance with the procedures resulting from the implementation of the treaty of lisbon, rule 51 of parliament's rules of procedure allows the two committees to draw up reports, acting jointly. the preparation of this report drew on the impetus of the discussions of the committee on legal affairs and the committee on women's rights and gender equality, as well as on the cooperation between the two rapporteurs. the final report presented reflects the results of the compromise agreement reached in the negotiations with the council during the cypriot and irish presidencies.
in writing. − the european union has successfully established a system of mutual recognition of judgments in civil and commercial matters under the brussels i regulation. this step has made a significant contribution to strengthening the area of freedom, security and justice. on the other hand, full completion of this area is not possible without further partial steps, including the introduction of mutual recognition of protection measures in civil matters. these measures are intended to enhance the rapid and effective protection of persons in need at any given moment, and the rapid action of the authorities concerned is a necessary condition for the effectiveness of the protection provided. moreover, the introduction of mutual recognition of protection measures will make a significant contribution to the protection of women and children, who are often the most vulnerable groups in the population. my only comment is that it would be a shame to limit the provision of special training to only those professionals who are likely to come into contact with victims of gender-based violence. every victim is a victim and deserves adequate assistance. the motive for the danger is irrelevant in this respect.
in writing. − the commission's proposal for a regulation on the mutual recognition of protection measures in civil matters will provide the highest possible protection to all victims throughout the eu. it is important to ensure that a person who has been granted protection in one member state does not lose that protection when he moves to another member state. a multilingual certificate should ensure this. this would ensure not only the rapid and simple recognition of safeguard measures but also their rapid and simple enforcement. in order to make protected persons better aware of their rights, it is necessary for member states to include information on free movement, protection measures and the uniform certificate in their education and awareness-raising campaigns. the rapporteurs also praised the work of civil society, in particular ngos and other voluntary organisations providing expert support to protected persons. protected persons should receive information and assistance in an intelligible form and in a language they understand, taking into account the needs of the protected person. i supported the ep's legislative resolution.
in writing. − the regulation on mutual recognition of protection measures in civil matters, adopted in 2002, responds to the need to harmonise the application of the european protection order directive. this regulation, unlike the directive, will apply directly in all member states and will also provide the necessary protection for victims of crime when travelling for a short period or moving to another eu member state. the new rules, which will enter into force on 1 january 2015 after approval by the eu council, will simplify the system for filing protection applications. this will help to alleviate the situation of women and children, who are the most frequent victims of violent crime. the introduction of a standard multilingual form should reduce translation costs and avoid the additional costs incurred by a protected person in connection with his or her movement within the eu.
in writing. − the customs relations between the european union and canada are based on the 1998 agreement on cooperation and mutual assistance in customs matters (cmaa). in 2005, canada indicated its interest in working more closely with the eu to ensure security throughout the supply chain and manage risks. the draft customs cooperation agreement, as far as supply chain security issues are concerned, which the commission has been discussing since may 2011, builds on the 1998 cmaa and extends it on the basis of this option provided for therein. the new agreement aims to strengthen customs aspects to ensure the logistics chain of international trade, including container security, while facilitating legitimate trade. it provides the legal basis for enhanced customs cooperation between the eu and canada on matters relating to risk standards, security controls, minimum standards for risk management techniques, information and data exchange, strategic partnerships on cargo control, as well as cooperation in multilateral fora such as the world customs organization. it will also build on, inter alia, the key elements of the world customs organisation's safe system of standards for the security and facilitation of global trade. the consent of the european parliament to its conclusion is justified and important.
in writing. − i thank the rapporteur for his work in informing the members of the european parliament of the draft legislative resolution. canada is one of the european union's oldest and closest partners. this partnership started back in the 1950s and today, at the beginning of the 21st century, we should not only cultivate good relations but also continue economic cooperation at a higher level. the 1998 cmaa is an important point in our economic cooperation. it is our task to create the conditions for trade between the union and canada to remain as simple as possible and for the rules to be transparent, as this will prevent illegality and increase the security of the chain. for the reasons set out above, i agree with the agreement and express my belief that it will help in the efforts to increase the security of supply chains worldwide.
in writing. − the european banking authority was established in 2011 to coordinate the work of national regulatory authorities and ensure the uniform application of eu rules. but the supervision of banks itself remained primarily in the hands of the national regulatory authorities. the european banking authority also provides expert advice to the eu institutions, has conducted a so-called stress test for banking and oversees the current recapitalisation performance of eu banks. the proposed banking union will change the way banks in the euro area are supervised, as a single supervisory mechanism will be established within the european central bank.
in writing. − the current financial and economic crisis has brought europe's banking system to the brink of collapse. the integrity of the single currency and the single market is threatened by the fragmentation of the financial sector. the integration of the banking sector now needs to be stepped up in order to strengthen european unity, restore financial stability and lay the foundations for economic recovery. in order to preserve financial stability in europe and to enhance the positive effects of market integration on growth and prosperity, the integration of supervisory responsibilities should therefore be strengthened.
in writing. − in view of the ongoing crisis and its consequences, i welcome the proposal for a regulation conferring special powers on the european central bank concerning the prudential supervision of credit institutions. i personally welcome the choice of article 127 (6) tfeu as the legal basis for the adoption of this act, although i am concerned about the possibility of extending the scope of the regulation to countries outside the euro area. article 127 (6) must be read in the context of the treaty as a whole and also in the context of the case-law of the court of justice in luxembourg. for this reason, it is necessary to take account not only of the principle of sincere cooperation, which is binding not only on the member states but also on the european institutions themselves, which implies that the european union must necessarily respect the principle of subsidiarity. article 282 (4) states, inter alia, that the powers of the member states and their central banks whose currency is not the euro are preserved. while i am aware of the need for uniform control not only in view of the single market but also for the very effectiveness of this regulation, i would venture to express my doubts as to whether article 127 (6) can also be used as a legal basis for acts which will also be addressed to non-euro area states.
in writing. − the transfer of powers from the member states to the eu in the field of taxation supervision must be accompanied by a strengthening of responsibility and control. the new eu banking supervision rules, which are a response to the failure of the banking sector, will allow the european central bank to supervise the largest banks in the euro area directly and to participate in the supervision of other banks. however, today's vote on these rules was not yet final, as negotiations are still ongoing with the european central bank on the details of its responsibility as a supervisor. a balance needs to be struck between powers and responsibilities in the area of banking supervision. the european central bank (ecb), as a supervisory authority, must be subject to stricter requirements in terms of openness, accountability and control.
in writing. − the report amends the european commission's proposal for a recast of directive 2007/23/ec on the placing of pyrotechnic articles on the market. the existing directive 2007/23/ec lays down the safety requirements to be met by pyrotechnic articles in order to be made available on the eu market. the new legislative framework was adopted to address the shortcomings of the union's harmonisation legislation in order to complete the single market with fair competition and safe products. the inconsistent implementation and enforcement of existing union harmonised legislation in the member states, as well as the complexity of the regulation, have made it increasingly difficult for economic operators and authorities to interpret and apply the legislation properly, leading to unfair market conditions and the placing on the market of dangerous products. the so-called product package provides an overall framework for simplifying product legislation with a view to harmonising the rules and making them more comprehensible for economic operators as well as market surveillance authorities. the amendments made to the provisions of this directive concern: the definitions, the obligations of economic operators, the presumption of conformity based on harmonised standards, the declaration of conformity, the ce marking, the notified bodies, the procedure relating to the safeguard clause and the conformity assessment procedures.
in writing. − the legislator has responded flexibly to market needs and the new legislative framework (nlr) addresses the shortcomings of the previous legislation that practice has pointed out. the new legislation will benefit not only economic operators but also ordinary consumers. last but not least, it is another step towards completing the single european market. i consider the main contribution of the nrp to be the unification and simplification of legislation. this simplification will help operators to understand existing legislation, which will lead to its correct application and to improvements in their production processes. moreover, market surveillance authorities will have an easier task in monitoring compliance and will be better equipped to stop the import of dangerous pyrotechnics from third countries. last but not least, the correct application of the legislation will automatically lead to increased protection of the final consumer and increased confidence in the ce marking, since only products that comply with the requirements of the european union can be marked with it.
in writing. − unfair market conditions, unequal treatment of non-compliant products or placing dangerous products on the market. these are just some of the shortcomings highlighted in the report. i supported the report because i expect that the amendments to the current directive will remedy these shortcomings. i also expect that the introduction of the new legislative framework will not be a matter of theory but will become an integral part of existing product legislation. i welcome all the commission's efforts to improve and harmonise the legislation in force, which should guarantee the free movement of pyrotechnic articles in the internal market. i also want to draw attention to the safety and protection of vulnerable consumers, especially those for whom pyrotechnic products are not intended for professional use. i expect that all measures, amendments and additions which present a risk to the health and safety of persons will not only be incorporated into the directive but will become part of the legislation of the union and its member states.
in writing. − if you have pursuant to article 33 of the audiovisual media services directive (avms directive), the commission is to submit a report on the application of this directive to the european parliament, the council and the european economic and social committee on a regular basis. the avms directive aims , within the meaning of the right to freedom of expression and information enshrined in article 11 of the charter of fundamental rights of the european union to ensure the free movement of audiovisual media services as an instrument of the internal market, while ensuring the protection of important public interest objectives. it sets minimum requirements to ensure a level playing field and allows the free movement of audiovisual media services across europe. in some cases, the avms directive harmonises certain concepts (e.g. advertising spots), but in other cases it does not affect the member states' competence to lay down specific requirements taking into account national circumstances and traditions (e.g. content harmful to minors). overall, the european regulatory framework for audiovisual media services serves citizens and businesses well. the current need is to monitor market developments and new business models and to ensure that the regulatory framework continues to provide the right conditions for growth and the achievement of public interest objectives.
in writing. − the constant development of technologies and the possibilities for the dissemination of audiovisual content are creating new market conditions for audiovisual media services across the eu. today, we can already see that, in addition to traditional television broadcasts, audiovisual content is also offered via the internet or mobile communications. although the audiovisual media services directive has been implemented differently in the member states and has been published with considerable delay, i supported the report as it not only contains a qualitative assessment of all the provisions but also presents challenges for the future which are linked to the dynamic progress in media services. i expect that, in the light of the expansion of technological possibilities and the growing importance of new forms of audiovisual media services, the commission will review the existing directives and, in its next report, focus on the issue of digital disparities. i expect more action from the member states in relation to disabled people, who should be given greater access to cultural events in accessible formats.

transporting pets is now a part of the daily lives of our citizens. people who care for companion animals commonly travel with them to visit friends or to vacation around the world. however, the prevalence of animal-borne diseases varies from region to region and therefore care should be taken to protect these animals from infection and spread of the disease. experience with the application of directive 998/2003 has confirmed to us the importance of good rules governing the migration of animals. the new legislation follows on from this directive and the experience of its application forms the basis for the legislation under discussion on the rules for the movement of pet animals. the amendments are aimed at clarifying the regulation, more practically distinguishing between commercial and non-commercial movements of animals, and at clarifying the structure of identification documents. we know that the new legislation will deliver and that it will help to bring about the changes that were expected.
in writing. − regulation (ec) no 450/2008 of the european parliament and of the council of 23 april 2008 establishing the community customs code (modernised customs code) entered into force on 24 june 2008, but in accordance with article 188 (2) thereof it applies after the date of application of its implementing provisions and at the latest on 24 june 2013. regulation (ec) no 450/2008 is intended to replace council regulation (eec) no 2913/92 of 12 october 1992 establishing the community customs code. on 20 february 2012, the commission presented to the european parliament and the council a proposal for a regulation establishing the union customs code, in the form of a recast of regulation (ec) no 450/2008, with a view to replacing it before the final date of its application. however, the ordinary legislative procedure cannot be completed in time for the adoption of that proposed regulation and its entry into force before the deadline of 24 june 2013. in order to avoid serious difficulties with union customs rules and to allow the legislature adequate time to complete the process of adopting the union customs code, the final date of application of regulation (ec) no 450/2008, as provided for in the second subparagraph of article 188 (2) of that regulation, should be postponed. the new date of application deemed appropriate for this purpose is 1 november 2013.
in writing. − since 1971, the european union has granted non-reciprocal trade preferences to developing countries, whereby exporters from these countries pay lower duties on some or all goods sold to the eu. they thus gain important access to the eu market, which contributes to the growth of their economy. this system is known as the generalised system of preferences (gsp). in 1997, the union of myanmar was temporarily withdrawn from gsp tariff preferences by council regulation (ec) no 552/97 in view of the common and widespread practice of forced labour, as confirmed by the commission of inquiry of the international labour organisation (ilo) in a special procedure. however, regulation no 552/97 also states that that temporary withdrawal of access will be lifted when the commission submits a report containing evidence that the procedures which led to that withdrawal have been eliminated. since 2011, the union of myanmar has made significant efforts to increase openness and reform, including in the area of forced labour. the european commission has concluded that the infringement can no longer be considered 'serious and systematic' and that the tariff preferences under the current gsp regulation should therefore be reintroduced. however, progress in the union of myanmar remains very fragile. i therefore consider it important to make the necessary efforts so that the proposed measures contribute to the creation of sustainable peace and positive development.
in writing. − i consider the gsp to be an effective instrument to help safeguard fundamental human and labour rights, reduce poverty and promote sustainable development in developing countries. i supported the report because, as the european commission notes, the reasons for the breach of the principles laid down in ilo convention no 29 have passed and are no longer considered to be 'serious and systematic'. i welcomed the fact that the relevant ilo monitoring bodies recognised the progress made in myanmar/burma, which has created scope for re-establishing access to the gsp and that the continued maintenance of the current measures would no longer be beneficial. i also regard the lifting of the restrictions as positive because the gsp can become a key instrument for this country to integrate into world trade, which can ultimately contribute to its economic development and growth. as forced labour in the union of myanmar has not yet been fully eliminated, i expect the commission to continue to monitor developments in myanmar/burma and, in the event of any shortcomings, to return to the withdrawal of access to customs preferences.
in writing. − if you have with the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon, the union acquired exclusive competence to conclude international agreements on investment protection. investment protection agreements generally include an investor-state dispute settlement mechanism allowing a third-country investor to assert a claim against the state in which he has made an investment. the settlement of disputes between the investor and the state may lead to judgments awarding monetary compensation. in addition, any such case will inevitably incur significant costs for the conduct of the arbitration proceedings as well as the costs associated with defence in the case. where the union has international liability for the treatment provided, it is expected under international law to pay any amount awarded in adverse judgments and to pay the costs of any litigation. however, where appropriate, a negative ruling may result either from the treatment granted by the union itself or from the treatment granted by a member state. i consider it justified that, in accordance with union law and without prejudice to the international liability of the union, the financial responsibility should be shared between the union and the member state responsible for the treatment provided.
in writing. − while negotiations to resolve the financial liability associated with investor-state dispute settlement tribunals are not at all straightforward, i support the report because i believe that the provisions of the regulation submitted by the commission clearly define the scope, the concepts and, in particular, the financial liability arising from a dispute under the agreement. while it is possible to assume that some discrepancies in the allocation of financial responsibility between the union and the member states will continue to exist, it is essential that alternative solutions are found in the event of dispute settlement that ensure financial compensation for the investor irrespective of the decision on the allocation of financial responsibility. i agree that in order to ensure uniform conditions for the implementation of the proposed regulation, implementing powers should be conferred on the commission, which could also improve the communication between the member states and the commission itself. i am convinced that if the commission conducts much more intensive discussions with the member states, in many cases not only a simplified procedure can be achieved, but in particular an agreement on the allocation of financial responsibility can be reached.
in writing. − the movement of pet animals has been regulated since 2003 by regulation (ec) no 998/2003 and 17 subsequent amendments. over the other period, the environment for the movement of pet animals has changed: the commission and the member states have, inter alia, carried out anti-rabies campaigns, which have allowed rabies to be considered to be overcome in several parts of the union, although there is a need for constant vigilance. rabies or its absence was the main, but not the only, reason for maintaining the special transitional arrangements for the movement of animals within the territory of certain member states (articles 6, 8 and 16 of regulation no 998/2003). the expiry of the additional transitional arrangements under article 4 (1) (tattooing or transponder marking) was another appropriate reason for the revision of the existing regulation no 998/2003. the primary intention is to make it easier for pet owners to travel within the union or to third countries, while maintaining a high level of safety in terms of possible health risks to the public or animals. in order to make the commission's proposal clearer, the wording and the order of some articles have been changed. however, the substance of the provision in question is preserved.
in writing. − moving pets always carries a risk of abuse and transporting animals for resale is often disguised as travelling with your pet. the average person owns no more than three animals, so limiting the number of animals per passenger to five seems reasonable and objective. on the other hand, if a person is travelling with a number of animals exceeding that number, he should be able to prove that the transport is not of a commercial nature. in any event, i am of the opinion that even in exceptional situations, such as travelling with a larger number of animals for exhibition purposes, the number of animals per person must be unconditionally limited, since each animal transported additionally imposes an increased burden on the owner and reduces the chances of the animal being properly cared for. last but not least, the safety and comfort of other passengers is also at stake.
in writing. − three categories of changes are proposed, most of them being of a technical nature. first, it is a question of replacing references to regulation (ec) no 998/2003 by references to a new regulation which is being negotiated in parallel with the proposal. secondly, in article 10, in comparison with the previous wording, it is proposed to include a reference to regulation (ec) no 1/2005 on the protection of animals during transport and related operations and amending directives 64/432/eec and 93/119/ec and regulation (ec) no 1255/97, which also applies to dogs, cats and ferrets. thirdly, and as regards the content, the only relevant amendment concerns the time limit within which animals must be subjected to a clinical examination before their movement by one of the veterinarians authorised by the competent authority to confirm that the animals are fit for the intended transport. the proposal is based on the recommendation of the world organisation for animal health and consists in extending this period from the current 24 hours to 48 hours. for practical reasons, as well as in the light of the signals received from the industry, it is appropriate to agree to the proposed amendments.
in writing. - first of all, i would like to thank the rapporteur for the report and the legislative amendments proposed by the commission. i am in favour of taking all the measures that are ultimately necessary not only to achieve the single market but whose main objective is to simplify the rules. the extension of the deadline from 24 hours to two days is a good example of how the european union can make life easier for citizens, as travelling with a pet and obtaining the necessary documents can be a very stressful affair. the overall improvement of the situation is not possible without certain partial steps and although the proposed changes may seem to be of only marginal importance, in fact they are another important step in the process of european integration.
in writing. − the commission's vision for a broad and genuine economic and monetary union, adopted on 28 november 2012, included proposals for short-, medium- and long-term measures to strengthen cooperation and integration in the financial, fiscal, economic and political fields. the measures included 'contractual arrangements' in combination with a solidarity mechanism to support national structural reforms aimed at competitiveness and growth. if these reforms were not implemented, their effects would extend to other member states. however, they would have to be implemented by the member state concerned, and in particular with considerable difficulty. the aim is to help member states experiencing difficulties that may affect the euro area as a whole to adopt the necessary reforms, through a convergence and competitiveness instrument, which is a combination of contractual arrangements and a financial support mechanism, sooner than they would be able to do so without this assistance. on the basis of the commission's concept and the report of the three presidents and the president of the ecb on a genuine economic and monetary union, the european council agreed on a roadmap for completing emu at its meeting in december 2012. until the european council in june 2013, work will continue in the following areas: coordination of national reforms, the social dimension of emu, including social dialogue, feasibility and operation of mutually agreed treaties and the solidarity mechanism.

in writing. − the eu and the us are the two main global traders and investors, together producing almost half of the world's gdp and accounting for a third of world trade. the union and the united states of america markets are closely interlinked the volume of trade in goods and services between them reaches almost eur 2 billion on average each day, supporting millions of jobs in both economies. eu-us investment is a real driver of transatlantic relations, with a total value of bilateral investment of over eur 2,394 billion in 2011. the eu and the us share common values and have comparable legal systems and high, albeit different, standards of labour, consumer and environmental protection. the eu believes that developing and strengthening the multilateral system is a key objective. this does not mean, however, that bilateral agreements cannot go beyond wto commitments and complement multilateral rules, as both regional agreements and free trade agreements lead to increased harmonisation of standards and wider liberalisation, which is beneficial to the multilateral trading system.

in writing. - the tragedy in bangladesh has highlighted an often-overlooked reality that we in the western world often tend to turn a blind eye to. sadly, western companies exploit the misery and poor living conditions of the people. unfortunately, public international law does not allow for liability for such conduct, as multinational corporations are not subject to it. moreover, multinationals operate in the third world mainly through subsidiaries, that is, through separate legal entities. consequently, it is legally impossible to derive consequences against the parent company and liability against the subsidiary can only be derived in the state in which it is established. since enforcement is extremely low in these countries, the guilty often go unpunished. sadly, this uncontrolled desire for profit often escapes the control of civil society, which remains blind to the problems of others. one solution i see is to boycott the products of those companies that profit from human misery, and i believe that spreading revenge is one of the european parliament's main tasks. for these reasons, i am fully in favour of parliament adopting a specific resolution on this problem.

in writing. − in a genuine european area of justice, individuals and businesses should not be deterred from exercising their rights by the complexity of legal and administrative systems. all citizens should have the same easy access to the courts and authorities of any member state as in their own country. in civil and commercial matters, access to justice should not be impeded by the costs associated with the cross-border nature of the dispute. as early as 1999, the european council called on the council and the commission to establish minimum standards ensuring an adequate level of legal aid in crossborder civil disputes throughout the union. on the basis of a commission proposal, the council adopted a directive on improving access to justice in cross-border disputes by establishing minimum common rules on legal aid in such disputes. this directive has entered into force on 30 november 2004. i am pleased that according to the commission's other findings all member states are generally applying this directive successfully.
in writing. − council directive 2003/8/ec on improving access to justice in crossborder disputes by establishing minimum common rules on legal aid in such disputes is a very important piece of legislation for european citizens, as it aims to ensure that the most deprived sections of society have access to justice in other member states, for example when exercising the right to free movement or benefiting from the internal market. this directive concerns only civil and commercial matters and does not cover disputes in the field of criminal or public law. the main problem with this directive remains that not much is known about it. according to the commission's findings, only 12% of citizens are aware that crossborder legal aid exists. if citizens are not aware of the possibility of requesting cross-border legal aid, they are unlikely to exercise this right. therefore, in this situation, i consider it necessary to take measures to ensure greater awareness of cross-border legal aid, not only among lay people, but especially among lawyers.
in writing. − even before the adoption of the directive, the provision of legal aid in crossborder civil matters was guaranteed only in some member states. i am very pleased that, after a certain period of time, we can say that, in general, all the member states have accepted the directive. what is less impressive is that not all member states apply this directive or apply it only in individual provisions. although the main responsibility for the correct transposition and application of the directive remains with the member states, i welcome the report presented, as i believe it comes with measures that can help to address the identified shortcomings in the area of legal aid in cross-border civil and commercial disputes. however, i consider the most serious aspect of this report to be the lack of awareness in the area of crossborder legal aid, where only 12% of citizens know that this form of aid exists. i expect that we will also make use of the european year of citizens in implementing this directive, which can support the process of removing further obstacles and solutions that stand in the way of citizens enjoying their rights fully in cross-border civil and commercial disputes.

in writing. − the aim of the rapporteur, ms delli, is to show the extent to which social housing can provide the union with the impetus to overcome the economic, social and environmental crisis. it is estimated that 25 million european citizens live in social housing. all member states except greece have social housing, the extent of which varies considerably from one country to another; the difference is mainly between the western and eastern member states. the provision of social housing is one of the ways in which public authorities can respond to housing market failures in order to ensure universal access to decent housing at an adequate price. member states shall organise the provision of social housing parallel to the unplanned market supply offered under specific access conditions and at a fixed rent, by both non-profit-making entities specifically created for this purpose and private investors. despite these mechanisms, many eu citizens no longer have access to decent housing for financial reasons. in 2010, 5.7% of europeans had housing problems, 17.86% of residents lived in overcrowded or unsuitable apartments and 10.10% of households reported that housing costs exceeded 40% of their income. i therefore consider it crucial that social housing investments are given greater weight in the union's macroeconomic and budgetary surveillance system.
