in writing. − it can be assumed that in the coming period europe will face a significant task in ensuring an increasingly open and accessible labour market. access to information on cross-border mobility is still limited and very often many people are discouraged by its low quality. i consider it justified and important to ensure that the range of individual training options meets the requirement to ensure the employability and adaptability of workers throughout their working lives, thereby increasing their capacity for professional mobility. all citizens have the right to an adequate level of education, to supplement their knowledge and to acquire new skills during their working life. education and training systems should be or continue to be adapted to the needs of the labour market, the economy and society. lastly, a broad and positive impact on growth can only be achieved by stimulating and supporting investment in women's human capital and productivity.
in writing. − the overall unemployment rate for women in the european union is 10.7% and for young women 22.7%. employment mobility is one of the factors contributing to employment growth and therefore greater emphasis should be placed on its information. women are paid on average 16% less than men. this wage gap should be closed as soon as possible. women are disadvantaged in the labour market in several ways. not just in terms of wages, but also in terms of mobility. the conditions for achieving a balance between family life and work also influence their mobility. they receive lower wages for time spent caring for children, caring for needy family members, less pension due to periods of unemployment; there is a risk of impoverishment, their social rights are not guaranteed. many women work as nurses in other member states (including slovakia), which makes it possible to financially support families. their families are characterized by a decline in the amount of time they spend together. the children and family members feel the effects of this. family life and career are difficult to reconcile in this case. the conditions listed need to be balanced in order to make mobility in employment an incentive for women. that's why i supported the report.
quality, accessible and integrated transport infrastructure, environmentally and energy-efficient and safe transport are very important for the internal market and for the living standards of all citizens of the european union. despite considerable technical progress and cost-effective improvements, the transport system has not changed significantly in recent times. this is also reflected in the report which states that the current system of the european electronic toll service introduced by the commission has not produced the desired results and needs to be revised. although the introduction of an electronic toll is not a simple matter, i am convinced that the uniform application of toll payments to all vehicle types is the right step and a necessary step for the future. i expect the commission to make a detailed assessment and, if necessary, to submit these measures to the european parliament. i also expect a more significant shift in mobile phone payments for toll collection and stamp purchases, and from the member states a simpler system for stamp payments.
in writing. − if you have this directive aims to achieve interoperability of electronic toll systems in the european union. member states shall keep national electronic registers indicating the toll network, toll chargers and toll service providers which they consider eligible for registration and shall make those registers available to the public by electronic means. in addition, they shall establish a conciliation body responsible for facilitating contractual arrangements between toll chargers and providers of the european electronic toll service (eets). toll chargers must set up their electronic tolling systems in accordance with the technical standards laid down in the legislation and make their contractual terms publicly available. i am convinced that an efficient internal market is a prerequisite for economic growth and prosperity and allows the smooth, rapid and safe movement of goods and people within the union. it requires a well-developed, maintained and efficiently managed infrastructure.
in 2012, some 330 000 asylum applications were registered in the european union. and since the right to asylum is a fundamental right and the european union is a community of values, which includes in particular the respect and protection of fundamental rights, every democratic state must recognise and respect the right to asylum. i am therefore convinced that a common european asylum system is absolutely necessary. we need rules that are fast, fair and effective. the conditions of admission and the rules of procedure must be clear and unambiguous. we need to have minimum standards that all member states must adhere to. it is the commission's task to monitor this. the level of treatment of asylum seekers in some countries is truly unacceptable. these people have rights, too. conditions throughout the union must be comparable, proportionate, clear and simple. we must protect the values on which we built the european union. there are those who seek refuge from persecution or, for example, from war. those entrusted with our protection should have it. but at the same time, we have to be careful and we have to prevent our asylum system from being abused in the area of crime.
our citizens have given us a mandate to address first and foremost their daily problems, such as lack of employment opportunities, high cost of living or insecurity of existence. in my country, 14% of the working age population and 26% of young people who have finished school are unemployed. however, we do try to provide the necessary assistance to vulnerable foreigners seeking protection, where justified. but my citizens would not accept a decision from brussels about who and under what conditions our country should accept. indeed, in a decent society, the granting of aid is a voluntary, sovereign and autonomous decision of the aid provider. it cannot therefore be enforced by a decision of any brussels authority. i am therefore convinced that decisions on asylum policy must be taken as closely as possible to the people who provide assistance, that is, at the level of the assisting state.
the creation of the schengen area is one of the european union's greatest achievements. according to the survey, 62% of our citizens consider schengen to be the most positive outcome of european integration. free movement is a fundamental freedom of the european union and we must respect it. it is therefore necessary to strike an appropriate balance between the right to free movement and the right to security that each member state should guarantee to its citizens. last year saw events that seriously threatened the guarantees of free movement and freedom of movement. however, all member states are obliged to manage their borders in such a way as not to interfere with the free movement of persons within the schengen area. the reintroduction of border controls should be allowed only in genuinely exceptional circumstances. each measure relating to the reintroduction of internal border controls must be carefully considered, proportionate and implemented only as a genuine last resort. however, such a decision cannot in any event be an individual decision of one member state. the european union as a whole is the only competent authority to decide on it. the european parliament may in no case be excluded from this process.
the schengen documents are one of the most important elements of the eu acquis, both from a political and a civic perspective. this is why the european system that has been achieved and worked out so far must be maintained and further refined. i think parliament's position is an attempt to preserve the principles of mutual trust and cooperation in the schengen package. however, the idea of making internal border controls more regular is an obstacle to european cooperation and coexistence. we do not have to go far back in time, but many of us still have the experience of constant checks on border crossers. internal border controls should continue to be carried out only in exceptional and justified cases. this procedure cannot become routine. immigration and migration are natural processes, the consequences of economic and global change. so, these are not questions that can be answered by another iron curtain. member states must achieve effective problem solving through a different, strengthened eu tool. the free movement of persons is one of the fundamental principles on which our community is built, and it is unique in the world. this needs to be further improved and rights consolidated, not a step backwards. schengen connects many regions, many peoples, but at the same time, the consolidation of external borders has pushed some countries further away from the eu that could be part of the european bloodstream. in addition to developing a solid internal system based on trust, appropriate guarantees should also be provided for cooperation with non-schengen countries. the main task of parliament in this process, in my view, is to strengthen europeanism, transparency and the sense of freedom of eu citizens, while guaranteeing security.
the report highlights the application of the european competition policy based on three basic instruments, i.e. antitrust rules, regulated state aid and merger control. with experience of the real functioning of economic life in my country, i would like to draw attention to the tangible phenomenon of replacing economic competition in some sectors. the coordination of price policies between a small number of decisive players in some sectors reminds me of the practice of cartels. for example, bank charges in my country are several times higher than in most eu countries, even though all the banks operating in our country are subsidiaries of the largest banking houses in the eu and have no reasonable reason to charge higher fees. however, they failed to prove the cartel agreement. a similar situation can be seen with mobile operators, whose prices we have managed to bring down significantly only through legislative measures and without the intervention of the state and the union, they would clearly not have been reduced by competition.
in writing. if we are to remove barriers to better access for smes to the internal market, we need an active competition policy. without it, the european social market economy is unthinkable. competition allows for price formation, efficient allocation and use of resources and social progress. in the context of globalisation, european businesses and the economy cannot survive without fair competition. the commission must therefore assess distortions of competition and their economic impact in cooperation with the national authorities. in the banking sector, the market share of some large financial institutions increased. the aim must be to strengthen competition in european banking markets. here, the antitrust rules need to be tightened. eu competition authorities must monitor markets for pharmaceutical, health and insurance services. in doing so, it is necessary to reveal abuses of patients' rights and discriminatory behaviour. while the organisation of the health and social care sector is primarily a member state competence, these services should be subject to controls to protect public finances and preserve competition law and the rights of eu citizens. the commission must take into account the employment objectives set out in the europe 2020 strategy. competition policy should allow better support for those smes which contribute most to job creation.
in writing. the topics of the forthcoming summit include increasing competitiveness, growth and jobs within the eu. but the unemployment rate in the eu countries was still 11% in may 2013! the youth unemployment rate exceeded, for example, the rate of the eu average in 2011. in greece and spain, the limit is 55%. within the eu, it has already risen to 21%, or 5.5 million people! the anti-crisis measures are ineffective! austerity and misdirected social investment have a negative impact especially on those eu citizens who are most affected by the crisis! member states need to set structural reforms more effectively, we need systemic measures and not just short-term solutions that only delay the necessary and ultimately have a negative impact on employment. we need to invest in a targeted way and strengthen the financing of the economy, we need to be decisive in taking measures for growth. it is therefore essential that member states continue to implement reforms and further strengthen social investment in order to create an effective social security system that should be a given in modern europe. the governments of the member states should focus on supporting small and medium-sized enterprises, which are the most affected by the economic and social crisis. we must prevent the growing social unrest that is the result of ineffective and often ineffective measures by the right-wing governments of the member states, but also by the eu institutions.
in writing. − mr mimicu's main priorities should be the interests of european consumers in the wider political and economic context. it should place particular emphasis on a group of consumers affected by the current economic situation. it is very important to emphasise the achievement of the objectives of the european consumer agenda. food safety should also be emphasised. consumer policy is a cross-cutting policy. we need to provide better targeted information to consumers and ensure the enforcement of the far-reaching consumer acquis already adopted within the eu. this should be the main priority of mr mimicu's mandate.
in writing. − mr mates' areas of professional interest include fiscal policy, budgetary management, macroeconomic adjustment policy, monetary policy issues, as well as central banking, including issues of budgeting oriented to results and the efficient use of government expenditure. mr mates' professional competence is undeniable, but it is important that the main aspect, namely the complete independence of the member of the court of auditors, be preserved. the court of auditors shall assist the european parliament in the exercise of its powers of control over the implementation of the budget. all members of the court must be aware of this role and must do their utmost to cooperate with the european parliament.
in writing. − the committee on budgetary control has carefully assessed mr pufan's qualifications in accordance with the conditions laid down in article 286 (1) of the treaty on the functioning of the european union. the candidate was duly heard on 27 may 2013. again, the candidate's independence must be emphasised in particular, unconditionally and in all circumstances.
in writing. − illegal fishing is carried out without regard for environmental, social and other standards. fish caught in this way are illegal. the fight against illegal fishing is not easy. the commission presented the first draft regulation back in 2007. illegal fishing is extremely damaging to our oceans. it must be effectively combated. the commission must continue this process. in the context of aligning regulation (ec) no 1005/2008 with the new rules of the tfeu, the commission has prepared a proposal to split the powers currently conferred on the commission by that regulation between delegated and implementing measures. in general, the proposed amendments concern only the types of acts to be adopted and do not change the content of the measures.
in writing. − in 2012, some 330 000 asylum applications were registered in the eu. the right of asylum is provided for in article 18 of the charter of fundamental rights of the european union, in accordance with the geneva convention of 28 july 1951 and the protocol of 31 january 1967 relating to the status of refugees. the right to asylum is therefore a fundamental right. the european union is a community of values, among which respect for and protection of fundamental rights is of paramount importance. every democratic state must recognise and respect the right to asylum. we must have minimum standards that all member states must respect.
in writing. − this report is part of the so-called asylum package. in particular, the regulation aims to increase the effectiveness of the dublin system and to provide for higher standards of protection for those persons who belong to that system. the proposal contributes to improving overall case resolution, in particular with regard to individual asylum systems. it shall emphasise early warning, preparedness and a crisis management mechanism. it is necessary to provide legal certainty, to ensure the right to information and to enhance the protection of particularly vulnerable persons, such as unaccompanied minors.
in writing. - the report is part of the asylum package again. the directive aims to eliminate the shortcomings of the procedure for granting and withdrawing international protection. the aim is to ensure a higher, harmonised level of protection. the revised version introduces a new institution of the so-called personal interview, improves access to information and provides greater legal certainty. it also provides for clearer rules, the identification of vulnerable persons and their specific needs, and clearer rules on procedural time limits.
in writing. − in 2011, 120 million europeans were at risk of poverty or social exclusion, an increase of six million in two years, and now it is almost a quarter of the total population. more than 40 million people suffer from severe material deprivation. one in ten people under the age of 60 lives in a household with a very low work intensity. another problem is homelessness. according to one estimate, a total of 4,1 million homeless people lived in the union in 2009/2010. in 2011, more than 25 million children in the union were at risk of poverty and social exclusion. in 2011, the number of people at risk of poverty and social exclusion returned to the level of 2008 and most member states are making no progress towards meeting their national 2020 targets for combating poverty and social exclusion. the fund for european aid to the most deprived could help to improve the situation.
in writing. - in the last five years, we have talked more about poverty than in any other decade. this fact came as a shock to us, for surely none of us expected that such a change of circumstances could occur in a prosperous europe. i'm glad we didn't just stop at the words. the idea of creating a fund for european aid to the most deprived (fead) is a sign that we are able to actively face adverse conditions. i am of the opinion that fead membership should not be an obligation of a member state but a voluntary decision. the main argument for voluntariness is that resources are distributed only among those member states which consider assistance from the fund to be necessary. this will avoid inefficient use of funds that are not available in the fund. i appreciate the proposed broad scope of the fead, as it will allow member states to use the funds to address their own problems and alleviate poverty in ways that the conditions require.
in writing. − the commission has proposed a regulation establishing for the period 2014-2020 a new instrument to complement existing cohesion instruments, in particular the european social fund, by using it to tackle the worst and most socially devastating forms of poverty, food deprivation, as well as homelessness and material deprivation of children, while supporting accompanying measures aimed at the social reintegration of the union's most marginalised people. in the context of the europe 2020 strategy, the european union has set itself the target of reducing by 2020 the number of people at risk of poverty or social exclusion by at least 20 million. however, the economic and financial crisis is deepening poverty and social exclusion across the union. in 2011, 120 million europeans were at risk of poverty or social exclusion, an increase of six million in two years, and now almost a quarter of the total population. more than 40 million people suffer from severe material deprivation. one in ten people under the age of 60 lives in a household with a very low work intensity. although the fund has certain limitations, i am convinced that it can make a significant contribution to improving the living conditions of marginalised people, especially the homeless and children and households with children affected by material deprivation, and to helping them live in dignity.
in writing. − in the european union, there is a dramatic increase in the number of people living at risk of poverty or social exclusion. today, this figure is around 116 million, or 24.2% of the european population. as the mep for slovakia, i would like to point out that there is a steady increase in the number of people at risk of poverty in slovakia. there are now about 700,000 of them in our state, or 13 percent of the population. this is an increase of about 50 thousand people compared to 2010. about one in eight slovaks is now living in poverty. the slovak republic is aware, as is the eu, that unless the situation is tackled more rapidly and radically, we are facing a social explosion. although the economic and financial crisis has reduced the possibility of supporting people at risk of poverty and social exclusion in slovakia, slovakia has committed to reducing the number of poor by 170 000 by 2020. i am aware that the purpose of the proposed fund is not to solve poverty and to consider it as a replacement for comprehensive policies, but i welcome this fund as an important eu instrument that can make a significant contribution to member states in improving the living conditions of people living on the margins of society.
in writing. − this is another report in the package on a common european asylum system. eurodac is an information technology system containing fingerprints and personal data of asylum seekers. it was created to facilitate the application of the dublin system. the aim of the regulation is to lay down precisely defined and harmonised rules concerning the retention, comparison and deletion of fingerprints. at the same time, it is necessary to provide for the protection and security of such sensitive personal data. eurodac also serves the purposes of preventing, detecting and investigating terrorist offences and other serious crimes, as organised crime networks from third countries seek to exploit the asylum system and try to bring offenders from one network into an eu member state as contact persons for criminal activity.
in writing. − the commission has presented a proposal for a council decision on the possibility for member states' law enforcement authorities and europol to request comparison with data in eurodac for law enforcement purposes, specifying the precise means of such access. the european parliament did not adopt a legislative resolution on the september 2009 proposals. the committee on civil liberties, justice and home affairs gave its provisional approval to the commission's proposal. the proposal therefore revises the 2010 draft regulation and replaces it with a new wording to take better account of the european parliament's resolution as well as the outcome of the council's negotiations. i considered the integration of law enforcement access into eurodac to be a necessary part of a balanced agreement in the negotiations on the package of the common european asylum system with a view to finalising its preparation by the end of 2012.
in writing. − free movement can be counted among the fundamental values of the european union, and the ability to move freely within the union without the need for internal border controls is one of its greatest achievements. after lengthy negotiations, the commission, parliament and council have reached agreement on new rules to improve the functioning of the schengen area. under the new agreement, frontex will periodically carry out an objective analysis assessing the risks and then consider what sanctions to apply. in the event of serious deficiencies, the commission will be able to propose, as a last resort, the reintroduction of border controls for a certain period. i am convinced that all the measures taken in this area will ensure that the schengen area, as one of the eu's most important achievements, is even better protected and managed.

'we have gone further by abolishing borders, following in the footsteps of the fathers of the union.' fifty years ago, that idea would have been a utopia, but today it's the reality we live in, and we have to make sure that it's preserved. although i am in favour of free movement without controls, i am aware that situations may arise in which the safety of the population is threatened. therefore, i agree with the proposal to re-establish internal borders as a temporary measure of last resort. in order to avoid any abuse of this measure, i agree with the proposal that the commission should report annually to parliament and the council on the functioning of the schengen area. i also agree with the rapporteur that parliament should adopt the commission's guidelines on the governance of the schengen area, as they will help to unify the interpretation and consolidate the rules on which the schengen area will continue to operate.

for the efd group. since 1975, we have been gradually improving and extending the contractual relations formally established between the european union and the acp countries under the lomé convention through the revision mechanisms of the acp-ec partnership agreement signed in cotonou in 2000. the latest revision of the agreement, in march 2011, brings a number of positive changes, including a joint effort to achieve the millennium development goals in the areas of poverty reduction, food security, health, climate change and sustainable development. the emphasis on strengthening the role of local authorities and national parliaments also raises hopes for more democratic and transparent governance in these countries. however, several important themes in this revision of the agreement are not included in its content. we know that in the developing world, illicit financial flows are a big problem, amounting to eight times the amount of official development assistance. if these illicit flows were properly taxed through good and transparent governance, countries would gain significant resources to implement the necessary social and health programmes. we should therefore not leave out of the agreement the issue of sound tax administration in relation to development aid opportunities. this area also includes the issue of fair trade and transparent financial flows, which should also be present in the revised version. a particular issue that we will have to seriously address in cooperation with our acp partners is the issue of mechanisms for the readmission of migrants in their countries of origin, which we do not have sufficiently regulated. i understand that we can no longer enter into the negotiated text of the revision of the agreement today. however, i would welcome it if the commission did not forget these areas in the forthcoming revision of the agreement.

rapporteur. − mr president, i will be very brief, since this report on the authorisation to accede to the 1997 protocol of the vienna convention has not been debated in the plenary, and i would like to give you some brief information about the subject matter and the aim of this report. the proposal enables the contracting parties of the vienna convention on civil liability for nuclear damage to ratify the protocol or to accede to it. the council’s decision is addressed to the eu member states that are contracting parties to the vienna convention but who have not ratified or concluded its 1997 protocols so far. these countries are bulgaria, the czech republic, estonia, hungary, lithuania, poland and slovakia. the amendment to the vienna convention is an update of the rules to strengthen the right to fair compensation for damage in the event of nuclear accidents. accession to the 1997 protocol is therefore beneficial for improving victim compensation across the european union. the council decision proposes to authorise the conclusion or ratification of the 1997 protocol for the council member states. in accordance with the treaties of the eu, the council decision requires the consent of the parliament. as your rapporteur, i do recommend that parliament gives it consent to the council decision in order to allow the contracting parties to conclude the 1997 protocol.
in writing. − population growth, large-scale increases in food and energy demands and the scarcity of natural resources pose new challenges for the union. the balance between production and consumption must be managed in an efficient and sustainable manner. the bioeconomy offers a good opportunity to meet these challenges. it also contributes to supporting rural development, reducing greenhouse gas emissions and making the production cycle more sustainable. the commission communication on the european bioeconomy and the action plan to bring the bioeconomy strategy to life outlined in the communication contain three components: promoting research and innovation, creating greater synergies between different policies and strengthening markets and competition. develop and support coherent research and innovation programmes, provide financing for industrial investments and make financial instruments available. public-private partnerships dedicated to the bio-based industry, support for new projects, development and marketing of new products should be encouraged. bioeconomy strategies should also promote more efficient use of household and municipal waste. the use of by-products and residues from agriculture and forestry shall be addressed. the adoption of better legislation is essential to the effective use of the latter, which is why i voted in favour of the report.
written − international nuclear liability is governed by two instruments: the vienna convention and the paris convention on third party liability in the field of nuclear energy. it appears justified to give priority to union legislation over the legislation of the member states which ratified the 1997 protocol before joining the european union, i.e. latvia and romania, and the member states which are parties to the paris convention. it is recommended that the contracting parties to the vienna protocol, namely bulgaria, the czech republic, estonia, hungary, lithuania, poland and slovakia, ratify or conclude the 1997 protocol.

in writing − the maritime labour convention (mlc) was adopted by the international labour organisation (ilo) on 23 february 2006. it is intended to replace the 37 existing ilo maritime conventions and related recommendations adopted since 1920, and will be the first comprehensive maritime labour code applicable to over 1.2 million seafarers worldwide. after some tense negotiations, the parties finally reached an agreement. the convention should enter into force in august 2013. among other things, one of its paragraphs states that the measures taken to implement this directive must not lead to a reduction in the general level of protection of seafarers in the context of social legislation within the union.

in writing − if you have the aim of the proposal is to promote and enforce the rules on the inspection of the technical condition of motor vehicles in order to enhance road safety and environmental protection. the proposal also improves the application of the roadworthiness test, in particular in cases where the technical condition of a vehicle poses an immediate threat to road safety. measures to this end include, for example, temporary withdrawal or permanent cancellation of the registration of a vehicle. the proposal submitted at the same time requires member states, when issuing a new registration certificate, to mutually recognise the validity of the roadworthiness certificate if a vehicle is re-registered in another member state or if there has been a change of ownership of the vehicle and a new registration is necessary. the aim should also be to comply with the regulations and to reduce the administrative burden.
in writing. − member states will be required to keep data on all vehicles registered in their territory in electronic databases. they will facilitate the exchange of information between member states, thereby helping to combat the trade in stolen vehicles and facilitating the verification of the validity of vehicle inspection certificates from other member states. effective exchange of information through electronic databases will help ensure that cars on the roads of the european union comply with the safety requirements. i supported the european parliament's resolution.
in writing. − the inspection of motor vehicles is essential for safe road traffic. more than five people die every day on europe's roads in accidents caused by technical failures. a vehicle may only be sold if it complies with the requirements of the safety, environmental and type-approval regulations. all vehicles with a european type-approval are required to be registered for the first time in the eu. after this approval, vehicles in use on the road shall be subject to periodic roadworthiness tests. means such as the temporary withdrawal of a vehicle's licence or its deletion from the vehicle register can make it more effective to screen out motor vehicles whose technical condition poses a direct risk to road safety. in order to facilitate vehicle identification, we also need to create a european electronic database linked to national databases. not all member states have adequate regulation of measures following the sale of vehicles. we need to ensure that vehicles that are re-registered in another member state are automatically deleted from the original register. i voted in favour of this report to allow the above reforms to be implemented.

as a renewable resource, clean, high-quality water is an indispensable component of the environment and also has an important place in the economic and industrial life of each member state. water policy is gaining new strategic importance in the context of global challenges to access to quality water resources. european union citizens are also increasingly aware of the importance of maintaining water purity in relation to its impact on human health and are expressing legitimate concerns about the state of water in individual member states. it is the eu's responsibility to respond to such concerns and to put in place an adequate monitoring system. the public should be informed in an appropriate and timely manner of the results obtained. water management, however, is based on water conservation. i agree with the gradual reduction of emissions of priority substances and, in particular, with the cessation of emissions of toxic bioaccumulative and persistent substances into the aquatic environment. in my view, it is also appropriate to monitor certain endocrine disrupting substances, so-called endocrine disruptors, which have a negative impact on our health.
written − the water framework directive establishes a list of priority substances that pose a significant risk to the eu's aquatic environment. in order to achieve good chemical status, the environmental quality standards established for these substances must be met. the commission proposal adds 15 new substances to the list, sets environmental quality standards for seven existing priority substances and introduces specific provisions for substances that behave as ubiquitous persistent, bioaccumulative and toxic substances. it is appropriate to consider that the proposed amendments could clarify and make the directive more effective in terms of achieving good surface water status in the eu, while also facilitating the implementation of the directive by the member states.
in writing − despite some improvements in recent years in the area of water quality, the situation regarding priority substances, which form the basis for the assessment of chemical status under the water framework directive, is not satisfactory. i believe that the problems of water pollution are of concern to all of us, which is why i voted in favour of the resolution which, as part of the update, adds 15 chemicals to the list of 33 pollutants to be monitored and controlled in eu surface waters. water pollution is now a global problem, and in many cases it is a major cause of death and disease. the statistics show that 14,000 people die each day as a result of water pollution. in the light of some global phenomena, which are increasingly also occurring in europe, i would like to point out some worrying trends that are related not only to water scarcity and water efficiency, but also to water quality. apart from demographic trends, i consider that exceptional events (such as floods) are a very serious matter, and their number is increasing in an increasing number of eu member states. therefore, we must also increase efforts in the removal and control of chemical pollution in water, which should be directed towards the progressive reduction of priority substances in water.
in writing. − environmental quality standards specify the maximum concentration of a given pollutant or group of pollutants in water and its deposits. it shall not be exceeded in order to ensure the protection of public health and the environment. the list of priority pollutants is valid for the whole eu. it has been expanded to include 12 new hazardous substances. the new legislation also introduces a list of potential pollutants to be monitored. it will also feature three pharmaceuticals for the first time. if regular inspections show that they have a negative impact on the aquatic environment, these substances will be included in the priority list. these are two hormonal products found in contraceptives and one painkiller. the maximum permitted concentrations, which are defined in the framework of environmental quality standards (eqs), will apply to new substances included in the priority list from 2018. to this end, member states will be required to draw up and submit to the commission by 2018 supplementary programmes of measures and monitoring programmes.
in writing − if you have in order to enforce and simplify administration without weakening the commission's control, council regulation (ec) no 994/98 of 7 may 1998 on the application of articles 92 and 93 of the treaty establishing the european community to certain categories of horizontal state aid authorises the commission to declare, by means of regulations, that certain types of state aid are compatible with the common market and are exempt from the notification requirement. the proposal to include certain new categories in the delegated regulation does not foresee an immediate block exemption for all of these categories, nor does it imply that all measures within a given category will constitute a block exemption in their entirety. instead, it allows the commission to adopt block exemptions gradually, when the experience gained will be sufficient to enable the commission to define clear compatibility criteria for certain types of aid measures, while ensuring that the impact on competition and trade between member states is limited.

in many countries, cooperatives are the backbone of the economy and in some are even considered as a new alternative. cooperatives are more resilient than traditional enterprises in times of crisis, which has also been reflected positively in some regions of the european union. the cooperative model has a high capacity to adapt to change, to restructure its production programme in order to survive in the market and, above all, to maintain the trust of the people. i supported the report because it not only highlights the achievements and importance of cooperatives for the european economy, but also makes concrete proposals to be adopted at different levels of government in the context of the conversion of enterprises hit by the crisis. i expect the commission and the member states to review their legislation on cooperatives and adopt measures that will facilitate not only access to the widest possible range of business support services for cooperatives, but also access to financial mechanisms at european union level.
the advantages of cooperatives are particularly evident in the social sphere, as they combine the pursuit of profit with solidarity. the cooperative model has proven itself in the eu over the decades. the evidence is that there are now 160,000 cooperatives owned by 123 million members, employing about 5.5 million people. the contribution of cooperatives to the gdp of the member states is estimated at up to five per cent on average. in the context of the crisis, i would also like to highlight the creation of jobs in the regions in the industrial and service sectors. however, cooperatives that create a suitable working environment for the employment of disabled people deserve special attention. in order to make it easier for cooperatives to find a place in the public interest, whether in social or health matters, we need to think about creating a favourable legal framework. their establishment and operation should bring their benefits to the greatest possible number of citizens of the european union.
in writing − cooperatives, together with other social economy enterprises, play a crucial role in the european economy, especially in times of crisis, because they combine profitability with solidarity, create high-quality jobs, strengthen social, economic and regional cohesion and produce social capital. the report further notes that social economy enterprises should benefit from a clearer and more coherent legislative framework, while taking due account of the rich diversity of social economy institutions and their specific characteristics. it is justified to create services for start-up cooperatives to support the creation of new cooperatives. it is equally important to support initiatives promoting the cooperative model among new potential entrepreneurs at both national and european level.

the common system of a financial transaction tax is one of the effective instruments to combat speculation, but also to overcome the crisis. the tax would be introduced on all financial transactions between financial institutions, at least one of which is established in a member state of the european union. the financial sector, which has so far been under-taxed by the exemption of most financial services from value added tax, simply has to contribute a much fairer share. by exempting financial services from vat, financial institutions will save up to eur 18 billion a year. the eu will spend a staggering €4.6 trillion to rescue the financial sector in times of crisis. the introduction of the system would raise about eur 57 billion per year. this revenue would be shared between the union and the individual member states. moreover, the system would discourage risky and speculative financial operations and complement measures aimed at preventing future crises.

in writing. − collective investment undertakings in transferable securities (ucits) are investment funds which have been set up in accordance with the ucits directive (adopted in 1985). once registered in one eu country, ucits funds can be freely traded throughout the eu. the ucits directive is currently under revision. it should be amended to take account of market developments and the experience gained so far by market participants and supervisors, in particular with a view to eliminating differences between national provisions on the obligations and liability of depositaries, remuneration policies and sanctions. the deficiencies identified can only be addressed through action at european level. therefore, the proposed measures or their objectives can be better achieved at union level as a whole.
in writing. − the eu emissions trading system (eu ets) created the first major global carbon market and set a common eu-wide price for carbon. this market is generally considered to be liquid and based on a well-functioning infrastructure. part of this infrastructure concerns the auctioning of emission allowances, for which implementing powers are conferred on the commission by the directive. the commission has already started to implement them and that regulation has been amended several times. it is not specified how the volumes of greenhouse gas emission allowances to be auctioned are to be allocated over the trading period. for the sake of legal certainty and market predictability, it appears important to clarify that the commission may, in exceptional circumstances, adjust the auction schedule in order to ensure the proper functioning of the market.

on behalf of the ppe group. – madam president, the introduction of tariffs on imports of agricultural products is a clear violation of the letter and the spirit of bilateral agreements. steps taken by norway can be considered protectionist and prohibitive to trade. the decision goes against one of the fundamental principles of the eu, namely the principle of trade liberalisation. norway, as a member of the european economic area, is bound to respect that principle. furthermore, these restrictions were adopted without any previous consultation with the commission. this is unacceptable, since norway is a country with which the eu has very close economic and political relations. it is also incomprehensible that a country that avoided the negative effects of the economic crisis would want to introduce such measures. we in the committee on international trade call on the norwegian government to withdraw the measures and enter into formal negotiations with the commission to resolve the issue. on a personal note, i sincerely hope that such stratospheric tariffs – 300%, 400% and more – will never be seen again in our region, particularly with a close trading partner such as norway.
in any decent civilized society, caring for vulnerable groups is an integral part of social policy. most european union countries have been developing their systems and mechanisms to provide the necessary assistance to the deprived population for a long time. the deteriorating economic situation has already put a greater burden on the social systems of the member states since 2009, as the number of unemployed continues to grow and the poverty of the population continues to increase. we therefore need to react swiftly to this unfavourable trend and look for further new ways to help the deprived groups to secure at least the basic necessities for a life of dignity. one of the basic needs of every human is access to daily food. and i think that it is precisely in the area of food policy that we have reserves in the union which we could effectively mobilise in these difficult times to improve aid to the deprived groups. european farmers are able to produce enough food to feed the entire population of the union. yet, our fellow citizens often do not have enough money to buy the necessary food. however, the european commission provides subsidies to farmers to keep the land and not generate surplus food. perhaps if, instead of these subsidies, we could buy back such surplus food from farmers and give it away at token prices to charitable and social institutions or health facilities, we could create a mechanism that would eliminate the threat of malnutrition or hunger to the population.
the report by jean lambert draws attention to the problems of vulnerable groups struggling with the consequences of the crisis with the usual thoroughness and common sense. the results of eurofund research show that the crisis has made the poor poorer, and there is no doubt that children are the most affected and vulnerable group. child poverty has serious consequences, especially in the early stages. malnutrition, lack of adequate health care - for example, lack of vaccinations - can cause developmental disorders that are much more burdensome for society to treat or correct. long-forgotten diseases, such as tuberculosis, are reappearing because vaccines are often not free or require expensive drugs to cure. in kindergarten, for example, every year of kindergarten education improves a child's chances of understanding what they read by 10 percent later on, and without that, of course, we can't talk about lifelong learning. access to basic services should not be jeopardised by restrictive measures to such an extent that they impose a multiple burden on public expenditure at a later stage. again, prevention is the cheapest solution, and it is true that the european union cannot solve these problems, but by making good use of the european social fund we can do a lot to alleviate them.
social inequalities in europe's regions are constantly growing and the situation among the most vulnerable groups of the union's population is deteriorating day by day. through pointless cuts and austerity measures, we have made the poor poorer, the vulnerable more vulnerable, and many european citizens lack access to basic health care or social services. low or no income means that people do not have access to even basic services, such as heating. this has extremely negative consequences for vulnerable groups such as the elderly or the sick. the european union's response to the crisis must therefore have a social dimension. government cuts and austerity measures have long and significantly worsened the quality of life of the citizens of the european union. so i ask you, what specific, effective measures have we recently taken that have actually improved the situation in the long run? europeans are skeptical, many live on the edge of poverty far beyond the bounds of human dignity, lack access to medicine, basic services and, today, no jobs.

in writing the issue of the legislative regulation of registered partnerships is a very sensitive one and views on it vary across the eu member states. i therefore welcome the fact that the draft regulation on the property consequences of registered partnerships respects the principle of subsidiarity in favour of the member states. this regulation should in no case be used as a pretext for the introduction of a registered partnership between two persons of the same sex. the regulation concerns matters relating to the property consequences of registered partnerships. simply put, it is a situation where two people who have entered into such a union in a state that allows such a thing want to annul it and settle their property. the term 'registered partnership' is included for the purposes of this regulation only and is defined as a union which is not a marriage. the specific content of the term 'registered partnership' is defined in the national legislation of the member states. the sole purpose of the recognition of a decision on the property consequences of a registered partnership in a member state is to enable the enforcement of the property consequences determined by that decision. however, member states in which there is no registered partnership are not required to set up such an institute under this regulation.

written − article 47 of the charter of fundamental rights of the european union, article 6 of the european convention for the protection of human rights and fundamental freedoms (echr) and article 14 of the international covenant on civil and political rights (iccpr) establish the right to a fair trial. article 48 of the charter guarantees respect for the right of defence. i consider the principle of mutual recognition of judgments and judicial decisions to be a fundamental pillar of judicial cooperation in criminal matters in the union. however, mutual recognition can only function effectively if there is mutual trust, which requires the adoption of detailed rules to protect the procedural rights and guarantees arising from the charter, the echr and the echr. common minimum rules should lead to increased trust in the criminal justice systems of all member states, which in turn should result in more effective judicial cooperation within the union. the obstacles to the free movement of citizens should also be removed. i consider it important to apply all the common minimum rules mentioned in relation to the right of access to a lawyer and the right to communicate after arrest. however, common minimum standards cannot be achieved by member states acting unilaterally, either at central, regional or local level. it is therefore desirable and necessary to act at the level of the european union in this matter.
in writing − if you have the level of assurance of access to an effective defence, which is one of the fundamental procedural rights in criminal proceedings, varies depending on the particular legal system of each member state and its application in practice. strengthening the procedural rights of suspects or accused persons in criminal proceedings is a logical consequence of the functioning of a democratic and rule of law respecting the fundamental rights and freedoms of citizens. in this context, it should be stressed that the presumption of innocence is one of the fundamental conditions for the proper functioning of justice in any state and constitutes a safeguard for the rights of suspects or accused persons in criminal proceedings who may not be the actual perpetrators of the offence. so i defend the rule that a suspect or accused person who is deprived of liberty has the right to be informed of this by at least one person of his own choosing. as regards certain acts of seizure of evidence, such as the taking of blood or dna samples or the search of body cavities, which are a significant interference with bodily integrity, the right of access to a lawyer must be clearly guaranteed.
written − the european parliament has long called for greater protection of the rights of victims of crime, but also of suspects and accused persons. following the failure to adopt a framework decision on certain procedural rights in criminal proceedings, proposed by the european commission in 2004, the plenary strongly called for the adoption of an ambitious legal instrument on procedural guarantees in criminal proceedings. these rights and freedoms are among the foundations on which any mature democracy is built, and the eu is certainly one of them. article 47 of the charter of fundamental rights of the european union, article 6 of the european convention for the protection of human rights and fundamental freedoms (echr) and article 14 of the international covenant on civil and political rights (iccpr) establish the right to a fair trial. article 48 of the charter guarantees respect for the right of defence. common minimum rules should lead to increased trust in the criminal justice systems of all member states, which in turn should result in more effective judicial cooperation within the union. the obstacles to the free movement of citizens should also be removed. all the common minimum rules mentioned should apply in relation to the right of access to a lawyer and the right to communicate after arrest. harmonised minimum standards cannot be achieved by member states acting unilaterally. action at european union level is therefore necessary.
in writing − the financial crisis has had a significant impact on the citizens of the union. in response to this, the commission has been undertaking a comprehensive review of the eu mortgage housing markets for some time. all this in an effort to ensure the effective functioning of the single market. one of the objectives of the proposal is to create an efficient and competitive single market for consumers, creditors and credit intermediaries with a high level of protection. the second objective is to promote financial stability by ensuring that mortgage markets operate in a transparent and accountable manner. i believe that it is necessary and important to give due attention to this issue, since the signing and conclusion of a mortgage loan contract is one of the most significant financial decisions in a person's life, representing a financial commitment potentially lasting for decades.
in writing − the aim of the directive is to extend the single market to the field of mortgage lending. for people applying for credit, this means the introduction of the same rules for assessing credit applications, sufficient information on the terms of the loan before the contract is signed and the certainty that compliance with these rules by banks will be rigorously monitored in all eu member states. the directive should also facilitate cross-border mortgage lending. the draft directive was prepared in consultation with all interested parties banks, consumer organisations, member states, but also representatives of creditors and credit intermediaries. as regards the proposed eu-level measures, the most prominent support from all the groups consulted was for the obligation to carry out a creditworthiness assessment, the need for clear, understandable and comparable pre-contractual information and the need to ensure that all actors in the lending market are subject to appropriate regulation and supervision.
written − the market abuse directive adopted in early 2003 established a comprehensive framework to combat insider dealing and market manipulation. the directive aims to enhance investor confidence and market integrity by prohibiting insider dealing in related financial instruments and by prohibiting market manipulation through practices such as the dissemination of false information or unverified reports and the execution of trades that guarantee prices at unnatural levels. overall, the preferred policy options, together with a sound approach to the use of inside information, can be expected to contribute to improving the integrity of financial markets, which will have a positive impact on investor confidence, while contributing to the financial stability of financial markets.

written − intense rainfall in late october and early november 2012 caused the overflow of rivers from their beds and the subsequent flooding of significant areas along the sava, kupa, mura and dráva rivers in slovenia, as well as in the mura, dráva and lavant river basins in austria and in the territory of croatia. the floods caused damage to private and public buildings, water infrastructure, including waste water treatment infrastructure, businesses, agricultural land and forest cover. the commission concluded that the damage caused by the floods mentioned in all three requests was due to the same meteorological conditions and therefore considers them to be one single event. according to the estimates of the slovenian, croatian and austrian authorities, the total direct damage amounts to eur 359,535 million for slovenia, eur 11,463 million for croatia and eur 9,6 million for austria. as regards slovenia, the disaster is considered to be a 'major natural disaster' in accordance with the council regulation. coming from a country that often faces floods, i am fully aware of the devastating effects that this natural element is capable of inflicting. i therefore fully support the commission's proposal to mobilise the european union solidarity fund for a total amount of eur 14 607 942.

in writing. −the present regulation covers a number of directives concerning certain foodstuffs such as coffee and chicago extracts (1999/4/ec), cocoa and chocolate products (2000/36/ec), certain sugars (2001/111 / ec), fruit jams, jellies and marmalades and sweetened chestnut purée (2001/113/ec), and certain dried milk products (2001/114/ec). the aim is to align the commission's current implementing powers with the provisions of the treaty of lisbon, in so far as they concern the power to adopt non-legislative acts of general application to supplement or amend certain non-essential elements of a legislative act delegated to the commission and, at the same time, the power to adopt uniform conditions for the implementation of legally binding union acts conferred on the commission.

in writing, the council adopted a regulation listing the third countries whose nationals must be in possession of visas when crossing the external borders and those whose nationals are exempt from this requirement. the regulation has been amended eight times since its adoption. in recent years, some further technical adjustments to the main text of the regulation have become necessary, such as to enhance legal certainty by laying down rules covering certain situations which were not previously covered by the regulation, or to adapt certain definitions following recent changes, such as the adoption of the visa code. lastly, further adjustments are required in view of the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon, including the adoption of a safeguard clause and the adjustment of the reciprocity mechanism.
in writing − if you have in june 2012, the euro area heads of state or government invited the commission to submit proposals for the establishment of a single supervisory mechanism that would include the european central bank (ecb). in its conclusions of 29 june 2012, the european council invited the president of the european council, in close cooperation with the president of the commission, the president of the eurogroup and the president of the ecb, to develop a concrete roadmap with binding deadlines for achieving a genuine economic and monetary union, consisting of concrete proposals to preserve the unity and integrity of the single market for financial services, taking into account the euro area declaration and the commission's intention to submit proposals on the basis of article 127 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union. the establishment of a single supervisory mechanism can, in my view, be considered as a first and important step towards the creation of a european banking union based on a single set of rules for financial services. it would also include a common framework for deposit protection and resolution. however, ensuring a high, effective and uniform level of regulation and supervision throughout the european union, protecting the integrity, efficiency and orderly functioning of financial markets and maintaining the stability of the financial system cannot be satisfactorily achieved at the level of individual member states. but it can be done at the level of the union as a whole.
in writing − if you have today, the stability of the banking sector is often still closely linked to the member state in which banks are based. doubts about the sustainability of public debt, the outlook for economic growth and the viability of credit institutions create negative, mutually reinforcing market trends. the resulting situation is often the cause of specific risks within the euro area, while the single market for financial services is weakened and the economy is in decline. for this reason, and as part of a longer-term vision of economic and fiscal integration, the commission called in may 2012 for the creation of a banking union to restore confidence in banks and the euro. one of its key elements should be a single supervisory mechanism with direct supervision of banks. on the basis of the above, it can be assumed that the pursuit of strict common standards for banking supervision throughout the euro area will contribute to the growth of mutual trust between the member states of the union.

in writing − the use of genetic resources can be very beneficial, but they are a natural resource that needs to be approached in a very conservative way. nor does technological superiority give any state the right to risk the loss of biodiversity. its threatened status is becoming a serious environmental problem facing mankind. the protection of biodiversity and the preservation of biological and cultural diversity must become a basic condition for any manipulation of the planet's gene pool. i also believe that the application of genetic research must take into account the bioethical aspect in each case.

in writing − the arrival of unaccompanied minors in the european union is not only a temporary phenomenon but a long-term one accompanying contemporary migration. it is therefore necessary for the union to adopt a common approach to this group of migrants. the reasons for the arrival of unaccompanied children remain diverse and interconnected. some flee armed conflict, natural disasters, discrimination, or persecution. the fact is that some unaccompanied minors arrive as victims of trafficking for exploitation. this sad reality is not limited to south-east asia, where the situation is most critical, but is increasingly being seen in europe as well. when comparing member states, it is clear that migration flows differ. in some countries, unaccompanied minors arrive mainly as asylum seekers. in other member states, asylum flows are relatively low compared to the numbers of children arriving as illegal migrants. the european union must continue to apply its guidelines on the promotion and protection of the rights of the child. in the enforcement of further procedures, it is necessary that these minors are not subjected to unnecessary medical examinations designed to establish their age, precisely in the context of and in accordance with the protection of the abovementioned rights.

the european carbon trading system covers some 11 000 companies, which account for more than half of the union's carbon dioxide emissions and around 40% of greenhouse gases. however, emissions trading is in crisis. their supply far exceeds demand and the low price does not motivate firms to innovate. there are more causes for this condition. first, the system does not work as an economic tool, because the number of permits was decided by politicians who, even under pressure from the industry lobby, apparently gave away too much. second, in addition to allowances, firms can also partially cover their emissions with cheap carbon credits from third country projects, which also contributes to the oversupply on the market. third, because of ill-considered policy decisions, there are a number of harmful exceptions to the system. it is clear that the current form of the emissions trading system is more of a burden than a benefit for both companies and consumers. companies lose money that they could invest in production and thus increase employment, while consumers pay for emission allowances in electricity prices because suppliers include their value in electricity prices despite having received the allowances for free. i therefore believe that the whole european emissions trading system needs to be thoroughly reworked as soon as possible.

in writing. smoking is one of the main causes of death in the eu. it kills 700,000 people a year! up to 70% of smokers start smoking before the age of 18. this is where our measures to discourage young people from smoking must go: tougher warnings on cigarette packs and bans on packaging and flavours that are attractive to young people. on the other hand, we must ensure that our measures are effective in combating counterfeiting and smuggling of cigarettes. for that reason, i cannot support the extreme proposal for the size of health warnings. eu health ministers agreed that health warnings should cover 65% of the box. according to information from the ministry of finance of my country, any size above 65% would make it technically impossible to put a check mark on the boxes. this would deprive the eu of an effective tool against counterfeiting and smuggling.
in writing. our discussion should not be about whether smoking is harmful or not. we know that the consumption of tobacco products is harmful to health and member states should strive to reduce the consumption of these products. however, some of the provisions of the commission's proposal raise serious doubts as to their compatibility with fundamental rights, such as the right to property, the right to information and the freedom to conduct a business. we should ensure a sustainable and fair european space for our companies to operate. the proposal introduces excessive regulation of the production and trade of tobacco products, to the detriment of the european internal market. increasing the scope of health warnings on tobacco product packages may be counterproductive. this counterproductivity of new measures may also be shown in the increase in the share of illicit trade. the directive may have a negative impact on the economic situation of smes. it must also be recalled that the increased market for counterfeit tobacco products means that member states are missing an important contribution to the national budget. we must protect the interests of the consumer, whether he is a smoker or a non-smoker. the consumer has a right to full information about the source of the product, which is why i'm in favor of a health warning up to 50%. however, our duty is not only to protect consumers but also producers, who have the right to have their protected trade marks displayed in a transparent manner.
corruption in the third world is reaching enormous proportions. perhaps as much as a third of development aid from the public budgets of third world countries is stolen. this problem can only be solved by increasing the transparency of banks and european companies in third countries, while at the same time increasing the protection of whistleblowers. because there is a significant connection between corruption and human rights violations. the european union must strictly require recipients of foreign aid to protect whistleblowers who point out corrupt practices. it's a matter of human rights in these countries, but also respect for our taxpayers.
in writing. − corruption in the public and private sectors costs nearly 5% of global gdp and the annual bribes paid are equivalent to the estimated gdp of all of africa. i find it scandalous that while 1.4 billion people live in poverty and hunger, some 20-40 billion dollars are annually stolen and hidden from the public budgets of developing countries through corruption, corresponding to 20-40% of official development assistance. i am appalled to find that in the years 2000 to 2009 alone, developing countries lost nearly $8.5 trillion to such practices, ten times the amount of foreign aid they received. as the largest provider of development aid, the european union must ensure that the funds it provides are used in a lawful and ethical manner. i therefore welcome the report by anna gomes on corruption in the public and private sectors and i believe that this report will become a good springboard for rapid improvement of legislation in the fight against corruption.
in writing. − although the eu and the member states have so far adopted a number of measures and instruments to prevent and control the spread of corruption and illicit financial flows, i believe that corruption continues to have a negative impact on all areas of our public life. this is evidenced by published statistics that show that corruption accounts for 5% of global gdp, with over $1 trillion paid in bribes annually. i also find it alarming that corruption increases the cost of doing business globally by up to 10% and the cost of public procurement in developing countries by up to 25%. i supported this current report not only because tackling corruption is one of the eu's key priorities, but also because i consider it to be one of the greatest threats to any democratic and rule of law state. although it is not possible to formulate a specific set of guidelines on anti-corruption measures, i expect the commission to step up its efforts in the fight against corruption. i also expect the commission to create sufficient space for member states to exchange best practices and experience in fighting corruption and complying with commitments made at eu level.
in writing. - i welcome the report on international private and employment law. this owninitiative report of the european parliament provides many useful solutions in relation to the determination of competences in the field of labour law. in the area of jurisdiction, the principle of the protection of the weaker party, which is the employees, must apply in labour law. many existing provisions could be improved for the benefit of employees. i therefore agree with the rapporteur that in cases where the employer is the defendant, the action may be brought either in the courts of the member state in which he is domiciled or, in another member state, in the courts of the place where or from where the employee habitually carries out his work. where such a place cannot be determined, this criterion shall be replaced by the place where the establishment which employed the staff member is situated.
in writing. − the jurisdiction of the european union in the field of the recognition and enforcement of judgments in civil and commercial matters was strengthened in 2012 by the brussels i regulation. it is not intended to substitute national jurisdiction but, on the contrary, to facilitate substantially the enforcement of judgments in another member state. labour law, on the other hand, is a separate area governed by national rules. however, in the past, individual member states' employment legislation has shown to differ significantly. it is absurd for a court in one state to be bound by the law of another state merely because of the vague establishment of the rules, as was the case with dfds toreline in 2004. in cases where the employer is the defendant, the case may be dealt with in the state where the employer is domiciled or in the place where the employee habitually carries out his work. if the usual place of work cannot be identified, the brussels i regulation provides for an emergency criterion concerning the place of business. problems may arise in the international transport sector. for airline employees or truck drivers, it is often difficult to reveal where an employee has been working since the company may be registered in different member states. i therefore welcome the report presented by the rapporteur, mrs regner, and i believe that by clarifying the rules on jurisdiction in employment matters we will help to speed up the resolution of disputes and better protect workers in other countries.
in writing. − i consider the fight against smoking, which causes incalculable damage to human life and health every year, to be an essential part of public health protection. health warnings are justified within an organised and long-term anti-smoking strategy. anti-smoking campaigns should target adolescents, who are often unaware of the real risks and consequences of smoking, as these are downplayed or deliberately ignored by the environment and the media. i also believe that we need to step up the protection of the rights of non-smokers, and in particular young people and children, against second-hand smoke, which causes many health risks, including asthma. special protection must also be provided to women during pregnancy in order to prevent diseases of human foetuses and newborns caused by the consumption of tobacco products by their mothers. furthermore, campaigns to prevent sudden infant death should inform parents that smoking in the presence of newborn babies can cause their sudden death. it also seems logical to me that tobacco manufacturers should be financially responsible for healthcare costs arising from tobacco consumption, in accordance with the principle of producer responsibility for damage caused.

in writing. − gender-based homicide has become a global phenomenon in recent years. gendercide occurs mainly in cultures where there is a strong preference for male offspring, with the female population subject to persistent stereotypes. other motives are declining birth rates and pressure to start small families. none of the above causes legitimize gender-based murder in any way. the gender-selective decision, the selective abortion or the killing of a child born solely on the basis of its sex is associated with the prevailing unequal perception of the status of both sexes in individual countries. discriminatory attitudes in some cultures are so ingrained that they affect the overall status of women in society. access to healthcare, education, social security and unequal treatment in employment are just some of the consequences of gender discrimination and human rights violations. i am fully aware of the complexity of tackling gendercide, as well as gender discrimination in countries with similar practices. on the other hand, i firmly believe that, through the cooperation of the european commission, the member states, civil society and international organisations, we will not only be able to put in place support measures to prevent gender-based killings, but also to shape, through education and positive example, the overall perception of the position of both sexes in patriarchal societies.
