the global economic crisis and the austerity policies of many member states have drastically reduced revenues for regional and local authorities. we decided that, despite the doubts, the use of the european funds, i.e. the reallocation of public budgets, is an effective way of promoting local development, the economy and employment. it is therefore necessary to promote the greatest possible flexibility for member states in the use of the structural funds. these are mainly smaller territorial units that need funds for investments in infrastructure and public services. as a result of the application of the stability and growth pact, there is scope for this flexibility and it should be used.
in writing. − the current financial and economic crisis is severely constraining member states' public finances. this means that regional and local authorities are unable to provide productive investment. on the one hand, they are experiencing a significant decline in their income, and on the other hand, they have to provide social services with increasing expenditure. it is important to make concrete proposals to ensure that, during the period of strict implementation of the stability and growth pact, national co-financing is linked as flexibly as possible to eu development expenditure. this requires knowledge of the extent to which the crisis has affected the ability of sub-national authorities to meet the europe 2020 targets for growth and jobs. proposals should be made to improve the capacity of these institutions to finance productive investments. i agree with the report that asks the commission to report on this subject, as requested by the so-called 'dual package': 'state expenditure related to the implementation of programmes co-financed under cohesion policy and rural development policy should be excluded from the restrictions of the stability and growth pact, as this expenditure is intended to support competitiveness and growth; exploiting the possibilities provided by the preventive arm of the stability and growth pact to strike a balance between the need for productive public investment and the objective of fiscal discipline. i voted in favour of the report.
in writing. − the financial and economic crisis has contributed significantly to increasing disparities between regions in the eu, with the poorest regions in the new member states and in southern europe suffering the most. it is in the most affected areas that cohesion policy finds its true meaning and mission as the main investment instrument for convergence and sustainable development. regional and local authorities play an irreplaceable role in socioeconomic development at local level, which the state, from its central level of management, somehow does not control. member states must therefore systematically facilitate the use of the funds by the regions and enable them to make use of the new resources allocated to the 2014-2020 programming period as quickly as possible. in conclusion, i would agree with the view that macroeconomic conditionality could cause problems in the implementation of cohesion policy, affect the most affected regions and, moreover, jeopardise the achievement of the eu's long-term objectives.

on behalf of the ppe group. – mr president, approving the resolution to open trade negotiations with taiwan is a step in the right direction towards strengthening the eu’s relations with taiwan both culturally and economically. over the past two decades, bilateral trade between the eu and taiwan has multiplied twelvefold, with trade between the two economies growing to eur 40 billion in 2011. even with this growth, trade between the eu and taiwan is still below its potential. taiwan is a rock-solid democracy and a vibrant economy that has many benefits to offer to the eu. a few years ago, when i argued in the committee on international trade meetings for a stronger trade relationship to harvest those benefits, the reply from the commission was that we did not want to be the first. the message was clear: the eu did not want to provoke china and wanted to see china’s reaction to taiwan’s ftas with other countries. now that china, the usa, south korea, singapore and new zealand are either negotiating, or have concluded, free trade investment and trade agreements with taiwan, can the eu afford to be left behind? the answer to this question should be very clear. to benefit citizens on both sides, negotiations on a stronger and deeper trade and investment agreement between the eu and taiwan should begin sooner rather than later.
taiwan is the union's seventh largest trading partner in asia. it is therefore in our mutual interest to deepen our cooperation in this area. i therefore want to support the negotiation of trade agreements between the union and taiwan. the stabilisation of relations between taiwan and china has created the conditions for the eu to extend its activities through taiwan towards china and south-east asia. it should be remembered that the eu should make more use of taiwan's position in research and development to improve the long-term growth and competitiveness of its own industry. the experience from slovakia confirms that taiwanese investments are coming to sectors with high added value. the possibility of more active negotiation in investment protection agreements and other mutually beneficial agreements should therefore be sought.
the unannounced tightening of border controls at the lithuanian-russian border against carriers importing goods into the russian federation is a serious problem. a quantity of goods originating in other countries of the european union is transported through lithuania to the russian federation and therefore the customs measures are directly transferred to the other countries of the union. the russian federation is one of the european union's most important trading partners and therefore a proper trade relationship with such a partner should be in the mutual interest, that is to say, in the interest of both parties. the resolution of this unilateral action by the russian authorities must therefore become one of the most important tasks of our trade diplomacy, so that the unannounced tightening of customs controls does not lead to more serious trade problems with consequences for both the european and russian economies. i am convinced, mr commissioner, that there is no need to hesitate for long and that we must begin to negotiate the problem factually and constructively with the other side, that is to say, with our russian partners.

for the efd group. we all know that the production and use of batteries and accumulators containing cadmium is a problem in terms of their environmental impact. cadmium from batteries can also penetrate the human body, to which it is toxic, and cause serious damage if handled improperly. it is therefore necessary to consistently promote appropriate collection and recycling systems that can achieve up to 100% recycling of cadmium from portable batteries and accumulators. the commission therefore concluded that the dumped imports from the prc had caused material injury to the union industry. the commission's proposal to phase out nickel-cadmium batteries in europe by the end of 2015 is therefore an administrative measure aimed at protecting the environment and promoting new technologies, which are however more expensive and technologically challenging. therefore, i agree with the rapporteur that a better compromise towards the european public would be a date for the end of the use of nickel-cadmium batteries by the end of 2016 and possibly beyond.
first of all, i'd like to congratulate my colleague panayotov on his excellent work. in 2011, 40% of all electric hand tools were classified as cordless electric hand tools. today, the largest proportion of cordless power tools are nickel-cadmium, nickel-metal hydride and lithium-ion rechargeable batteries. of these, 70% were lithium-ion battery powered and 27% were nickel-cadmium battery powered. however, it should be noted that the reverse is true for the central and eastern european member states. it will take more time to completely eliminate the market for batteries containing cadmium in this region. due to its harmful effects on the environment and human health, cadmium is included in the list of substances of greatest concern. when it accumulates in the environment and in the human body, it is toxic because it persists indefinitely and often causes irreversible damage. given the possibility of 100% recycling of collected nickel-cadmium batteries, the risks are manageable and less significant. the extension of the exemption for one year would allow for a reasonable compromise. this would protect the interests of both consumers and businesses along the entire value chain.
in writing. − the use of batteries and accumulators containing cadmium or mercury poses many problems in terms of their loading, consumption and subsequent disposal. because cadmium is a chemical element that cannot be broken down by the human body, it accumulates. moreover, cadmium and its compounds are toxic not only to humans but also to the environment. i fully support the introduction of efficient collection and recycling systems, as the cadmium contained in many appliances can be 100% recycled. in this way, we would achieve a significant reduction in risks to humans and the environment. i believe that stricter rules on the use of batteries and accumulators will take account of the economic context of the sector and contribute to limiting the release of harmful substances into the environment.

the proposal for a directive regulates the market in in vitro diagnostic devices and in the determination and analysis of dna. this is about setting minimum standards, for example, for the use of dna tests. in particular, it is important that in the future, counselling by qualified professionals should be made compulsory throughout the european union. in particular, the issue of informed consent, which is one of the fundamental rights guaranteed by the charter of the european union, is important. only informed patients can take responsibility for often very serious decisions concerning their lives and health.
in writing. − i would like to thank rapporteur petr lies for his excellent work on the in vitro diagnostic report, as safe and high-quality diagnosis is a fundamental pillar of medical care. the need for stricter regulation has arisen in particular in view of the poorly documented quality of several hiv or dna tests, the incorrect results or interpretation of which can have fatal consequences. a european surveillance system is necessary given that there are no national borders on the european market for these products. i particularly appreciate the efforts to strengthen ethical safeguards, especially on the issue of informed consent, where dna tests cannot be used without appropriate and responsible genetic counselling to provide sufficient information before the test is carried out.
in writing. − health and safety of diagnostic equipment or devices is one of the eu's priorities. in vitro diagnostic devices also fall into this category. these are medical devices intended for use in diagnosis outside the human body, which may be carried out in a laboratory or in the vicinity of the patient, for example at bedside. this includes a wide range of tests, such as self- blood sugar tests, hiv tests and dna tests. in vitro diagnostic medical devices are products which are freely available on the common market. however, the current directive does not guarantee that low-quality diagnostic medical devices of this type will not be placed on the market. a substandard hiv test has entered the european market. this type of test produced far more false negatives than other available hiv tests. so the tests showed no virus, when in fact, it was there. however, this product has been available to patients in europe for several years. there are many issues where the european commission proposes to regulate in vitro diagnostic medical devices in the same way as other medical devices. there are no national borders for these products on the european market. the european union is therefore obliged to ensure the greatest possible security.
in writing. − i supported the report because i believe that the changes and proposed measures can strengthen and improve the current status and system for in vitro diagnostic medical devices in a more significant way. i understand that the application of the principle of free movement of goods in trade in in vitro diagnostic medical devices varies considerably between member states. it is of concern that in vitro diagnostic medical devices are often placed on the eu market of poor quality, endangering life, and posing a risk not only to patients, users but also to healthcare professionals. i think that whether we consider in vitro diagnostic medical devices as 'little sisters' or 'parents', we must first of all consider safety and the protection of human health. while there have been several positive developments in the field of in vitro diagnostic medical devices, which represent a wide range of products, i expect that the market surveillance system will be strengthened, the public safety and oversight of the entire certification system will be improved and a better system for devices in the highest risk classes will be introduced to address the shortcomings.
in writing. − i welcome this necessary revision of the legislation with an emphasis on improving access to medical devices, but in particular their safety for patients. safety is the key point in the approval process based on sufficient clinical trials. those devices which are intended to be implanted in the body must be subject to particularly stringent criteria, which will be ensured by the establishment of specific notified conformity assessment bodies. such bodies shall operate in an efficient, transparent and qualified manner. i want to stress the importance of an independent ethics committee, which must give an opinion before the start of a clinical trial, as is the case with clinical trials of medicines. all member states must ensure the proper functioning of such commissions.
in writing. − as with the in vitro diagnostic medical device report, i voted in favour of this report because i consider it to be an important part of the safety, quality and efficacy of medical devices, which aims to address safety concerns related to these products. while some other changes and measures could be incorporated into the new regulatory framework, i am pleased that the commission is coming up with a solution to classify medical devices into four categories according to the level of risk to patients. i believe that these changes can help to eliminate the serious shortcomings that have emerged in the past. i expect that medical devices that pose the greatest risks to patients will be subject to more stringent procedures and not just conformity assessment by notified bodies. i find it very worrying that the functioning of notified bodies has been judged to be very weak in recent times. this is evidenced by the fundamental differences in the conformity assessments carried out, the lack of transparency of these organisations, their vigilance, etc. i am convinced that the provisions on the staffing of notified bodies will be strengthened at national level in order to improve this situation.
in writing. − i supported the proposal because it aims at a high level of health protection for both patients and medical device operators. i believe that medical devices on the european union market must be safe not only for patients but also for the healthcare professionals who use or operate them and for lay people who come into contact with them. not only nurses and doctors are at risk, but also nurses, laboratory workers, and support staff. medical devices must be subject to the strictest controls. manufacturers of both original and refurbished devices should collect data on whether they meet all the requirements for functionality and safety. at the same time, however, any increase in costs must not jeopardise the availability of these devices to all those who need them.
in writing. − we have already called in the past, together with our colleagues from the new member states, for the deletion of article 4 from this regulation. the reason was the interests of our citizens working and living abroad, who will have no one to represent them in the eu council from next year. according to the original text of the demographic statistics regulation, they would be included among the residents of the state in which they live at that time. however, since they cannot vote in parliamentary elections, the host government would not represent their interests on eu soil, even though this would give it more weight in votes in the eu council. the text adopted today is a compromise which allows member states to use statistical estimates for representation in the council, while at the same time extending the definition to cover legal and registered residence. i supported this compromise, although i think that omitting this paragraph is a better solution.

in writing. − drug precursors are chemicals with a wide range of legal uses. trade in them is legitimate, both in regional and global markets. however, some of them have the potential to be misused for the illicit manufacture of narcotic substances. the control of drug precursors is one of the key actions in the effective fight against drugs. despite the establishment of a regulatory framework at both international and eu level, a legal gap has emerged that needs to be filled. these are in particular preparations for human use containing ephedrine or pre-doephedrine when these medicinal products have been exported from or transited through the customs territory of the union, even though it was foreseeable that they would be misused for the illicit manufacture of methamphetamine in the country of their destination. for this reason too, the eu is expected to close the legislative gap.
in writing. − drug precursors are chemical compounds that are produced for legal purposes but can be misused to produce narcotic and psychotropic substances. the trade in drug precursors is not prohibited. these bars are used in many standard industrial processes. however, to prevent the misuse of drug precursors for illicit manufacture, a regulatory framework has been established at national level, to which the eu is a party. a vast network of manufacturers, distributors, intermediaries, importers, exporters or wholesalers of chemicals operating in legitimate trade must take anti-theft measures, control their customers, detect suspicious transactions and report them to the competent authorities. it is therefore precisely this partnership between industry and the authorities that is of vital importance for the effective functioning of the regulatory framework.
in writing. − drug precursors are chemicals commonly used in various industrial processes, such as the production of plastics, pharmaceuticals, cosmetics or cleaning products, but which can be misused to produce illicit drugs. among the less well-known are so-called bath salts. this type of drug is often found in large quantities in online shops and is virtually legal to sell. synthetic drugs are sold as products for other uses, such as cleaning agents. however, these substances have many times more dangerous effects than 'conventional' drugs made from natural substances. this type of drug has been popular for the last four years or so. the information available has repeatedly shown that these substances have unpredictable effects on their users, often associated with violent crime. over the past few years, the eu has been the target of international criticism for its allegedly too lax control measures. this criticism focused in particular on one substance, acetic acid aa. the quantities of aa seized within europe in 2008 would be approximately sufficient to cover the half-year demand for aa needed to produce heroin in afghanistan. it is therefore very important to ensure that drug precursors such as aa do not fall into the wrong hands.

in writing. − organized crime is no longer a phenomenon limited to a historical and territorial dimension. today, there are some 3 600 international criminal groups operating in the eu alone. organised crime is characterised by intimidation, corruption, money laundering or tax fraud and tax evasion. in order to prevent such unfair practices, efforts to counter them should be made at global level. effective judicial cooperation at european and international level is desirable. in this context, it is necessary that each member state has adequate legislation.
in writing. - organized crime knows no borders. to this end, a special committee was set up in the european parliament to study the activities of organised crime in the european union and to propose a legal framework to enable the member states to combat it more effectively. this report discusses a number of tools to combat organised crime. however, i am not sure that the proposal for a pan-european corporate income tax really falls within the scope of this report. the level of income tax in the member states reflects the extent and quality of public services. if we unify the tax rate without guaranteeing the same quality and scope of these services, we will put the new member states at a disadvantage in favour of the old ones. i strongly disagree.
in writing. − the european neighbourhood policy (enp) has helped to change the relationship between the eu and its neighbours. since 2004, when the esp began to take place, contacts between the two sides have intensified. trade has doubled, and eu aid to neighbouring countries has increased. however, further progress is needed to deepen bilateral security and stability. the treaty of lisbon also commits to developing mutual relations.
in writing. − the commission presented the annual growth survey (ags) as early as november 2012. the commission has not found any evidence that the union industry has benefited from the measures in force. in the last 12 months, the number of unemployed has increased by another two million, reaching a level of 25 million. the segmentation of the labour market continued to increase and long-term unemployment reached alarming levels. in many member states, average household incomes are falling and indicators point to deeper forms of poverty and social exclusion. in order to improve the current critical situation, member states simply have to make, and above all actually implement, the necessary commitments, in the framework of their national reform programmes.
in writing. − according to the international organisation for migration, at least 20 000 people have died at sea since 1993. this sad news underscores the need to make every effort to save the lives of people in danger in international waters. the tragic event that took place in early october on the italian island of lampedusa should be a real milestone for the eu. in order to prevent similar tragedies, it is justified to adopt a common european approach aiming at taking steps to prevent such events from happening again. this can also be helped by deepening cooperation with third countries and by strengthening cross-border cooperation at the external borders of the member states of the union.
in writing. − i supported the joint resolution in the hope that the commission would come forward very soon with a comprehensive proposal for solutions to deal with the influx of refugees into eu countries, such as the cases in recent weeks where people have lost their lives in the hope of a better and safer future for themselves and their children. council directive 202/90/ec should have been revised long ago so that people providing humanitarian assistance to migrants at sea in emergency situations could not be sanctioned for facilitating unauthorised entry, transit and residence in any country. refugees who choose to leave their homeland, where they were born, and have families of their own are often forced to make such a grave decision out of fear for their lives. they are therefore desperate to find refuge in an economically strong and secure europe. we therefore need to review asylum policies in all member states and jointly build capacity to enable the temporary resettlement of refugees in emergency situations. on the other hand, we must be firm against criminal groups involved in human trafficking and smuggling.
in writing. − the eu-us agreement on the processing and transmission of data contained in financial messages from the eu to the us for the purposes of the terrorist finance tracking program entered into force on 1 august 2010. press reports indicate that the us national security agency (nsa) has direct access to the information systems of many private companies and has obtained direct access to data contained in financial reports. one of the union's main objectives is to promote individual freedom. however, in order to respect the rights and freedoms of citizens of the union's member states, the processing of personal data must also comply with eu and member state rules.
in writing. − the importance of the draft amending budget presented is to avoid a cash shortage which could lead to a failure to meet the commitments in question in 2013. the commission notes that the commission has not provided any information on the amount of the capital injections in question. the reduction in the forecast of traditional own resources by approximately eur 3 955 million and in the vat-based own resources by eur 384 million is offset by fines totalling eur 1 229 million. although this will place a considerable burden on national budgets, the revenue side change should not be at the expense of financing the full amount of eligible items already defined by the commission in the draft subsequent amending budgets.
in writing. − the eu's goal is to have a smart, sustainable and inclusive economy by 2020, with a set of policies and measures to enable a smooth transition to a low-carbon, resource-efficient economy. since 1973, the subsequent environmental action programmes (eaps) have provided the framework for union action on environmental issues. so far, the last, sixth eap, has recognised that the programme has been environmentally beneficial and has created an overarching framework for the strategic direction of environmental policy. however, despite these successes, unsustainable trends persist in all four priority areas identified in the 6th eap. further action is needed to address these issues in order to ensure the long-term prosperity of the union. it is important to set the union's priority objectives for 2020 in the light of a long-term vision, with the new programme building on europe 2020 initiatives as a priority.
in writing. − exposure to ionising radiation has resulted in harm to health. however, small doses may have a delayed effect. it is assumed that there is no dose limit for this effect: any exposure, however small, can cause cancer in later life. the euratom treaty contains an important body of legislation dealing with various radiation protection issues. these are the so-called basic safety standards. however, their development overlaps over a relatively long period, there are several inconsistencies between the individual acts and references are obsolete due to updated legislation. these gaps need to be aligned with the commission's policy of simplifying european legislation. this is, however, primarily to ensure better protection of the general public.
in writing. − the annual report addresses the main issues of the eu's cfsp, both institutionally and politically. it stresses in particular the central role of the promotion of democracy, human rights and the rule of law in the eu in the context of foreign policy. it highlights the challenges facing the eu in the cfsp in relations with countries such as russia (especially in relation to eastern partnership issues) and china. a new element in this year's report is a reference to the changes in iran after the election of the president. the report calls for consideration of possible incentives, taking into account whether and when iran will meet its commitments to the international community with regard to its nuclear programme.
in writing. −the latest proposals to amend the union's framework for electronic communications were submitted by the commission back in november 2007. the revised framework was adopted by the european parliament and the council two years later, in november 2009. it was necessary to transpose this framework into national law at the latest 18 months after its adoption. however, to date very few member states have transposed these rules in time and the last member states notified full transposition only in january 2013. although the commission is obliged to review this framework on a regular basis and has recently committed to carrying out a review of two components of the framework, it has not yet announced that it intends to carry out a full review in the foreseeable future. it can be said that the internal market in electronic communications is not yet complete. however, it is desirable and necessary that it should be an instrument that could create the necessary conditions to promote and link investment and competition, and thus ultimately have a positive impact on the lives of citizens. this is where all the efforts of stakeholders should be directed.

for the efd group the proposed commission regulation responds to the problems of implementing the trans-european transport network, which is one of the union's key investment projects. the commission has also been working on a number of other projects, including the development of a new european transport network. the commission's proposal to divide the transport network into two tiers, the basic network, to be completed by 2030, and the comprehensive network, to be completed by 2050, can be understood as an effort to introduce certain priorities into the union's transport system, on the basis of which it would be possible to prioritise the construction of certain parts of the network over others. however, i also consider it important to involve local and regional authorities in the preparation of such projects. as an example, i could mention the priority project no 17 of the paris-strasbourg-vienna-bratislava railway line, which is to meet at the bratislava node with corridor no 4 berlin-prague-bratislava-budapest-thessaloniki and the northern branch of corridor no 5 venice-thirst-ljubljana-budapest-bratislava-zilina, etc., without meaningfully linking at this node. both local and regional authorities have repeatedly called for a more rational and pragmatic technical solution for this railway junction with a natural north-south connection in the city. but our brussels representatives have so far stubbornly ignored the regional authorities' logical arguments, and i think that is not good.

in writing − a government procurement agreement is an international agreement of a legally binding nature. it deals with access to government procurement markets and some members of the world trade organisation are also co-signatories. it currently has 15 contracting parties, one of which is the european union. the contracting parties agreed to revise the text laying down the rules as early as 2006. under the treaty of lisbon, ratification must be agreed by the european parliament and the council. however, this does not allow the european parliament to make certain changes to the text. it can only express its consent to the agreement as such. it is therefore of the utmost importance to carefully weigh the benefits of the agreement against its possible negative consequences.

written − the trans-european transport network (ten-t) is one of the key infrastructure projects of the european union. it is an essential part of the common market, indispensable for the mobility of eu citizens, for economic, social and territorial cohesion, for economic growth and for job creation. however, the implementation of this network is currently facing a number of problems, including in particular funding difficulties during the economic crisis and significant delays in the implementation of many projects. europe needs to complete the missing links and remove the obstacles in the common transport infrastructure, as well as to ensure the future and sustainability of transport. the newly approved eu infrastructure policy aims to create a genuine network and no longer focus on isolated projects. for projects of common interest, deadlines have been set for their implementation in order to ensure priority implementation by the member states. better analysis of socio-economic costs and benefits, including environmental impact assessment, and a clear definition of european added value will contribute to a stronger focus on ten-t infrastructure priorities. therefore, maximising added value and making the most progress possible with limited financial resources must be one of the key priorities of the ten-t network.

in writing − if you have the aim of this proposal from the european commission is to amend nine legislative acts in the field of agricultural and fisheries statistics. the aim is to adapt them to the new institutional context. in the context of regulation (eu) no 182/2011 of the european parliament and of the council of 16 february 2011, the commission undertook to review legislative acts which refer to the regulatory procedure with scrutiny in the light of the criteria laid down in the treaty. the aim is to remove all provisions referring to the regulatory procedure with scrutiny from legislative acts by the end of the seventh parliamentary term of the european parliament. the second part of the commission's proposal deals with the simplification of the european statistical system. the european statistical system is defined as a partnership between the european statistical authority, the commission, and the national statistical institutes and other national authorities responsible in each member state for the development, production and dissemination of european statistics.

in writing the aim of amending articles 25 and 26 of the unece convention on the protection and use of transboundary watercourses and international lakes, also known as the helsinki convention, is to establish a framework for bilateral and multilateral cooperation in the prevention and control of pollution of transboundary watercourses. equally important is the rational use of water resources in the unece member countries. the member states of the european union are also co-signatories to this convention. the parties to the helsinki convention have expressed the need to allow countries outside the unece region to become parties for the purpose of cooperation. the amendment was formally accepted by 2/3 of the parties back in 2012. however, the european union has not yet formally accepted the entry into force of these amendments.

in writing, the slovak republic, like lithuania and bulgaria, has committed to shut down and decommission its nuclear reactors. the european union has concluded that they are too outdated and potentially dangerous, and that the necessary modernisation would be extremely inefficient in terms of cost. however, this requirement by the union represents a significant environmental, economic, social and, of course, financial burden, and the eu has therefore committed to providing financial assistance to these countries by the end of 2013. the total amount of european union aid to slovakia, lithuania and bulgaria until the end of 2013 is estimated at eur 2 847,8 million (eur 1 367 million for lithuania, eur 613 million for slovakia and eur 867,8 million for bulgaria). however, in 2011, the estimates of the resources needed to decommission the reactors were updated to eur 5 300 million, which is eur 2 500 million short of the funds currently available at national and programme level. this lack of funding seriously jeopardises the successful completion of the decommissioning process of old nuclear installations. the draft report in its current form is a one-sided presentation of negative information. the findings presented cast a negative light on the whole dumping process, also indicating a potential risk of endangering eu citizens, which is not based on the truth.

in writing − the agreement between the european union and the russian federation aims to improve cooperation between the two trading partners in the area of monitoring the trade in drug precursors. drug precursors are legally available substances that can be used to produce synthetic drugs. for example, acetic acid is used in the production of heroin. drug precursors are subject to relatively strict controls on import, export or transit, depending on the risk of misuse. the european commission therefore submitted a proposal for a regulation in accordance with the ordinary legislative procedure in order to establish a supervisory framework. this international agreement was signed on 4 june 2013 at the eu-russia summit in yekaterinburg. it is based on cooperation between the parties in monitoring trade in certain chemicals and on a system of mutual administrative assistance. in addition to administrative assistance, it also contains provisions on scientific and technical cooperation. i consider that provision of this kind is very important in the context of the current boom in synthetic drugs, which i also mentioned last month. they aim to identify new methods of abuse as well as appropriate countermeasures. the joint expert monitoring group will be composed of representatives of the competent authorities responsible for the administration and proper implementation of the agreement.

written − the european grouping of territorial cooperation was created by regulation (ec) no 1082/2006 with the aim of creating a cooperation instrument at european union level, which will have its own legal personality. the main task of this grouping was to overcome the obstacles to territorial cooperation. in 2011, the commission presented a report on the application of this regulation, identifying areas for improvement. these amendments relate in particular to taking account of the treaty of lisbon, simplifying and clarifying certain provisions which cause confusion and establishing a legal basis for the participation of authorities and regions from non-member countries. the amendments to the regulation should in particular ensure a higher degree of legal certainty and enhance territorial cooperation within the european union and between regions of the member states and third countries.
in writing. − the primary objectives of the revision of the original regulation were to simplify, provide legal certainty and flexibility in the application of the rules and to reduce the administrative burden on groups and their prospective members. the egtc shall be deemed to be approved by tacit consent after the expiry of the six-month limited time limit for the examination given to the competent national authorities during the authorisation procedure. exemption from this rule shall be granted only to the member state in which the proposed seat of the egtc is to be located in accordance with the egtc's constituent instrument. the new regulation makes a clear distinction between the statute and the convention. only the convention is subject to formal approval, reducing the administrative burden for members by facilitating and speeding up the authorisation process. it clarifies the rules on the employment of the staff of the groupings, whereby members may choose between the law of the grouping's seat, the law of the place where the staff is employed or the national law of the staff concerned. the egtcs will be open to all publicly owned undertakings providing public services, including those governed by private law. i hope that this regulation, which is more precise, will put an end to arbitrary and sometimes unlawful interpretations by the member states. that's why i voted for this motion.

written − the european union stands by the principles of liberty, democracy, respect for human rights and fundamental freedoms and the rule of law, which are unique to and common to the member states. the charter of fundamental rights of the european union, which became legally binding with the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon, sets out the fundamental rights and freedoms to which individuals are entitled within the union. it is essential to guarantee the full enjoyment of these rights and to remove all related obstacles. experience with action at union level has shown that achieving the set objectives in practice requires a combination of several instruments, including legislation, policy initiatives and funding. it therefore appears important to establish a funding programme. in response to the need for simplification and efficient management of funds, this regulation establishes the rights and citizenship programme, which ensures the continuation and further development of the activities carried out previously under the three programmes.
written − the rights and citizenship programme is intended to merge the three existing citizenship programmes. these are the fundamental rights and citizenship programmes, daphne iii, the 'combating discrimination and diversity' and 'gender equality' sections of the employment and social solidarity programme. in the new programme, we sought not only better funding for specific initiatives, but also to extend the scope of the funds in the area of minority rights, including roma rights, and the fight against racism and xenophobia. the consequences of the financial and economic crisis are increasingly threatening our fundamental values. in these circumstances, the rights and citizenship programme pays great attention to combating discrimination, hatred, the marginalisation of other groups, segregation and all forms of violence. it is particularly important that the rights of persons with disabilities are guaranteed. eu funding must contribute to a more open society, one of the commitments of the eu 2020 strategy. however, i regret that due to the inability of the institutions to agree on implementing and delegated acts, the commission will only publish a call for proposals next year and therefore the actual implementation of the programme will only be possible in the second quarter of 2014.
in writing mr. chairman, the treaty on the functioning of the european union only talks about equality between men and women. there is no legal basis for the use of the terms 'gender' and 'gender equality'. the extended meaning of the term gender is also not supported by international law. its only definition is found in the rome statute of the international criminal court. quote: "in social contexts, it refers to both sexes, male and female. the term gender does not imply any other meaning which differs from the meaning already mentioned. end of quote. the idea that inequality leads to exploitation comes from marxist doctrine. the communists have never hidden their desire to eliminate the 'bourgeois-capitalist power structures'. marriage and the family, according to marxists, are products of a power structure that is meant to serve as a means of maintaining the power of capital. in the report submitted, the term 'gender' and 'gender equality' appear 12 times. it's not a coincidence. thank you. thank you.

written − the un international convention against organised crime is the first-ever global instrument established to combat transnational organised crime and the illicit trade in firearms. it is also supplemented by three protocols laying down specific measures to combat specific crimes. they relate in particular to trafficking in human beings, smuggling of migrants and the production and illicit trafficking of firearms. in this context, the european union has adjusted its legislation on record-keeping, firearms marking, firearms disposal, export, import and transit licence or authorisation requirements, enhanced controls at export points and brokering activities. given that the existing instruments have already been reformed and new legislative measures have been adopted, the european union can now ratify the protocol against the illicit manufacturing of and trafficking in firearms, their parts and components and ammunition.
in writing − the accession of bulgaria and romania has led to the enlargement of the eu customs union. in this context, the union was obliged to enter into negotiations with wto members in order to reach an agreement on a countervailing duty to balance the increase in the level of the duties imposed and the resulting significant losses. the eu has so far concluded such compensation agreements with brazil, cuba, new zealand, australia, argentina and the usa. the agreement with the people's republic of china aimed at restoring its original trade rights concerns in particular mushrooms, garlic, chocolate and confectionery.

in writing − the scope of the european globalisation adjustment fund was extended to include support for workers made redundant as a direct result of the global financial and economic crisis for applications submitted from 1 may 2009 to 30 december 2011. in the case of denmark, this is the eighth application and concerns the mobilisation of a total amount of eur 6 364 643 from the egf. it concerns the dismissal of 611 workers from a vestas group company. the request was sent to the commission on 21 december 2012 and supplemented by additional information by 16 july 2013. on the basis of the facts available, the commission has concluded that the application qualifies for a grant from the fund.

written − roma women have a particularly difficult position. not only do they face racist attacks on a daily basis because of their membership of the roma minority, but they are also victims of gender discrimination on a daily basis. the reality in europe is that roma women have limited access to education, employment, decision-making, and basic health and social services. on this basis, roma women are at much higher risk of poverty than roma men. moreover, the situation is aggravated by the continuing economic and social crisis. roma women are an extremely vulnerable group of the european population and need our help to integrate properly into society.
in writing. − roma communities are currently in a vicious circle of poverty and social exclusion. according to statistics, more than 90% of roma live in extreme poverty. despite numerous efforts by the european institutions and national governments over the last decade to change their predicament, the living conditions of this community are more than drastic. the situation of roma women is even worse, because a society dominated by patriarchal and sexist traditions does not allow women to freely decide on the fundamental issues of their lives. our task is not to criticize the lifestyle of the roma community, but to propose possible solutions to the unsustainable situation of roma women. one of the options proposed by ms járóka is to allocate sufficient funds to member states' national roma integration strategies and to develop national action plans to address specific roma women's problems. but our ambitions must be directed primarily at ensuring the equal status of roma women in society. every woman has the right to access health care, education and employment. let's put an end to violence against women and prostitution, which is unfortunately still a reality in roma communities. i believe that also by supporting special programmes targeting roma youth, we can ensure that every girl goes to school and receives an adequate education, which is a prerequisite for a successful start in her personal and professional life.

in writing − voluntary work is any form of unpaid work carried out by an individual on the basis of his or her own free will. it is a manifestation of solidarity, social cohesion and mutual assistance and has a direct impact on society. moreover, engaging in volunteering activities can bring significant learning and has a positive impact on the acquisition of skills in the labour market. this work is increasingly being disseminated among young and older people, which has a positive impact on intergenerational dialogue, active ageing and the involvement of citizens in society at all stages of life. it is thus an active way of developing civil society, which also contributes to the development of intercultural dialogue and thus effectively combats prejudice and racism. therefore, it is very important to try to create favourable conditions for volunteering.
in writing. − volunteering is an important aspect of active civic engagement and democracy, as well as personal development. this is manifested in any form of unpaid work where the work is done by the person's free will. volunteering promotes solidarity between generations and contributes to active ageing and lifelong civic engagement, thereby facilitating social inclusion. i agree that the commission should establish a single point of contact in the form of a service responsible for the policy on volunteering and for the coordination between the commission departments and the various institutions in this field. the commission should continue to liaise with the successor of the european year of volunteering 2011 alliance, the european voluntary federation and other voluntary organisations, and should also take due account of the recommendations of the european voluntary service policy agenda as a basis for the action plan for the future. it should be made easier for ngos active in voluntary work to receive european support, in particular under the esf, at national and european level. it would also be useful for volunteering time to be recognised by the beneficiary as co-financing in kind for all european grants. that is why i voted in favour of this proposal.
in writing − volunteering helps in many areas where positive change is only brought about by the persistent efforts of ordinary people doing extraordinary things. i believe that volunteering and its contribution to society must be properly promoted and that good deeds must also be socially rewarded. member states and the union should therefore create a favourable legislative and social environment for the development of this altruistic area. large reserves are emerging in the area of corporate volunteering, which should be cultivated more, including in the form of public incentives to act for a good cause. however, young people should also be trained to engage in volunteering from an early age, even though volunteering is for all ages and social groups. in addition to feeling good, many gain many useful skills, experiences and contacts that can later be useful in finding employment.
in writing − despite the positive impact of the european year of volunteering 2011 on the world of volunteering, there are still clear problems with volunteering in europe. i believe that volunteering is an important aspect of active citizenship and democracy, but its added value for society and for economic and social cohesion is still underestimated. it is therefore important that the skills acquired during volunteering are generally recognised by employers in the labour market. if we want to combat these problems, we should support and promote initiatives that promote volunteer activities. but what still strikes me is that in many advanced democracies, there is still a societal undervaluation of volunteering. in several member states, voluntary activities are still held in low esteem despite their contribution to society. in practice, however, we are still struggling with the fact that the public does not know what to think of volunteering and volunteering. therefore, despite the positive impact of the erd 2011, i believe that there is still a lack of concrete measures to develop volunteering on a european scale. i see volunteering as a pro-social behaviour, and promoting and supporting it has a number of positive effects. our role is to support and improve the legislative conditions for volunteering activities, raise awareness of volunteering and promote cross-border cooperation between public and non-governmental organisations.

rapporteur. − madam president, since 2011 we have been discussing the new approach to our neighbourhood policy. today we have a chance to discuss one more element of this approach: the new neighbourhood instrument which will from 2014 provide increased support to 16 partner countries to the east and south of the eu borders. through this instrument the eu can rise to the current challenges and become the real force in supporting reforms in our neighbourhood. support for reforms related to deep and sustainable democracy and creating closer links with the societies of partner countries are crucial for developing our partnership, and now they have become elements or central parts of the instrument. the partnership with our neighbours should be mutually beneficial. we need to focus on support for good governance, the rule of law and fundamental freedoms. supporting integration into the union internal market, economic development and job creation in partner countries benefits the eu as well. similarly, managed movement of people could bring about positive effects for the entire neighbourhood, thus facilitating the mobility of students, workers and tourists. active engagement between the eu and its neighbours in areas such as education, environment and research and innovation can also do much to support our shared objectives. we have prepared quite comprehensive texts of the regulation. the framework of the new instrument lies in a more tailor-made differentiated and intensive-based approach to the partner countries, which means that our partnership must be based on mutual accountability and shared commitment to the universal values of human rights, democracy and the rule of law. our relations with each neighbourhood country will be more differentiated. each country should have a chance to develop its relations with the eu at its own pace. we need to take into consideration the aspirations, capacities and ambitions of particular countries but also their efforts in implementing the agreed reforms. we can offer more support to the countries which have decided to progress in the reforms. thus increased support from the union will be available to the countries in line with the principle of ‘more for more’. the basic condition for such support will be progress in building and consolidating democracy. clearly the more a country progresses in this field, the more support will be available from the eu. the european parliament has always played a constructive role in the eu neighbourhood policy: encouraging progress in democratisation processes and actively supporting the values of human rights and the ambitions of people to live in free and peaceful societies. therefore i am glad that our voice will be also heard in building the policy framework of this regulation. in conclusion, i would like to thank my colleague shadow rapporteurs for their support during the preparation and negotiation of this regulation. the negotiations were tough; but all is well that ends well. i would like to commend highly the positive and constructive approach which was shown by the representatives of the commission and also thank the council representatives for their business-like approach.
rapporteur. − madam president, first of all i would like to thank all the colleagues who have contributed to this discussion. i shall make only two short remarks. the discussion showed again that we are even more aware these days that our neighbourhoods south and east are subject to a fast changing reality. while the wave of revolutions in the arab world exposed the weakness in some of the paradigms in our neighbourhood policy, the current situation on our eastern borders shows once again the necessity of following a clear policy line supporting values of democracy and human rights, and being consistent on that. my other remark. i did not mention it properly in my introductory statements so i want to draw attention to it again: this concerns civil society. we have seen that civil society plays a crucial role in promoting democracy, reforms and in holding governments responsible. this instrument, the european neighbourhood instrument, will support precisely this role of civil society. moreover, when governments are targeted by eu sanctions or other policy measures, we make sure that the eu upholds and strengthens further its support to civil society through this very instrument.
madam president, in today’s discussion, a week before the european council, i would like to support the upholding of the european commission’s recommendation to grant candidate country status to albania without undue delay. albania is on the european track and has only been there for a short time. the general political climate is improving thanks to the work of all major political players and i think it gives good prospects for the future. yes, it needs to be stressed that the progress achieved so far needs further consolidation and implementation. this is the time when the adoption of the remaining reforms should be intensified. once again, i would like to give my support to the resolution and congratulate the rapporteur. i hope that my message will also be shared by the council later this month.
rapporteur. − madam president, let me welcome the representative of the council and also especially the euʼs special representative for human rights, mr stavros lambrinidis. i am glad that our discussion is taking place today on 10 december in remembrance of the international day of human rights. this year we also mark the 20th anniversary of the 1993 world conference on human rights in vienna, which led to confirmation of the universality of all human rights. today’s report highlights the interconnection between the universality of human rights and democracy-building. let me outline the three major themes to which i paid considerable attention in this report: the eu policy framework on human rights, the issues of human rights in transition processes, and the euʼs support for human rights worldwide. the eu policy framework on human rights needs to become the backbone of our actions in this field. a year ago the eu adopted its strategic framework and action plan on human rights and democracy, and appointed our first special representative for human rights. this was a right step forward by which we have opened doors for mainstreaming human rights policies in the euʼs external relations. on this occasion i would like to welcome the active approach of the new special representative who has taken over the responsibilities of coordinating and promoting the euʼs human rights policies. i would encourage him to continue in these activities and keep in close contact with this parliament, which has been the case so far. building a rights-respecting democracy in which human rights are adequately protected is not an easy task. the processes of transitions are often exhausting and lengthy; the ideals are confronted with uncertainties and unleashed power can strike the most vulnerable parts of the population. as someone who has experienced such processes and saw its risks, i dedicated a part of the report to these problems. the eu has the potential and the responsibility to support these processes. we need to pay more attention to the problems and challenges of the countries overthrowing authoritarian regimes, countries where democracy processes are still fragile; but also to those countries trapped in transition for a long time where the processes stopped without any clear prospects of further changes. justice, rule of law, building of democratic institutions, reconciliation and addressing the human rights abuses: these are only a few of the problems on the road. even in the countries aspiring to membership of the european union questions on the rights of minorities, civil liberties and fundamental freedoms remain open; specific challenges for the protection of human rights post-transition in post-conflict contexts. the report deals therefore with questions of transitional justice, accountability for past abuses and fighting impunity, which needs to remain an integral part of the process. in conclusion, the eu needs to remain determined in promoting and protecting the universality of human rights, be it through our own instruments, though the un human rights system or through support to other international organisations such as the international criminal court. i would like to thank all the colleagues, the shadow rapporteurs and others who participated in preparing this report. their contribution was very important for me and i appreciate it.
rapporteur. − mr president, this has been a very good debate and i will only make a couple of remarks. i will start with mr lambrinidis. an overwhelming majority of the speakers addressed you or mentioned your name, and i am sure that i am expressing the wish and desire of all of us present in this room when i say that you should be given the floor to address us. but, as minister leškevičius said, the existing rules do not allow this. i heard this from a very good source. rules are rules, but if the rules are not contributing positively, i think it is worth thinking about changing them. but i am glad that you were present here. your aura and the positive energy which you radiate nevertheless made a contribution to our debate. in a way it is unfair to you, stavros. you have been sitting here all the time listening very attentively to what we all have to say, you cannot say anything yourself, and afterwards you will have to deliver what we have discussed and what we have agreed upon here. i think this is unfair, and next time i am sure it would be only fair to give you the floor and a full opportunity to participate in our discussion. concerning the contributions made by members, i would like to thank those who expressed their support for the report. i really do appreciate that. for those who criticised it and said that the report is unbalanced or not objective, what can i say? in this world we do not live in a vacuum but in a political reality. given the complex character of the issue of human rights, i do not know whether the most capable magician could reconcile all the political positions or standpoints which we all have. i did not expect my report to satisfy everybody, because that is simply not possible. i have tried to do as well as possible, even when accepting or rejecting the amendments, even those from gue/ngl members, i have taken several additions from them because i really think that to have the majority of this house behind this report is very important. another thing i would like to mention is that next year the new action plan will be adopted and will start functioning from 2015. parliament should use this opportunity because it will be consulted. we should take it as a new opportunity to strengthen our role in the whole human rights agenda. i would like to remain friends with vice-president protasiewicz so i will finish my intervention now.
on behalf of the ppe group. the european globalisation adjustment fund can clearly provide effective support, particularly in the event of mass redundancies. if we are honest with ourselves, we have had cases where we have financed retraining for the benefit of new investors from third countries, but also cases where 70% of the aid was paid as unemployment benefit - obviously not to the member state - so that the european added value was often not really reflected. it is also a known fact that some member states have never applied for aid from this fund, even though they fulfilled the conditions for being eligible, because access is too complicated, too bureaucratic. we hope that, taking lessons from experience, the regulation will make the fund more efficient. it is pleasing to note that the grant payments may not exceed 35% of the total cost of the personalised service package. unfortunately, no better compromise was reached on the co-financing rate. the council insisted on a uniform 60% rate, and parliament's proposal would have taken greater account of the specific situation of the region and adjusted the co-financing rate accordingly. a new element of the regulation is to address youth unemployment through the use of the fund's resources. it is hoped that it will be an effective tool in the fight against youth unemployment. finally, i would like to thank marian harkin for her very excellent and effective cooperation.
the fight against tax evasion and fraud is not only a matter of state revenue but also a matter of justice. in these difficult times, decent, honest taxpayers must bear the cost of the losses caused by speculators who parasitize and profit from loopholes in the tax code. in the european union, we lose about one billion euros a year in this way. so it is our duty to do everything in our power to eliminate this robbing of decent people. the extension of the structure of information to be exchanged automatically between member states from 2015 onwards to include additional categories of income and assets, namely dividends, capital gains, other financial income and account balances, which are not yet defined, is, in the european commission's view, intended to help reduce the space used for the untaxed transfer of profits. that is why the member states also support the proposed extension of such automatic exchange of information between the tax authorities of the member states of the union and, ladies and gentlemen, they expect the same attitude from us.
the main topics of the forthcoming summit include economic and monetary union and economic and monetary policy. it is essential to continuously deepen the economic and monetary union, which requires not only more intensive and sustainable economic growth but also, and above all, employment and social cohesion. our top priority must therefore be to promote employment and social security. ladies and gentlemen, we need systemic measures and not just short-term solutions. these ultimately only have a negative impact on the employment of people already hard hit by the crisis. we must therefore invest in a targeted way and strengthen the financing of the economy, adopt pro-growth measures and strengthen social investment; we must also establish an effective social security system. the growing social unrest resulting from ineffective and ineffective measures must be prevented. eu citizens deserve a high level of social protection... rapporteur. − madam president, the amendment i am presenting reads as follows: ‘recalls its resolutions of 25 november 2010 on the situation in western sahara, of 22 october 2013 on the situation of human rights in the sahel region, and calls for a guarantee of human rights for the saharawi people and stresses the need to address these rights in western sahara and in the tindouf camps, including freedom of association, freedom of expression and the right to demonstrate, to be respected; demands the release of all sahrawi political prisoners; demands the opening of the territory to independent observers, ngos and the media; supports a fair and mutually acceptable political solution on western sahara, in accordance with the relevant united nations resolutions, including those allowing self-determination;’. that is the amendment, and i would ask for the house’s kind support.
in writing, the counterfeiting of the euro has both economic and social consequences. this is a serious crime. moreover, there is a clear link between this practice and organised crime. counterfeiting of the euro is harmful to the european economy and threatens the stability of the currency, thus endangering the financial interests of the european union. the european union must therefore combat this negative phenomenon. the pericles 2020 exchange, assistance and training programme for the protection of the euro against counterfeiting is an excellent helper in this regard, including in the dissemination of best practices. but we must ensure that the money spent is actually used effectively.
in writing − if we are to implement our policies responsibly at european level, we need high-quality and reliable statistical information on the situation in the union and its components. high-quality empirical data and statistics are essential to measure progress and in the process of evaluating the effectiveness of our policies and programmes, in particular in achieving the objectives set out in the europe 2020 strategy. the european statistical programme provides the legislative framework for the development, production and dissemination of european statistics for the period 2013 to 2017. the report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending regulation (eu) no 99/2013 on the european statistical programme 2013 to 2017 therefore needs to be given due consideration.
in writing eurostat data show that there are 2.6 million domestic workers in the european union, of which 89% are women and half are migrants. domestic work is a kind of invisible form of work, and the union's citizens who do it are the least protected. this type of work is very often exploited by workers who often work without a contract, without overtime pay, without entitlement to holidays or paid public holidays. moreover, this form of work leads to a certain isolation and people who do it are not sufficiently informed about their rights. in the present high unemployment rate, this phenomenon is all the more dangerous because people are forced to accept even obvious disadvantages in order to survive. increased protection of domestic workers is therefore necessary.
in writing − given that 2.6 million people are currently working in the eu and that domestic work is one of the least protected and invisible forms of work, i supported the motion for a resolution calling on member states to ratify the international labour organisation convention on decent work for domestic workers. household work must be subject to normal working hours, overtime pay, daily and weekly rest periods, paid annual leave and, above all, social and health insurance. domestic workers must have a healthy and safe working environment. in many countries, domestic workers are employed without contractual conditions, and children are exploited to work in the home. it is therefore essential that the member states ratify the ilo convention as soon as possible.
in writing - mr president, i am very pleased that the council and parliament have reached agreement on decent working conditions for domestic workers. this is a significant step towards valuing the unpaid work of women and mothers in caring for the home, children and family members. the next step should be to eliminate discrimination against these women. under the convention, a domestic worker is entitled to 24 hours of uninterrupted rest and a remuneration of at least the minimum wage. this is more than the minimum maternity or parental allowance in slovakia, for example. but the work is comparable, only the rest is less. i therefore call on the council and the commission to eliminate this inequality and thus end discrimination against mothers and families caring for young children. thank you. thank you.
written − the neighbourhood policy is one of the most important union policies. maintaining and deepening good relations between the european union and third countries is of paramount importance. armenia has been an active participant in the european union's neighbourhood policy since 2004. the union's partnership and cooperation agreement with armenia has been in force since 1999. the republic of armenia expressed its request to participate in the union's programmes as well as in its agencies in april 2012. it is a good opportunity to strengthen mutual contacts, whether cultural, educational, technical, scientific or environmental. moreover, it can contribute to improving people-to-people contacts, political relations and sectoral cooperation.
in writing − the territorial community of saint barthélemy has ceased to be an outermost region of the union by virtue of european council decision 2010/718/eu and has acquired the status of an overseas country and territory as from 1 january 2012. the european council decision in question provides that the french republic has undertaken to conclude the agreements necessary to safeguard the union's interests in this change. in order to speed up the procedure, the council authorised the european commission by decision to agree the terms of these agreements. this authorisation therefore concerns an agreement between the french republic, representing the community of saint barthélemy, of the one part, and the european union, of the other part, providing for the application of union legislation on the taxation of savings and administrative cooperation in the field of taxation in this territory.
in writing − spain has requested the re-introduction of the tax exemptions or tax restrictions to be applied to the list of products produced locally in the canary islands. these derogations were granted to it by council decision 2002/546/ec of 20 june 2002. in 2010, spain requested an extension of the period of application of the decision by two years in order to bring its expiry date into line with the expiry date of the guidelines on national regional aid for the years 2007 to 2013. council decision 895/2011 therefore extended the period of application of decision 2002/546/ec until 31 december 2013. spain has now requested a second renewal of these measures. as the new regional aid guidelines for the period 2014 to 2020 will enter into force on 1 july 2014, the commission considers it justified to extend the application of decision 2002/546/ec ec as amended by decision 895/2011/eu by six months in order to ensure that the expiry date coincides with the date of entry into force of the guidelines.
in writing − the european union's development aid should be more coordinated. if we focused our aid on fewer countries and fewer activities, we could reduce transaction costs and save up to 800 million euros a year. better coordination of country allocations would ensure annual savings of up to €8.4 billion. existing mechanisms should therefore be thoroughly reviewed and efforts made to improve coordination across the union. this will help us achieve better results and better cost-effectiveness in development aid. however, an effective coordination mechanism is necessary to achieve these objectives.
