in writing − if you have it is desirable that the european union adopt a comprehensive set of instruments covering the full range of policies relating to external action. these are in particular the development cooperation financing instrument, the european instrument for democracy and human rights, the european neighbourhood instrument, the stability instrument, the nuclear security cooperation instrument, the pre-accession assistance instrument and the partnership instrument. these instruments generally ensure that the actions to be financed under them are subject to multiannual indicative programming. the financial interests of the european union should be protected through appropriate measures throughout the expenditure cycle. in this context, it also appears justified to adopt additional measures to protect the financial interests of the union.
in writing − if you have crises and conflicts affect countries all over the world and threaten global security and stability. they are often linked to state instability and are exacerbated by poor governance and poverty. natural disasters, man-made disasters, drug trafficking, organised crime, terrorism, cybersecurity challenges and threats and related disruptions increase uncertainty, impede development, weaken the rule of law and contribute to instability. in this context, a comprehensive eu response to international crises, strengthening the eu's preparedness for crisis management, preventive action and interventions, is of particular importance. it is precisely the measures adopted under this regulation that can effectively complement and pursue the objectives pursued in the field of the common foreign and security policy.
in writing − the strategic review of the european neighbourhood policy (enp) analyses and assesses the changes in the eu's relations with its neighbours and developments since the establishment of the enp. while the european neighbourhood and partnership instrument is generally considered to be a successful instrument accompanying the eu's policy towards its neighbours, the enp political review and other assessments, lessons learned and public consultations have revealed a number of problems that will need to be addressed in the future by adapting the instrument to make the union's response even more effective. the union shall, through dialogue and cooperation with third countries, seek to promote, develop and consolidate the values of freedom, democracy, respect for human rights and fundamental freedoms, the principles of equality and the rule of law on which it is founded. since its inception, the esp has significantly strengthened relations with partner countries and has been a major asset for the union and its partners.
in writing − if you have over the past 50 years, through both integration and enlargement, the eu has grown from its original six members to its current 28. enlargements have arguably contributed to the greater prosperity of eu citizens and made europe stronger in the global economy. the institutional and legal frameworks and common eu policies have played a very important role in ensuring success. however, candidate countries are often unable to cope with all the efforts and costs required to meet the eu accession criteria on their own. technical and financial assistance is thus currently provided through the instrument for pre-accession assistance (ipa). however, it expires at the end of 2013. the new instrument for pre-accession assistance should continue to focus on delivering on the enlargement policy, one of the eu's main external action priorities, and thus effectively help to promote stability, security and prosperity in europe.
in writing − if you have over the past decade, the european union has considerably strengthened its bilateral relations with a number of industrialised and other high-income countries and territories in various regions of the world, notably north america, east asia and australasia, but also south-east asia and the gulf region. at the same time, the union has deepened its cooperation and partnership with developing and transforming countries in asia, central asia, latin america and with iraq, iran, yemen and south africa. it is in its interest to strengthen relations with partners playing an increasingly important role in international economy and trade, in international fora, including the group of 20 finance ministers and central bank governors (g20), in global governance and in addressing issues of global concern. building comprehensive partnerships on the international stage to promote a stable and inclusive international order, to look after shared global public goods, to defend the union's fundamental interests and to increase knowledge of the union in these countries is one of the eu's many priorities.
written − the european union is founded on the values of respect for human dignity, freedom, democracy, equality, the rule of law and respect for human rights. promoting democracy and human rights in this context is an essential aspect of the eu's external action. to this end, the union is using a wide range of measures around the world, from political dialogue and diplomatic initiatives to financial and technical cooperation and assistance. it is the regulation on the european instrument for democracy and human rights that provides support to civil society and human rights institutions worldwide. in order to address the wide range of issues in the field in an effective, transparent and flexible manner, specific financial resources and a specific financing instrument that can continue to operate independently are still needed.
in writing. − the union remains committed to helping developing countries. to achieve this objective, a regulation on a development cooperation instrument for the period 2007-2013 was established, the main and general objective of which is, in particular, to work towards poverty eradication. this regulation constitutes one of the instruments for providing direct assistance to the external policies of the european union and replaces the regulation establishing a financing instrument for development cooperation, which expires on the abovementioned date of 31 december 2013.
in writing. − the commission has recently repeatedly stressed the need to tackle effectively a number of problems which pose a serious threat to social cohesion and competitiveness. in this context, i consider it of particular importance to pay particular attention in the multiannual financial framework (mff) for the period 2014-2020 to one-off support for workers made redundant as a result of major structural changes brought about by the increasing globalisation of production and trade patterns. such specific support should be as hitherto - provided through the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf), an instrument the use of which does not affect mff expenditure.
in writing, the commission has recently brought tax fraud and tax evasion to the forefront of attention, not only in the union but also in the world. for this reason, it is also of the utmost importance to take steps to increase the efficiency and effectiveness of tax collection. in this context, the automatic exchange of information is an important tool. at the same time, in order to combat tax fraud and aggressive tax planning effectively, it is appropriate to make efforts to extend the mandatory automatic exchange of information in the field of taxation from the european union to the global level.
in writing − if you have at european level, carriers of radioactive materials are subject to transport legislation originating in the treaty on the functioning of the european union (tfeu) as well as legislation deriving from the treaty establishing the european atomic energy community (euratom). given that transport is the only 'mobile' activity, and given its often crossborder nature, it can quite easily happen that a carrier has to follow procedures in several member states, which has complicated transport operations, especially with the differences in the systems of those states. in order to make the situation more transparent, the proposed regulation also introduces a european system for the registration of hauliers and, by doing so, replaces reporting systems with a single registration.
in writing − justice, the rule of law, accountability, the fight against impunity and fair and independent judicial proceedings are among the essential elements of the protection of human rights. in june 2012, the eu council adopted a strategic framework and action plan for human rights and democracy, committing the eu institutions to a number of policy objectives. also, in july 2012, the eu council appointed the first eu thematic special representative for human rights. following up on this, the eu's 2012 report on human rights and democracy in the world provides information on the eu's efforts to promote the integration of human rights, gender equality, democracy and good governance in development policies and instruments.
in writing − i welcome the report on human rights in the world in 2012. the european union's strategic relations with third countries must be based on respect for fundamental values, which primarily include human rights and the principles of democracy and the rule of law. i consider it unacceptable to apply double standards in foreign policy, which undermines not only human rights themselves but also the dignity of the european union as a whole. we need to apply a certain minimum standard in all international agreements with third countries, including trade agreements. but we will achieve real compliance with the systematic monitoring of human rights proposed several times and their evaluation with a view to drawing conclusions. in conclusion, i would once again call on all eu institutions to apply a clear, unified approach to respect for human rights in both internal and external policies.
in writing − competition policy aims to ensure the smooth functioning of the internal market and a level playing field, to protect consumers from anti-competitive practices and to guarantee the best prices. it is not about micromanaging, but about enforcing clear and fair rules within which market forces can operate effectively. however, even two decades after the creation of the single market, many consumers are still seriously affected by anti-competitive practices in different economic sectors. in many cases, the private and public sectors did not provide fully independent regulatory authorities capable of ensuring that markets continue to function properly in a fair and non-discriminatory manner. the identical situation applies to competition authorities.
written − competition policy contributes to the efficient functioning of the internal market and the protection of consumers living in the eu. the enforcement of clear and fair rules in the internal market clearly leads to a better use of available resources, the development of innovation, economic growth, lower prices for goods and services, but also to job creation. nevertheless, competition policy is often perceived negatively in terms of the imposition of high fines, which can lead to insolvency and subsequent job losses or bankruptcy for some firms. however, this is highly undesirable and should not be the consequence of the application of competition policy in times of economic crisis. on the contrary, the european commission and other antitrust authorities should focus more on promoting a healthy competition culture, as adequate awareness is still lacking in many companies.
in writing − if you have the year 2015 will see major changes in the dairy sector. from that period, the milk quotas will no longer apply. in order to secure the future of this sector, i consider it extremely important to promote rules that strengthen the bargaining power of producers. at the same time, it is well-founded to examine in detail the impact of the abolition of quotas and the impact of this act, in particular on remote regions and disadvantaged areas.
written − the european parliament's own-initiative report on milk production in mountain and less-favoured areas is timely given that the milk sector will undergo huge changes after the end of the quota system in 2015. the milk and milk products market will have to respond to market forces, which is likely to have a negative impact in particular on smaller producers in mountain areas. these are small and medium-sized family businesses whose owners are often essentially dependent on this source of income and livelihood. moreover, it is desirable to maintain the traditional milk production, which has many advantages, including the high quality of the products. as milk production is a major source of local or regional development in many regions, i consider it urgent to examine the impact of the expected measures on the regions concerned and to develop a strategy for a smooth transition of producers in these most vulnerable regions to the new system. for these reasons, i vote in favour of the report.
in writing last october, the commission published a communication aimed at guiding the union's approach to building resilience and reducing vulnerability in developing countries. the report focuses in particular on the poorest groups of the population where there is a high risk of exposure to danger. at the same time, it also focuses on countries often beset by crises. most damage from disasters and crises occurs mainly in the poorest and most unstable countries. in order to avoid such situations, where possible, it is important to focus on the root causes of risks and to seek to reduce risk factors.
written − women with disabilities are at the crossroads of various forms of discrimination, whether based on gender or disability. they face complications of unemployment, lack of access to education, or problems with marriage or motherhood. women with disabilities are likely to be more vulnerable when it comes to victims of violence, including domestic and sexual exploitation and abuse. in this context, i consider it important to pursue specific objectives in order to improve the quality of life of women with disabilities.
in writing − i am very pleased that it was the european parliament itself which initiated the report on women with disabilities, as this issue deserves special attention from legislators at european and national level. today, some 80 million people with disabilities live in the eu, more than half of them women and girls. i consider it unacceptable that in our modern society there should be barriers and stereotypes that prevent these people from fully enjoying their basic human rights and their human potential. in our policies, we as legislators must put emphasis on creating favourable conditions for the participation of people with disabilities in economic and social life. women, who unfortunately often suffer double discrimination in practice, continue to require special attention. i therefore call on the competent authorities of the member states to make active use of european funds in the new 2014-2020 programming period to promote the inclusion of people with disabilities, and in particular women, in active life.
in writing − the retail and wholesale sector is among the key sectors that can act as a driver in the transition to a more sustainable economy and consumption patterns. efficiency in this sector has an impact on competition, innovation, price trends and competitiveness. retailers are the ones who make a significant contribution to enabling consumers in the union to benefit from the benefits of the single market. however, obstacles to the creation of an efficient and competitive single retail market remain. micro-enterprises and smes make a significant contribution to the eu's added value and for this reason measures are needed to boost their productivity even further in order to achieve even more economic growth and jobs within the union.
i believe that the management of emu clearly lacks sufficient democratic legitimacy, as in many areas the institutional framework is literally circumvented. the founding treaties since the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon have created considerable scope for strengthening democratic decision-making. however, these possibilities are seldom used and so there is no parliamentary control at all in many key economic and monetary areas. we must urgently correct this democratic deficit if we are not to contribute to the sharp rise in often justified euroscepticism across europe. the proper functioning of economic and monetary policy must provide legal certainty for all actors and take account of the social consequences of economic measures. i consider that fragmentation and the conclusion of intergovernmental agreements are highly undesirable at this stage of integration.
the complex and dynamic economic developments in europe, but also in the world, have required the european council to be more closely involved in shaping the european union's policy actions. although article 15 (1) of the treaty on european union defines the european council as merely the institution which gives the union the necessary impetus for development and sets the general direction and priorities, its actual involvement in determining the essential political and economic measures has become far more pronounced. it is therefore necessary to adapt the way in which the european council and the european parliament communicate in an appropriate form so that the activities of these institutions complement and enrich each other and avoid unnecessary misunderstandings or delays. the best solution today seems to be to conclude an interinstitutional agreement that would define and regulate more precisely the relations and the methods of cooperation between the two institutions. intense social and political developments not only in the union but also in the immediate vicinity require us to be able to respond to these diverse impulses in a prompt, correct and coordinated manner. well-formulated rules of cooperation can only help us to do so.
mr president, i might differ from some of my colleagues, but i believe the european commission has not undermined the european parliament by introducing this delegated act. by forcing a vote on a resolution that only complicates the act, my colleagues are slowing the process of introducing new trade preferences to around 2% of our imports. the committee members who are against the act are not in favour of all countries on the beneficial list being in a single piece of legislation, and they believe that the commission is not legally allowed to include all the countries in the single act. the commission is legally allowed to do so. the committee does not need to make a show of strength against legislation the commission is legally allowed to introduce. both the council and the commission are in favour of the delegated act, as it is a good piece of legislation. i see no reason to amend the act. any effort to amend the act only complicates a process that already has strong support. for us to go back and vote on separate delegated acts for each country on the list would hurt the political process. we in the european people’s party – at least most of us – are satisfied with the single delegated act and believe that the commission is respecting its mandate. blue-card answer. – well, you are the professor; you are the expert. i understand that you can see all of these nuances, but i have to tell you that in this case i agree with david martin because, if we jump and pick up on every little thing, we might never accomplish anything and there is too much at stake, too many benefits – not only for us but for some other countries, including improving their democracies. so certain things we might have to let go.
i would like to commend your initiative on green policy, particularly infrastructure, because industrial agglomerations are often supplemented by housing for workers, for people who work in these agglomerations, and these agglomerations are concrete jungles without any quality environment, and only with the funds of the european union will it be possible to revive and cultivate these housing areas so that they are able to provide children, but also families, with a quality environment. such a policy for the people of the european union, for those who work and who build this union, is very important, because so far we have only talked about industrial policy, about the policy of the various financial institutions, but we have said little about the problems of the people who live in this environment.
mr president of the european central bank, in your speech you stressed that in the fragmented environment of the euro area, where we use the single currency, it is difficult to define monetary policy in a way that is both suitable for the industrialized countries of northern europe and at the same time for a debt-laden country struggling with economic decline. your efforts to reorganize the national banks of the enlarged countries by exchanging european central bank funds for worthless securities are devaluing the ecb's portfolio and raising the legitimate question of how long such a practice will be sustainable without a systemic collapse. therefore, mr president, i think it would be good to focus progressively on supporting active entrepreneurs who produce real value and to focus less on the restructuring of the ever-growing debts in the budgets of some countries.
for the efd group the estimated €1 billion lost annually to the eu in tax evasion and fraud is a large enough sum to give serious consideration to measures to eliminate these losses. one of the first steps we should take is to simplify and make the union's tax system transparent so that the flow of money within and between member states, as well as in cooperation with third countries, is transparent and controllable at every stage. tax administrations must have effective technical means and effective legislative mechanisms to obtain the necessary overview of ongoing transactions within their remit and to be able to react immediately to attempts to evade tax obligations. in may this year, the president of the european commission, mr barroso, announced the commission's commitments to fight tax evasion and fraud. it is therefore, i think, appropriate to add to this general commitment objective, measurable parameters so that our public knows what effect we can expect from the measures being prepared.
in writing ladies and gentlemen, tax fraud is unacceptable. but only through relentless coordination at national, european and global levels can they be stopped. none of them are enough. in slovakia, we have literally launched the fight against tax fraud and it must be said that the first efforts have already produced results, which significantly contribute to reducing the public finances deficit. the 'lottery' project, which actually allows any consumer to check the tax integrity of retailers and service providers, is proving to be very successful. this project would deserve european attention. furthermore, the eu must not relax at the global level, especially in the g20 agenda. to push hard for all the decisions taken to be implemented and to prepare further steps and proposals by the ec to prevent tax fraud, evasion and what we call aggressive tax planning globally. the commission's mandate is essential here, because even the strongest nation states have no chance at the global level: the complicated 'coercion' of swiss banks to open up and the resistance of the swiss parliament are examples. yes, the fight is still ahead of us. but for the recovery of the world economy and for the deepening of justice, it is a necessity. thank you. thank you.
in writing − the number of pending cases before the general court, as one of the courts of the court of justice of the european union, is on a steady upward trend. the increasing workload and the growing agenda are no longer sustainable. this situation results in a denial of the right to a fair trial and thus a denial of article 6 of the european convention for the protection of human rights. it is therefore clear that the number of judges needs to be increased urgently, but the question of the selection criteria themselves is controversial. the rule of one judge per member state currently applies, making this a rather sensitive issue for all member states. in any event, the question of the professional and personal background of each candidate, which is not indisputably indicated by nationality, must be relevant.
in writing − if you have this is a legislative resolution of the european parliament on the proposal for a council directive amending directives 2006/112/ec and 2008/118/ec as regards the french outermost regions and in particular the island of mayotte. pursuant to decision 2012/419/eu of the european council amending the status of mayotte in relation to the european union, mayotte will have the status of an outermost region, pursuant to article 349 tfeu, instead of an overseas country and territory within the meaning of article 355 (2) tfeu, as from 1 january 2014. on the basis of that decision, mayotte is added to the list of outermost regions. the proposed directive thus aims to grant mayotte the same status as that long applied to other french outermost regions such as guadeloupe, french guiana, martinique and réunion, namely exclusion from the scope of the common system of value added tax, under secondary eu legislation.

in writing − if you have innovation is absolutely key in the green economy. in the context of the strategy for sustainable growth, from an environmental, economic and social point of view, which, together with the creation of sustainable jobs, is a prerequisite for social cohesion, eco-innovation is fundamental. the green economy in europe has an estimated annual turnover of €319 billion, representing 2.5% of eu gdp. the sector employs 3.4 million people. moreover, the global turnover in the green sector is expected to double to eur 3 100 billion by 2020. i think it would be a great shame not to use this huge potential. effective investment in this area will have environmental benefits as well as significant economic benefits.
written − following the adoption of regulation (eu) no 182/2011 on implementing acts following the amendments provided for in the treaty of lisbon, the european commission was asked to adapt the rules on decision-making procedures in the field of trade policy to the new regime of delegated and implementing acts. the commission therefore presented two proposals, omnibus i and omnibus ii, which are consolidated acts in the field of trade policy. they combine the trade-related underlying regulations into one instrument. this needs to be updated with the previous regulations. in this proposal, it therefore proposes the necessary amendments to the underlying texts, while also specifying the procedures to be applied. in particular, this concerns the choice between the advisory procedure and the examination procedure for implementing acts.
in writing − the rules on trade policy decision-making need to be adapted to the new regime of delegated and implementing acts, in the light of the changes introduced by the treaty of lisbon and regulation (eu) no 182/2011 on implementing acts adopted in the wake of those changes. in order to achieve harmonisation, the commission therefore submitted two proposals, omnibus i and omnibus ii. in both cases, the basic trade regulations that need to be updated are thus combined into one legal instrument. the proposal therefore brings the necessary changes and updates to the basic legislation.
in writing − if you have everyday life in today's society without a checking account is extremely complicated. without a payment account, it is almost impossible for a union citizen to receive a salary or pay water, gas or electricity bills. he is deprived of the benefits of cashless transactions and this makes it very difficult for him to participate in social and economic life. however, many union residents face enormous difficulties in opening a payment account. the commission's proposal is therefore timely and should be adopted as soon as possible. every citizen of the european union has the right to access the standard transactions of everyday life, regardless of his or her financial situation, place of residence within the union, credit history or employment status. equally important for me, in the interest of the european consumer being as well informed as possible, is the transparency and clarity of bank charges and the possibility of switching from one account to another.
in writing − if you have the importance of marine and coastal areas and the maritime economy is significant for the european union. these sectors employ almost 88 million europeans, representing 40% of the union's gdp. of these, 5.4 million are employed in the marine and maritime sector. the gross value added of this sector is almost 500 billion. moreover, 90% of the european union's external trade is transported by sea. the demand for maritime space is therefore clear and is likely to continue in the future. our maritime economy is also of particular importance in view of the objectives we have set ourselves in the europe 2020 strategy. but we are using the sea in an uncoordinated way, and that has a variety of negative consequences. to use this space effectively, we need a clear strategy, taking into account all the economic, social and environmental factors involved.
in writing following constitutional amendments to mayotte, france has requested the european council to take a decision to change its status to an outermost region within the meaning of article 349 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union, in view of its relationship with the european union. the european council granted the request and, by decision 2012/419/eu, the new status of mayotte as an outermost region of the european union will enter into force on 1 january 2014. this entails the full application of union legislation. however, the immediate full application of union legislation is not possible and therefore certain transitional provisions are laid down.
written − the european capitals of culture project has gained wide recognition since its inception in 1985 and has transformed itself from an intergovernmental initiative into a european action. this award is a benefit in many ways. it enhances the international prestige of european cities, has a positive impact on sustainable development and tourism, stimulates competitiveness within the creative sectors and creates incentives to promote investment in culture and the creation of long-term cultural initiatives.
in writing − if you have with effect from 1 january 2014, the european council amended the status of mayotte in relation to the european union. mayotte thus ceases to be an overseas territory and becomes an outermost region within the meaning of the relevant article of the treaty on the functioning of the european union. the review of the situation with regard to mayotte has shown the need to protect the sensitive biological situation of its waters. in certain respects, france needs additional time to comply with the union acquis in relation to mayotte. in this context, it also appears necessary to allow the modernisation of the mayotte fleet to allow fishing outside the lagoon, where resources are less fragile than in the lagoon. however, there is also a need to improve safety and working conditions.
written − regulation (eu) no 978/2012 lays down the modalities of the union's generalised system of preferences, which aims to improve access to the eu market for developing countries. this will be made possible by granting preferential treatment to their export products. the gsp is composed of a general measure and two specific measures, including a special incentive measure for sustainable development and good governance (sgf+), under which no duties are required from a beneficiary country for imports of more than 6 000 tariff lines. the gsp+ is intended to serve as a credible incentive for countries to commit to implementing the key international conventions considered crucial in the context of sustainable development.
i support efforts to integrate people living in extreme poverty and social exclusion. for the most part, they are not in a position to handle their situation on their own. roma problems are the problems of people who are on the margins of society and are trying to survive as they know how. they face discrimination from their fellow citizens, governmental authorities, and businesses. the creation of specific roma-focused strategies leads to a paradox, which is also reflected in the resolution. on the one hand, we want to monitor the observance of roma human and civil rights, on the other hand, we are afraid that the roma registry would deepen the prejudice against them. i therefore recommend that we instead seek to integrate strategies and policies to combat extreme poverty. it will also help us to get more support from the general public, especially taxpayers.
written − the european union stands for the values of respect for human dignity, freedom, democracy, equality, the rule of law and respect for human rights. it is well known that roma suffer discrimination within europe and that their socioeconomic and fundamental rights situation is often worse than that of the non-roma population. as far as poverty and social exclusion are concerned, they have reached a critical level in the roma population, limiting the life prospects of these families. in addition, negative attitudes of the non-roma population and open discrimination against the majority society contribute to the exclusion of roma. in this context, it is justified that the member states of the union take the necessary measures to ensure that roma are not discriminated against and that their human rights, as enshrined in the charter and the european convention on human rights, as well as in eu law, are respected and enforced.
in writing − all summit participants reaffirmed their commitment to the principles of international law and to fundamental values such as democracy, the rule of law and respect for human rights. ukraine is a country of strategic importance to the eu and an indispensable partner in the european neighbourhood policy and the eastern partnership. however, ukraine has recently abandoned its planned association agreement with the european union and is strengthening relations with russia. this situation has arisen despite the union's will to continue the association process. however, deepening the mutual relations should be in the interest of both parties concerned.
in writing − albania has demonstrated progress in achieving the 12 key priorities of the 2010 commission opinion and the reform process can be considered to be progressing satisfactorily so far. the necessary measures have been taken in the area of jurisdiction or public administration. at the same time, i am convinced that the remaining challenges must also be addressed in an effective manner in order to make further progress towards european union membership. the accession process itself has become a sort of driving force for the continuation of the reforms in albania, and in this respect the support of the albanian population is also particularly high.
in writing, the european union institutions and the member states have made efforts to restore financial credibility and stability. this was done in particular by adopting and implementing structural reforms and adopting a new framework for the management of economic affairs. i believe it is important that this effort be completed by the creation of a genuine banking union. better coordination of economic policies is necessary and justified in order to strengthen competitiveness, sustainability and job creation within the member states of the union. i think one of the basic premises of such a policy is to make an effort to apply eu legislation thoroughly.
voting on this report was not easy for me and i ended up abstaining in the final vote. on the one hand, i support the project of a genuine economic and monetary union, because only then can we eliminate the systemic deficiencies created by the introduction of the euro. but the financial transaction tax is an increase in the tax burden and at the same time the first step towards harmonising tax rates, which i reject. i am against weakening the position of small member states in the council and against the creation of more union agencies. and in particular, i reject the possibility of adopting a deficit union budget and introducing additional own budgetary resources. if member states have reasonable doubts about the proper use of their appropriations to the union budget, the solution must not be to increase other resources but to improve management.
in writing. − the crisis has exposed the forced integration associated with the euro, and this development has added a new dimension to the debate on multilateral governance in the union. in this context, however, it is necessary to take into account that the discussion on multilateral governance does not overlap with the issue of multi-level governance, which concerns the balance of powers and the involvement of national, regional and local authorities. it is important to monitor social and employment policies in particular with due intensity and to assess their economic and social impact in a manner comparable to the provisions on the surveillance of national economic policies, in particular so that the european union's recommendations can be properly directed.
decision-making in the eu is certainly not one of the easiest, quite the contrary. most citizens in the member states still do not understand how the european law-making process works. they often overlook the role and responsibility of their governments in this process. i consider this to be the main problem. at the same time, i am not opposed to learning from the specific confusions and failures that have occurred in recent times and have complicated legislative work. the purpose of the resolution adopted is to improve the practical functioning of relations between the european parliament, the european commission and the council of the european union. i think these issues need to be addressed, which is why i supported the report.
in writing, the treaty of lisbon gave the european council the status of a european institution without changing its role. under the pressure of the crisis, its role has grown considerably, the number of extraordinary meetings has increased and issues normally discussed at council level have been transferred to the european council. this went far beyond the framework of a key provision of the treaty, which states that the european council has no legislative functions. in this context, and in order to strengthen the democratic character of the decision-making process, i consider it particularly justified to adopt appropriate measures of parliamentary scrutiny.
in writing − green infrastructure is a strategically planned network of natural and semi-natural areas with other environmental characteristics, which are designed and managed to provide a wide range of ecosystem services. includes green spaces (possibly blue if aquatic ecosystems) and other physical features in terrestrial (including coastal) and marine areas. on the mainland, green infrastructure is found in rural and urban areas. green infrastructure can be said to help understand the value of the benefits that nature provides to human society and to mobilise investment to maintain and enhance them. it assumes that the protection and enhancement of nature and natural processes, and the myriad benefits provided by nature to human society, are purposefully integrated into spatial planning and territorial development.
in writing − if you have in an environment of declining economic activity and volatile financial conditions resulting from the financial and sovereign debt crises, 2012 was another challenging year for the conduct of monetary policy. real economic activity declined during the period, mainly due to weak investment and private consumption. the annual inflation rate remained elevated in 2012, despite adverse macroeconomic conditions, although it declined during the year. the level of inflation has been substantially affected by strong increases in energy prices and increases in indirect taxes and administered prices in several euro area member states. as for interest rates, they hit an all-time low of 0.5 percent in may of that year.
in writing − if you have according to available information, eur 1 trillion is lost annually in the european union as a result of tax evasion and avoidance, without any restrictive measures being taken to respond to this. the amount lost in europe through tax evasion today exceeds the total amount that member states spend on healthcare, and also represents more than four times the amount spent on education within the member states of the european union. i am convinced of the need to promote social justice while seeking to tighten the regulatory framework so that there is no active system bypassing and that europe does not suffer the consequences of large-scale tax evasion or financial losses.
for the efd group the situation in the central african republic, where various armed groups have been fighting each other for a year and where criminal gangs have been terrorising the local population, is unsustainable. the national authorities are unable to guarantee the safety of the civilian population, and the deployment of the common units of the community of central african states has not helped to bring order to the country. therefore, the only appropriate way to protect public order and the safety of the local population today appears to be to implement the un security council resolution and to rapidly reinforce the international mission in the central african republic under the auspices of the african union. however, i am convinced that at the same time the country's humanitarian aid capacity must be strengthened so that the necessary food supplies for the local population, which has been impoverished by the fighting, can be made available while order is restored.
for the efd group the official admission by the director of the chinese organ donation committee at the madrid conference that more than 90% of transplanted organs come from executed prisoners indirectly confirmed that prisoners of conscience in this country have become involuntary victims of human organ trafficking. these people are being killed just to get organs fit for transplant for clients coming into china and into their hospitals from all over the world. the chinese government's announcement that it will phase out this practice by 2015 is a cynical admission of the incredibly cruel treatment of some groups in the country. i confess it is incomprehensible to me that a nation with such rich culture and civilization should ever have embarked on such a decadent approach to the human organism. i'm sure if the top officials of this country reflect on the ethical aspects of this action, they'll immediately understand that they have to stop.
